# UNRESOLVED: 48h elapsed; active research duration not measured

Solution class to which this headline applies: class A' of Section 2.3, that is Setting A1 (C^infinity stationary
self-similar profiles of the 2D inviscid Boussinesq equations with the fourfold parity, a0 = Theta_y(0) != 0, the
canonical full-plane sublinear velocity U = o(|X|) and polynomially bounded Theta, Omega and their gradients), with
every exponent beta > 0. Section 1 states the class in full. Neither accepted endpoint (YES, independently validated
numerical evidence; NO, a rigorous nonexistence theorem for the whole class) was reached.

## Summary

Status: UNRESOLVED: 48h elapsed; active research duration not measured. Nonexistence is proved for 0 < beta <= 2. For beta > 2 neither
existence nor nonexistence is established, and no numerical state is offered as a candidate solution.

Proved results (statements with hypotheses in Section 3, proofs in Appendix A; each was checked by an independent
verifier with its own derivation or proof and by an external referee, a second model; Section 7 records the checks):
 - Theorems 1 to 3 and Corollary 4: there is no A1 profile with Theta, Psi in C^infinity, a0 != 0, U = o(|X|) and
   0 < beta <= 2. beta < 2 is excluded by the transport equation on the vertical axis alone; a bounded nonzero
   temperature forces beta = 2; beta = 2 is excluded for C^infinity profiles by a flatness argument at the neutral
   vertical eigenvalue (no finite-regularity version is claimed). Every class A' profile therefore has beta > 2 and
   an unbounded temperature, strictly monotone on the vertical axis.
 - Subclass exclusions that contain values beta > 2: Omega >= 0 on the open first quadrant (Proposition 6, with no
   integrability assumption), Theta_x >= 0 there (Proposition 13), finite L^p temperature (Proposition 5),
   compactly supported vorticity (Proposition 7), finite angular spectra (Proposition 19), and exact membership in the
   finite numerical representations used here, under the conditions stated there (Propositions 18, 27, 30).
 - Necessary conditions for beta > 2: far field Theta ~ r^(1 - 2/beta) F(phi) with F(pi/2) != 0 (Theorem 11), a
   two-branch far-field dichotomy with unbounded velocity and infinite kinetic energy (Theorem 12), finite-order far
   expansions (Theorems 15, 16), weighted integral identities (Proposition 14), the strain condition c = -2 as a
   vorticity moment (Proposition 17), centre Taylor identities consistent at every order (Proposition 26), and
   conditions on sign-changing vorticity (Propositions 33 to 40), none of which excludes its sign class in general.
 - A class A' profile would give a smooth self-similar solution with infinite-energy data whose temperature grows
   like |z|^(1 - 2/beta); it would not be blowup from bounded or finite-energy data (Section 2.5).

Best numerical evidence (numerical only; Section 6.9, Section 10.3): a transport-exact representation in which (P2)
and its Taylor identities hold exactly for stored functions with a recorded global chart certificate, with beta = 3
and the stored temperature coefficient held at 600 (the physical centre slope is 600/h, with h the centre value of
the chart; Section 6.9). For the state 134d9098 the
independent verifier found maxima 9.80e-7 (prompt ratio) and 7.83e-7 (grouped ratio) at 10000 independent points,
1.089e-6 and 8.65e-7 after zooms near the centre. Refined states with core degree 32 have the authors' sampled maxima
down to 3.0e-7 and 2.7e-7; at its finite point sets for those two states the verifier found at most about 5.62e-7
and 4.81e-7, and conditional interval enclosures at 1183 points of each show a nonzero vorticity residual at every
point. No stored state is exact (Propositions 27, 30, nonzero certified centre defects). Earlier polar least-squares
states have sampled core residual ratios between 3.6e-5 and 5.0e-4.

Exact remaining gap. Analytic: for beta > 2 no argument couples the centre jets (Propositions 17, 26) with the far-field
data (Theorems 11, 12, 15, 16). Separately, each end gives no contradiction at any proved order, and two leading
angular functions of the far field stay free. The first missing implication for NO is an exclusion of sign-changing
vorticity in class A' with beta > 2 (for example of Omega <= 0 on the first quadrant, or of one sign change on every
vertical line). Numerical: for YES, beta and a0 would have to be determined rather than held; three independent
full-plane fit and inverse domains are needed (only a row-split study was made); residual control beyond finite
point sets is needed; and a second method would have to reproduce the state (Section 10.6).

## 1. Solution class to which the headline applies

The headline applies to class A' of Section 2.3: triples (beta, Theta, Omega) with beta > 0; Theta and Psi in
C^infinity(R^2) with the A1 parity (Theta even in x and odd in y, Omega and Psi odd in x and in y);
a0 = Theta_y(0) != 0; U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x) the canonical velocity, with U = o(|X|) uniformly; the profile equations (P)
holding pointwise; and |Theta| + |Omega| + |grad Theta| + |grad Omega| <= C (1 + |X|)^m for some m. For this class
nonexistence is proved for 0 < beta <= 2 (Theorems 1 to 3, Corollary 4); for beta > 2 neither existence (numerical
evidence meeting the requirements listed in 10.6) nor nonexistence has been established. Each theorem
of Section 3 states the hypotheses it actually uses; several need much less than class A'. Section 3 states all 40
numbered general results proved in this report (theorems, a corollary and propositions), each with its lettered parts
and hypotheses; auxiliary lemmas inside the proofs of Appendix A and the exact certificates for stored numerical
states (Section 6) are not among them. Section 10.1 summarizes a selection.

## 2. Problem statement

### 2.1 Physical system and ansatz
On R^2 with coordinates z = (z1, z2):
  omega_t + u.grad omega = d_{z1} theta,   theta_t + u.grad theta = 0,   u = (-psi_{z2}, psi_{z1}),   -Lap psi = omega.
With these conventions curl u = Lap psi = -omega, so omega is minus the usual vorticity and the system is the
standard Boussinesq system for the buoyancy -theta.
Self-similar ansatz, tau = T - t: X = z/tau^beta, omega = tau^-1 Omega(X), theta = tau^(beta-2) Theta(X),
u = tau^(beta-1) U(X), psi = tau^(2 beta - 1) Psi(X). With W := beta X + U and lambda := beta - 2 the profile
equations are
  (P1) W.grad Omega + Omega = Theta_x,
  (P2) W.grad Theta = lambda Theta,
  (P3) -Lap Psi = Omega,  U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x).
div W = 2 beta.

### 2.2 Setting A1
Theta is even in x and odd in y; Omega and Psi are odd in x and odd in y. Both axes are invariant curves of W and
U(0) = 0. Jet: Theta = a0 y + O(|X|^3) with a0 = Theta_y(0) != 0 unknown (not normalized). beta > 0 unknown.

### 2.3 Canonical full-plane inverse and admissible class
Throughout, U = o(|X|) is meant uniformly: sup_{|X| >= R} |U(X)|/|X| -> 0 as R -> inf.
The velocity is the unique divergence-free field with curl U = -Omega, U = o(|X|) and the A1 parity (or U(0) = 0)
(uniqueness: the difference of two such fields has harmonic components of sublinear growth, hence is constant by
Liouville, and the constant is 0 by parity). When the integral converges it is given by the subtracted kernel
  U(X) = int [K(X-Y) - K(-Y)] Omega(Y) dY,   K(Z) = -(1/(2 pi)) Z^perp/|Z|^2,  Z^perp = (-Z2, Z1),
and, mode by mode for Omega = sum w_n(r) sin(n phi) (n even), by the modal Green formula
  P_n(r) = (1/(2n)) [ r^-n int_0^r s^(n+1) w_n(s) ds + r^n int_r^inf s^(1-n) w_n(s) ds ],
the unique solution of P'' + P'/r - n^2 P/r^2 = -w_n regular at 0 and o(r^2) at infinity. No affine strain,
uniform flow or harmonic field is added. The centre strain is c := Psi_xy(0). For beta > 2 and smooth A1 solutions with
U = o(|X|), |Omega| <= C (1 + |X|)^(-alpha') for some alpha' > 0 and |grad Omega| polynomially bounded (in particular in
class A', by the power decay in the proof of Theorem 11), it is given by the absolutely convergent integrals
  c = (1/pi) int xy |Y|^-4 Omega(Y) dY = (1/2) int_0^inf w_2(r) dr/r
(the second is the n = 2 modal Green formula at r = 0); the formula is not used outside this setting.

Class A' (main admissible class). (beta, Theta, Omega) with beta > 0, Theta, Psi in C^infinity(R^2) with the A1
parity and a0 != 0, U the canonical sublinear velocity, (P) holding pointwise, and |Theta| + |Omega| + |grad Theta|
+ |grad Omega| <= C (1 + |X|)^m for some m. A sufficient condition for the existence of the canonical velocity is
Omega -> 0 at infinity with int_{|Y|>1} |Omega| |Y|^-2 dY < inf; it is not necessary (example: Psi = sin x sin y / 2,
which has bounded velocity and non-decaying vorticity).

### 2.4 Elementary consequences
 - Order y of (P2): a0 (c + 2) = 0, hence c = -2 and DW(0) = diag(beta + 2, beta - 2).
 - With Theta = a0 y + b1 x^2 y + b2 y^3 + ..., Psi = -2xy + d1 x^3 y + d2 x y^3 + ..., Omega = g xy + ...:
   order x^2 y and y^3 of (P2) and order xy of (P1) give
     (T1) (2 beta + 4) b1 + 3 a0 d1 = 0,  (T2) 2 (beta - 2) b2 + a0 d2 = 0,  (T3) (2 beta + 1) g = 2 b1,
   with g = -6 (d1 + d2) from (P3).
 - Spatial scaling Theta -> l Theta(X/l), Omega -> Omega(X/l), Psi -> l^2 Psi(X/l) maps solutions to solutions and
   preserves beta, a0 and c. Theta -> -Theta is not a symmetry; both signs of a0 are permitted by the definition
   (existence for either sign is not established).

### 2.5 Physical reconstruction and conservation laws (what a profile would give)
Direct computations; none of them asserts that a profile exists.
 - Reconstruction. Let (beta, Theta, Omega, Psi) be smooth on R^2 with U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x), and define omega, theta, u, psi
   by the ansatz of 2.1 for t < T. For a profile function f and tau = T - t, d_t [tau^q f(X)] = tau^(q-1) [-q f + beta X.grad f](X)
   and grad_z [tau^q f(X)] = tau^(q-beta) (grad f)(X), hence
     omega_t + u.grad omega - d_{z1} theta = tau^(-2) [W.grad Omega + Omega - Theta_x](X),
     theta_t + u.grad theta = tau^(beta-3) [W.grad Theta - (beta - 2) Theta](X),
     -Lap psi = tau^(-1) (-Lap Psi)(X),   (-psi_{z2}, psi_{z1}) = tau^(beta-1) U(X) = u.
   The prefactors are nonzero and z -> z/tau^beta is a bijection of R^2 for each t, so the reconstruction solves the
   system of 2.1 classically on R^2 x (-inf, T) if and only if (P1) to (P3) hold on R^2. This is a local classical
   statement; it implies no global bound.
 - Parity and centre (Setting A1 and (P) assumed in addition). The parities are preserved: theta is even in z1 and odd
   in z2, omega and psi are odd in both, u1 is odd in z1 and even in z2, u2 is even in z1 and odd in z2; both axes are
   invariant and u(0, t) = 0. If U = o(|X|) uniformly, then sup_{|z| >= R} |u(z, t)|/|z| = tau^(-1) sup_{|X| >= R tau^(-beta)}
   |U|/|X| -> 0 as R -> inf, so at each t the velocity is the unique sublinear field with the given divergence, curl and
   parity (2.3). At the centre d_{z2} theta(0, t) = a0 (T - t)^(-2), Du(0, t) = (T - t)^(-1) diag(2, -2) (c = -2), and
   ||omega(t)||_inf = ||Omega||_inf/(T - t). For a class A' profile 0 < ||Omega||_inf < inf (Omega is smooth and
   O(r^(-1/beta)) by Theorem 11(a), and Omega = 0 would give U = 0, against c = -2), so the time integral of
   ||omega(t)||_inf up to T diverges.
 - Data and the limit t -> T (class A' profile; then beta > 2 by Corollary 4; delta = 1/beta, gamma = 1 - 2 delta, the
   angular functions of Theorems 11 and 12). Since tau^(-1) = |z|^(-delta) |X|^delta, the far-field limits of Theorem 11(b)
   give, as |z|/tau^beta -> inf (at spatial infinity for fixed t, and as t -> T at fixed z != 0),
   theta = |z|^gamma (F + o(1)), grad theta = |z|^(-2 delta) (gamma F e_r + F' e_phi + o(1)), and in branch (i) of
   Theorem 12 omega = |z|^(-delta) (A + o(1)), u = |z|^(1 - delta) (V + o(1)), in branch (ii) omega = tau |z|^(-2 delta)
   (B + o(1)), u = tau |z|^(1 - 2 delta) (V_2 + o(1)). So the data at any t0 < T are C^infinity, with temperature and
   velocity growing at spatial infinity; as t -> T, theta, u and omega have finite limits at every fixed z != 0 while
   the centre becomes singular, and the limiting temperature |z|^gamma F(phi) is not differentiable at the origin
   (0 < gamma < 1, F(pi/2) != 0). With R = tau^(-beta) one has theta(z, t) = R^(-gamma) Theta(R z),
   omega(z, t) = R^delta Omega(R z) and u(z, t) = R^(-(1 - delta)) U(R z), so Theorem 15(b), applied on dyadic annuli,
   gives convergence of theta, omega and u as t -> T in C^k on every compact subset of R^2 \ {0}, for every finite k,
   to |z|^gamma F, |z|^(-delta) A and |z|^(1 - delta) V (smooth away from 0 by Theorem 15(a); A = V = 0 in branch (ii));
   so every spatial derivative stays bounded on compact subsets of R^2 \ {0} up to T, while d_{z2} theta(0, t) diverges.
   No continuation through T is asserted.
 - Conservation laws (formal; with the conventions of 2.1 the momentum form is u_t + u.grad u = -grad p - theta e2).
   Temperature is transported along the volume-preserving particle flow, which exists for t < T because u is smooth and
   at most linearly growing, so d_t Phi(theta) + div(u Phi(theta)) = 0 for every C^1 function Phi. For a class A' profile
   int |Phi(theta)| dz = inf for every continuous Phi that is not identically zero: every large circle contains a point
   where theta takes a prescribed value s with Phi(s) != 0 (theta(0, z2) tends to +inf and -inf at the two ends of the
   vertical axis), and |grad theta| = O(|z|^(-2 delta)) keeps theta close to s on a disc of radius c |z|^(2 delta) around
   it; in particular every L^p norm of theta is infinite. The local energy balance is
   d_t (|u|^2/2 + z2 theta) + div(u (|u|^2/2 + p + z2 theta)) = 0, but int |u|^2 dz = tau^(4 beta - 2) int |U|^2 dX = inf
   at every t (Theorem 12) and int |z2 theta| dz = inf, so the usual finite kinetic and absolute potential energy
   assumptions fail (this does not address a renormalized or conditionally cancelled combined integral). The vorticity
   balance is
   d_t omega + div(u omega - theta e1) = 0; omega(t) lies in no L^p with p <= beta (Theorem 11(d)), so the absolute
   circulation and the enstrophy are infinite (the integral of omega over centred discs vanishes by parity), and the
   circulation around a material loop changes at the rate -(loop integral of theta dz2). The L^m balance of the
   vorticity closes for m > 2 beta: int |omega|^m dz = tau^(2 beta - m) M_m and int omega |omega|^(m-2) d_{z1} theta dz =
   tau^(2 beta - m - 1) B_m, with M_m = int |Omega|^m and B_m = int Theta_x Omega |Omega|^(m-2) absolutely convergent by
   Theorem 11, the flux at infinity vanishes, and d/dt int |omega|^m dz = m int omega |omega|^(m-2) d_{z1} theta dz is
   exactly the identity (1 - 2 beta/m) M_m = B_m of Proposition 14(c). At m = 2 beta the physical advective flux
   through large circles still vanishes at fixed t (|u| |omega|^(2 beta) |z| = O(|z|^(-delta))), but in branch (i) of
   Theorem 12 the moment int |omega|^(2 beta) dz is infinite; the profile identity there is Proposition 14(d), in which
   the flux of W |Omega|^m/m through large circles tends to (1/2) int |A|^(2 beta) dphi, positive in branch (i) and zero
   in branch (ii).
 - Meaning. A class A' profile would give a C^infinity solution on R^2 x (-inf, T), with infinite-energy data whose
   temperature grows like |z|^(1 - 2/beta) along the vertical axis; as t -> T the fields converge with every spatial
   derivative on compact sets away from z = 0 (above; the limits of omega and u vanish in branch (ii)), while the centre
   gradients diverge and the limiting temperature is not differentiable at z = 0. No extension beyond T is constructed.
   It would not be a blowup from finite-energy or decaying data; passing to such data would need a localization
   and a control of the far field that this report does not provide.
 Status: direct computation by the authors, checked by an external review and confirmed by the independent
 verification, conditional on an exact class A' profile and the cited theorems; time derivatives of all orders and
 continuation through T, and any renormalized energy, are not addressed.

## 3. Results (status at the freeze of the report body)

Every statement below is a partial result. The results comprise parameter and subclass exclusions, necessary
conditions, formal jet constructions, and conditional coordinate and certification results; none of them decides the
existence question for beta > 2. Complete proofs are in Appendix A and the dated verification record is in Section 7 (table) and Appendix B (full text). "Confirmed" means:
independent derivation by the independent verifier and an independent external audit, as recorded there.

Theorem 1 (axis exclusions). Hypotheses: beta > 0; T(y) := Theta(0, y) differentiable with T(0) = 0 and
T'(0) = a0 != 0; V(y) := W2(0, y) = beta y + U2(0, y) continuous; the axis equation V T' = lambda T on y > 0 (this is
(P2) on the invariant y-axis under the A1 parity); and U2(0, y) = o(y) as y -> inf (implied by U = o(|X|)).
 (a) 0 < beta < 2 is impossible.
 (b) If beta > 2, then V(y) > 0 for all y > 0, Theta(0, y) has the sign of a0 y, |Theta(0, y)| is strictly increasing
     on (0, inf), and |Theta(0, y)| >= C y^((beta - 2)/(beta + eps)) for every eps > 0 and large y. In particular
     Theta is unbounded.
 (c) Hence bounded Theta forces beta = 2.
Status: confirmed.

Theorem 2 (beta = 2 forces bounded temperature). Hypotheses: beta = 2, W in C^1 with U = o(|X|), Theta continuous
and constant along trajectories of W. Then sup_{R^2} |Theta| = max over a fixed closed ball. Status: confirmed.

Theorem 3 (smooth beta = 2 is excluded). Hypotheses: beta = 2, Theta and Psi in C^infinity(R^2) with the A1 parity,
a0 != 0, (P) holding pointwise, U = o(|X|). Then no such profile exists. No inverse formula, integrability, decay or
analyticity assumption is used. The proof uses flatness of every order; no finite C^k version is claimed.
Status: confirmed.

Corollary 4. Every profile of class A' has beta > 2 and unbounded temperature: Theta(0, y) is strictly increasing
on the whole y-axis if a0 > 0 (strictly decreasing if a0 < 0), and for every eps > 0,
|Theta(0, y)| >= C_eps y^((beta - 2)/(beta + eps)) for all sufficiently large y. (Theorems 1 and 3.)
Status: confirmed.

Proposition 5 (finite L^p norms). Hypotheses: beta > 0, W in C^1 with div W = 2 beta and complete flow, Theta
continuous with Theta(phi_s X) = e^(lambda s) Theta(X). If 0 < int |Theta|^p < inf for some p in [1, inf), then
beta = 2p/(p + 2) < 2. For A1 profiles (the hypotheses of Theorem 1) this is excluded by Theorem 1(a). If beta = 2
and Theta -> 0 at infinity, then Theta = 0 identically, which contradicts a0 != 0. Status: confirmed.

Proposition 6 (sign of the vorticity). In class A' (in fact for smooth odd-odd Psi with U = o(|X|) and c = -2),
Omega >= 0 on the open first quadrant Q1 is impossible. No strain-integrability condition, flow assumption or
inverse formula is used. Status: confirmed.

Proposition 7 (compactly supported vorticity). In class A', Omega cannot have compact support, for any beta > 0.
Smoothness of Theta near an exterior point of the x-axis is what the key step uses. Status: confirmed.

Proposition 8 (sign of the temperature, beta > 2). Hypotheses: beta > 2; W = beta X + U and Theta in C^1 with the
A1 parity; div U = 0 and U = o(|X|); (P2); a0 > 0 (for a0 < 0 reverse the signs). Then Theta > 0 on B intersected
with {y > 0}, where B is the set of points whose backward trajectory tends to 0. If 0 is the only equilibrium of W,
then B = R^2. Status: confirmed (the transport equation (P2) and the listed structure are needed: Theta = y(1 - |X|^2)
with W = 3X satisfies the other conditions and changes sign).

Proposition 9 (characteristic formula). Hypotheses: beta > 0, W = beta X + U and Theta, Omega in C^1, U = o(|X|),
(P1). There is a radius R such that every backward trajectory eventually enters the closed ball B_R and stays there;
the whole backward half-orbit of X lies in the closed ball of radius max(R, |X|). For every X in R^2,
Omega(X) = int_{-inf}^0 e^s Theta_x(phi_s X) ds. In particular Omega is determined by (W, Theta).
Status: confirmed.

Proposition 10 (spatial gauge). Hypotheses: beta > 0, smooth fields satisfying (P2), the A1 parity, div U = 0,
U = o(|X|), a0 != 0. Then tau(x) := Theta_y(x, 0) takes the value a0/2 at some finite x_h > 0, so the normalization
Theta_y(1, 0) = a0/2 is always available by spatial scaling. Status: confirmed.

Theorem 11 (far field for beta > 2). Hypotheses: beta > 2; Theta, Psi in C^infinity(R^2) with the A1 parity and
a0 != 0; U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x) with U = o(|X|) uniformly; (P) holding pointwise; |Omega| + |grad Omega| <= C (1 + |X|)^m
for some m (all of this holds in class A'). Put delta = 1/beta, gamma = 1 - 2 delta = lambda/beta and d = 2 - delta,
so 0 < delta < 1/2 and 3/2 < d < 2. Then:
 (a) |Theta| = O(r^gamma), |grad Theta| = O(r^(-2 delta)), |Omega| = O(r^(-delta)), |U| = O(r^(1 - delta)) as r -> inf.
 (b) Uniformly in the angle phi: r^(-gamma) Theta -> F, r^(2 delta) grad Theta -> gamma F e_r + F' e_phi,
     r^delta Omega -> A, r^(-(1 - delta)) U -> V = -H' e_r + d H e_phi, where F is C^1 and not identically zero,
     F(pi/2) is nonzero with the sign of a0, A is Holder continuous, and H is the unique 2 pi-periodic solution of
     -H'' - d^2 H = A (unique because d is not an integer).
 (c) r^(-gamma) Theta = F + r^(-delta) F_1 + o(r^(-delta)) uniformly in phi, with F_1 = gamma V_r F + V_phi F'.
 (d) Omega is not in L^p(R^2) for any 0 < p <= beta; more precisely int_{R<|X|<2R} |Omega| >= c R^(2 - 2 delta) for
     all large R.
Status: confirmed (external derivation checked by the authors; independent derivation and external review by the
independent verifier).

Proposition 13 (one-signed horizontal temperature derivative). Hypotheses: beta > 0, smooth fields with the A1
parity, a0 != 0, W = beta X + U, div U = 0, U = o(|X|) uniformly, (P1)-(P3), c = -2. Then Theta_x >= 0 on Q1 is
impossible, and Theta_x <= 0 on Q1 forces int_{Q1} |Omega|^p = inf for every 0 < p <= 2 beta. Status: confirmed.

Theorem 12 (far-field dichotomy; velocity growth). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11, exactly one of the
following holds.
 (i) A is not identically zero; then V is not identically zero and U = r^(1 - delta) (V + o(1)) uniformly.
 (ii) A = 0 identically; then B := sin(phi) F' - gamma cos(phi) F is continuous and not identically zero,
     Omega = r^(-2 delta) (B + o(1)) and U = r^(1 - 2 delta) (V_2 + o(1)) uniformly, with V_2 = -H_2' e_r
     + (2 - 2 delta) H_2 e_phi not identically zero and -H_2'' - (2 - 2 delta)^2 H_2 = B. In this branch Theta_x takes
     both signs on the open first quadrant, and if a0 > 0 so does Omega.
In either case, with h = 1 - delta in (i) and h = 1 - 2 delta in (ii), int_{R<|X|<2R} |U|^p >= c_p R^(2 + h p) for
every 0 < p < inf and all large R. Hence U is unbounded, belongs to no global L^p space, and the physical velocity
has infinite kinetic energy at every t < T. Status: confirmed.

Proposition 14 (weighted integral identities). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11 put k_* = 2 + 2 gamma = 4 - 4/beta,
I_k = int Theta^2 |X|^(-k) dX and J_k = int Theta^2 (U.X) |X|^(-k-2) dX.
 (a) For k_* < k < 4 both integrals converge absolutely and [beta (4 - k) - 4] I_k = k J_k; in particular J_k < 0.
 (b) At k = k_* the integral J_{k_*} converges absolutely, I_{k_*} = inf, and beta int_0^{2 pi} F^2 dphi = -k_* J_{k_*}.
 (c) For every m > 2 beta, (1 - 2 beta/m) int |Omega|^m = int Theta_x Omega |Omega|^(m-2), both absolutely convergent;
     in particular the right side is positive.
 (d) For m = 2 beta the source integral converges absolutely and
     int Theta_x Omega |Omega|^(2 beta - 2) dX = (1/2) int_0^{2 pi} |A|^(2 beta) dphi,
     which is positive in branch (i) of Theorem 12 and zero in branch (ii).
These are necessary conditions on an exact profile. With M_m = int |Omega|^m > 0 and B_m the source integral,
(c) is equivalent to beta = (m/2)(1 - B_m/M_m) for m > 2 beta. These identities alone do not determine or isolate
beta without independent information about the profile-dependent integrals or fluxes. Status: confirmed
(independent derivation and external review by the independent verifier; checked by the authors; external audit of
this wording).

Theorem 15 (smooth far field and second-order terms). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11:
 (a) F, A and V are C^infinity functions of phi, and for every integer k >= 0 and r >= 1
     |D^k Omega| <= C_k r^(-delta - k), |D^k Theta| <= C_k r^(gamma - k), |D^k U| <= C_k r^(1 - delta - k).
 (b) As R -> inf, R^(-gamma) Theta(R X), R^delta Omega(R X) and R^(-(1 - delta)) U(R X) converge in C^k(1 <= |X| <= 2)
     for every k to |X|^gamma F(arg X), |X|^(-delta) A(arg X) and |X|^(1 - delta) V(arg X).
 (c) With B = -delta V_r A + V_phi A' - gamma cos(phi) F + sin(phi) F', V_2 = -H_2' e_r + (2 - 2 delta) H_2 e_phi and H_2
     the unique 2 pi-periodic solution of -H_2'' - (2 - 2 delta)^2 H_2 = B (unique since 1 < 2 - 2 delta < 2), for each
     fixed integer k >= 0 the C^k(S^1) norms of
       r^(-gamma) Theta(r, .) - F - r^(-delta) F_1,  r^delta Omega(r, .) - A - r^(-delta) B,
       r^(-(1 - delta)) U(r, .) - V - r^(-delta) V_2
     are o(r^(-delta)) as r -> inf (F_1 as in Theorem 11(c)). No uniformity in k, no complete asymptotic series, no
     absence of logarithms in higher terms and no statement about continuation in time is asserted.
In branch (ii) of Theorem 12 (A = 0), B and V_2 reduce to the leading terms given there. Status: confirmed
(independent derivation and external review by the independent verifier; checked by the authors; external audit of this
wording, no substantive gap).

Theorem 16 (finite far expansion). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11 let N be an integer with 0 <= N < 4 beta - 1 and
put a_j = (j + 1) delta, d_j = 2 - a_j. There are C^infinity functions A_j, F_j (0 <= j <= N + 1) and V_j (0 <= j <= N) of
phi, with A_0 = A, F_0 = F, V_0 = V, such that for each fixed integer k >= 0 the C^k(S^1) norms of
   r^delta Omega(r, .) - sum_{j=0}^{N+1} r^(-j delta) A_j,   r^(-gamma) Theta(r, .) - sum_{j=0}^{N+1} r^(-j delta) F_j,
   r^(-(1 - delta)) U(r, .) - sum_{j=0}^{N} r^(-j delta) V_j
are o(r^(-(N+1) delta)), o(r^(-(N+1) delta)) and o(r^(-N delta)). Here V_j = -H_j' e_r + d_j H_j e_phi, H_j being the unique
solution with only sin(2 n phi) modes (n >= 1) of -H_j'' - d_j^2 H_j = A_j (unique since |d_j| < 2), and for 0 <= j <= N
   (j + 1) A_{j+1} = sum_{k+l=j} [ -a_l V_{k,r} A_l + V_{k,phi} A_l' ] - (gamma - j delta) cos(phi) F_j + sin(phi) F_j',
   (j + 1) F_{j+1} = sum_{k+l=j} [ (gamma - l delta) V_{k,r} F_l + V_{k,phi} F_l' ].
At beta = 3 one may take N = 10. The leading data F and A are not determined by these relations; they contain no
equation selecting beta. The homogeneous inverse is asserted only for A_j, 0 <= j <= N, where (j + 1) delta < 4. The
coefficients A_{N+1}, F_{N+1} and their stated remainders remain asserted when (N + 2) delta >= 4, but A_{N+1} is not
inverted here. At a = 4 an interior stream multipole or a resonant logarithmic term may occur at velocity order
r^(-3); no continuation of the velocity expansion through this threshold is proved. Status: confirmed (independent
derivation and external review by the independent verifier; checked by the authors; external audit of this wording, no
substantive gap).

Proposition 17 (centre jets). Let beta > 2 and let Theta, Omega, Psi be smooth near 0 and satisfy (P1)-(P3) there with
the A1 parity, Theta_y(0) = a0 != 0 and Psi_xy(0) = -2. Write the finite Taylor expansions Theta = sum a_ij x^(2i) y^(2j+1),
Psi = sum h_ij x^(2i+1) y^(2j+1) (each with its smooth remainder). For every even m >= 2 let C_m be the coefficient of
r^m sin(m phi) in the homogeneous degree m Taylor part of Psi; in particular C_2 = -1. For each n >= 1, given the lower
blocks, the coefficients a_ij, h_ij (i + j = n) are affine functions of h_(n,0), and C_(2n+2) = kappa_n h_(n,0) + (terms
of lower blocks), with kappa_n > 0 whenever a0 < [2n(beta - 2) + 8][2n(beta - 2) + 5]; kappa_1 = (2 - a0/D)/8 with
D = 2(beta + 2)(2 beta + 1) (D = 70 at beta = 3). Hence, for fixed beta > 2, a0 != 0 with a0 < D, and fixed
C_4, C_6, ..., any two local solutions with these data and h_00 = -2 have identical Taylor jets at the origin; since
D > 0 this holds for every a0 < 0. At a0 = 2D a solution must have C_4 = 0. For profiles in the class of Theorem 11 the
C_m are the moments of the profile's own vorticity,
   C_m = (1/(2m)) int_0^inf rho^(1-m) Omega_m(rho) d rho,  Omega_m(r) = (1/pi) int_0^(2 pi) Omega(r, phi) sin(m phi) d phi,
and for m = 2 this is the necessary condition int_0^inf rho^(-1) Omega_2(rho) d rho = -4. Independent prescription or
global realizability of a moment sequence is not asserted, nor is convergence of the Taylor series or uniqueness of
smooth solutions with given jets. The bounds [2n(beta - 2) + 8][2n(beta - 2) + 5] (70, 108, 154 at beta = 3 for
n = 1, 2, 3) are sufficient conditions, not exceptional amplitudes. Status: confirmed (independent derivation and
external review by the independent verifier; checked by the authors, including a direct symbolic coefficient computation
through n = 3; external audit of this wording, no substantive gap).

Proposition 18 (representation obstruction of the compactified basis). Let beta > 2 with 2 beta not an integer, put
p = 2 beta, n = ceil(p), and for L > 0 let E = 1 + (r/L)^2, rho = (r/L) E^(-1/2), z = E^(-delta/2).
 (a) Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11, let m be a positive odd integer such that the angular coefficient
     Theta_m(r) = (1/pi) int_0^(2 pi) Theta(r, phi) sin(m phi) d phi has F_m = lim r^(-gamma) Theta_m(r) != 0 (such m
     exists since F != 0). Then Theta_m cannot be written as rho^m E^(gamma/2) P_m(1 - 2z) with P_m of class C^n from
     the left at 1, in particular not with a polynomial P_m: in the variable z the representation requires the
     endpoint term (m - gamma) B_0 z^p/2, B_0 = L^gamma F_m.
 (b) Let Theta and Omega be finite angular sums with Theta_m = rho^m E^(gamma/2) P_m(1 - 2z) and
     Omega_m = rho^m E^(-delta/2) Q_m(1 - 2z), P_m and Q_m polynomials, Theta != 0, U the canonical velocity, and
     R_Theta = (beta X + U).grad Theta - (beta - 2) Theta. Then R_Theta does not vanish identically. If
     F = lim r^(-gamma) Theta != 0, then r^(-gamma) R_Theta = sum_{1 <= k < 2 beta} B_k(phi) r^(-k delta) + C(phi) r^(-2)
     + o(r^(-2)) with C = beta L^2 sum_m (m - gamma) F_m sin(m phi), a nonzero angular function.
Consequently no exact class A' profile with 2 beta not an integer lies in the finite compactified representation
used for the numerical states of Section 6. When 2 beta is an integer (for example beta = 3) this fractional-power
obstruction disappears; no existence or exact-membership conclusion follows. The proposition provides no
quantitative residual bound for the numerical domains, norms and degrees used, and does not explain why the fits
prefer beta near 3. At beta = 3 the external audit noted that the velocity threshold a = 4 of Theorem 16 might
force a term z^12 log z in the temperature factor; this is a possible further obstruction, not proved and not used.
Status: confirmed (independent derivation and external review by the independent verifier; checked by the authors;
external audit of this wording, no substantive gap).

Proposition 19 (finite angular spectra are excluded). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 11, for every integer M >= 0
there are r > 0 and an angular frequency j > M such that the j-th angular Fourier coefficient of Omega(r, .) or of
Theta(r, .) is nonzero. Equivalently, at least one of Omega, Theta has infinitely many angular coefficient functions
that are not identically zero on (0, inf). The statement concerns exact finite spectra only: it does not exclude rapid
angular decay, gives no lower bound for the residual of an angular truncation, and does not decide the existence
question. Status: confirmed (independent derivation and external review by the independent verifier; checked by the authors; external audit of this wording, no substantive gap).

Proposition 20 (source coordinates; reconstruction of Theta and Omega from the velocity). Let beta > 2 and let U be a
smooth divergence-free vector field on R^2 with the A1 velocity parity (U1 odd in x and even in y, U2 even in x and odd
in y), U(X) = o(|X|) as |X| -> inf uniformly in direction, and DU(0) = diag(2, -2). Put a = beta + 2, b = beta - 2,
W = beta X + U, let Phi_t be the flow of W (complete, since W grows at most linearly) and let B be the backward basin of
the origin, the set of X with Phi_t X -> 0 as t -> -inf (an open, flow-invariant neighbourhood of 0). Write
W = (x A, y B0) with A, B0 smooth and even in both variables, A(0) = a, B0(0) = b.
 (a) The functions
       xi(X) = x exp(-int_{-inf}^0 [A(Phi_s X) - a] ds),   eta(X) = y exp(-int_{-inf}^0 [B0(Phi_s X) - b] ds)
     are smooth on B, and H = (xi, eta) is an area-preserving diffeomorphism of B onto R^2 with H(X) = X + O(|X|^3),
     xi odd in x and even in y, eta even in x and odd in y, and H(Phi_t X) = (e^(a t) xi(X), e^(b t) eta(X)).
 (b) For every real a0, Theta = a0 eta is the only C^1 function on B with Theta = a0 y + o(|X|) at 0 and
     W.grad Theta = (beta - 2) Theta (no parity is needed for the uniqueness).
 (c) For this Theta, Omega(X) = int_{-inf}^0 e^s Theta_x(Phi_s X) ds is the unique classical C^1 solution of
     W.grad Omega + Omega = Theta_x on B that is bounded in a neighbourhood of 0; it is smooth, odd in each variable and
     O(|X|^2) at 0.
 (d) Let K be a compact subset of B and T > 0. Along the path Phi_s X, -T <= s <= 0, solve q' = [b I - DW(Phi_s X)^T] q,
     w' = q_1 - w (q_1 the first component of q) with q(-T) = a0 e_y, w(-T) = 0, and put
     Theta_T(X) = a0 e^(b T) y(Phi_(-T) X). Then |Theta_T - Theta| + |q(0) - grad Theta| + |w(0) - Omega| <= C_K e^(-2 b T)
     on K for all T > 0. This concerns exact trajectories and exact solutions of these ordinary differential equations;
     it is not a discretization estimate.
Consequently, any class A' profile with beta > 2 and B = R^2 satisfies Theta = a0 eta and Omega = Omega[U, a0], the
function of (c). Define T_(beta, a0)(U) to be the canonical velocity of Omega[U, a0] whenever that canonical inverse is
admissible. Every such profile satisfies U = T_(beta, a0)(U). Not asserted: inverse admissibility for arbitrary
prescribed velocities; that T_(beta, a0) maps any class of velocities into itself; the full-basin property B = R^2 for
a sought profile; existence of a fixed point. Status: confirmed (independent derivation and external review in the
independent verification; checked by the authors; external audit of this wording, no substantive gap, scope
clarifications incorporated).

Proposition 21 (angular limits of the source coordinates). Let beta > 2, delta = 1/beta, alpha = 1 + 2 delta,
gamma = 1 - 2 delta and q = alpha/gamma > 1. Let U be as in Proposition 20 and assume in addition
|D^k U(X)| <= C_k |X|^(1 - delta - k) for |X| >= 1 and every k >= 0 (true for profiles in the class of Theorem 11, by
Theorem 15(a)), and B = R^2. Then there are C^infinity functions g, h of phi such that, in every C^k(S^1) norm,
     r^(-alpha) xi(r, .) = g + O(r^(-delta)),   r^(-gamma) eta(r, .) = h + O(r^(-delta)),
with g, h > 0 on (0, pi/2), g(0) > 0, h(pi/2) > 0, h'(0) > 0, g even about 0 and odd about pi/2, h odd about 0 and even
about pi/2, and
     alpha g h' - gamma g' h = 1,   g(phi) = (1/gamma) h(phi)^q int_phi^(pi/2) h(s)^(-q-1) ds  (0 < phi <= pi/2).
Let d_j be the Taylor coefficients of the smooth even function (h(phi)/phi)^(-q-1) at 0 (a finite expansion with
remainder at each order; convergence of the series is not asserted). If q is not an even integer then
     lim_(eps -> 0+) [ int_eps^(pi/2) h(s)^(-q-1) ds - sum_(2j < q) d_j eps^(2j - q)/(q - 2j) ] = 0;
if q = 2 l is an even integer then d_l = 0, and the finite part need not vanish (for the pair below at beta = 6, q = 2,
d_1 = 0 and the finite part is -1/3). For a profile in the class of Theorem 11 with B = R^2, Theta = a0 eta by
Proposition 20(b), so the far-field function of Theorem 11 is F = a0 h and these are necessary conditions on
h = F/a0. At beta = 3 (q = 5) they state that, with (F(phi)/phi)^(-6) = D_0 + D_1 phi^2 + D_2 phi^4 + O(phi^6),
     lim_(eps -> 0+) [ int_eps^(pi/2) F(phi)^(-6) d phi - D_0/(5 eps^5) - D_1/(3 eps^3) - D_2/eps ] = 0,
a statement valid for either sign of a0. The angular conditions alone impose no restriction on beta > 2: for every such
beta the pair g = cos theta, h = sin theta, with theta defined by phi = theta + delta sin(2 theta), satisfies the stated
symmetries, signs, differential identity, integral formula and endpoint conditions. This does not establish a velocity
realizing the pair, smooth source coordinates at the origin for it (the homogeneous extension (r^alpha g, r^gamma h)
is not C^1 at 0), a coupled profile or its canonical inverse relation, and no statement about the vorticity equation
follows. Status: confirmed (independent derivation and external review in the independent verification; checked by the authors; external audit of this wording, no substantive gap, scope clarifications incorporated).

Proposition 22 (transport errors; the temperature residual does not control the reconstruction). Let beta > 2,
b = beta - 2, let U be a smooth prescribed velocity, W = beta X + U with DW_ij = partial_j W_i, and let X be a point
whose flow line Phi_s X exists for -T <= s <= 0. On a flow tube containing this path let Theta, Omega be smooth with
residuals R_Theta = W.grad Theta - b Theta and R_Omega = W.grad Omega + Omega - Theta_x, and let Theta^, Omega^ be smooth
exact solutions of W.grad Theta^ = b Theta^ and W.grad Omega^ + Omega^ = Theta^_x there. Put e = Theta^ - Theta,
q = grad e, z = Omega^ - Omega, and let P(t, s) solve partial_t P(t, s) = (b I - DW(Phi_t X)^T) P(t, s), P(s, s) = I
(equivalently P(t, s) = e^(b (t - s)) [D Phi_(t - s)(Phi_s X)]^(-T)).
 (a) e(X) = e^(b T) e(Phi_(-T) X) - int_(-T)^0 e^(-b s) R_Theta(Phi_s X) ds,
     q(X) = P(0, -T) q(Phi_(-T) X) - int_(-T)^0 P(0, s) grad R_Theta(Phi_s X) ds,
     z(X) = e^(-T) z(Phi_(-T) X) + int_(-T)^0 e^s [q_1 - R_Omega](Phi_s X) ds   (q_1 the first component of q).
     These are finite-time identities; discarding the boundary terms requires separate estimates.
 (b) partial_x R_Theta = W1 Theta_xx + W2 Theta_xy + (partial_x W1) Theta_x + (partial_x W2) Theta_y - b Theta_x.
     Assume the A1 parities: Theta even in x and odd in y, W1 odd in x and even in y, W2 even in x and odd in y (the
     parity of Theta alone is not sufficient). Then each of the five terms is odd in x and odd in y, each term divided
     by x y extends smoothly to the axes, and the sum of the absolute values of the five terms divided by |x y| extends
     continuously. For relative residuals we use the conventions that 0/0 = 0 and that points with a nonzero numerator
     and a zero denominator are reported separately; the quotient of partial_x R_Theta by the absolute-term sum need not
     extend continuously where the divided sum vanishes. A common parity factor x or x y cancels in a relative residual
     and does not by itself make it small.
 (c) Take U = (2x, -2y), so W = (a x, b y) with a = beta + 2, and a0 > 0. Among C^1 solutions on the plane, the
     temperature with Theta^(0) = 0 and grad Theta^(0) = (0, a0) is unique and equals a0 y, and the vorticity bounded
     near 0 is unique and equals 0. Let f be a smooth, even, nonnegative, compactly supported function that vanishes on
     [-1, 1] and has f' > 0 on (1, 3/2), put J(zeta) = int_0^1 t^b f'(zeta t^a) dt and, for k >= 1,
          Theta_k = a0 y + y f(k x)/k,   Omega_k = y J(k x).
     These fields have the A1 parities and equal a0 y and 0 on the strip |x| < 1/k; R_Omega = 0 exactly,
     R_Theta = (a/k) y (k x) f'(k x) tends to 0 uniformly on bounded sets, and on the whole plane
          |R_Theta|/N_Theta <= a sup_zeta |zeta f'(zeta)| / (2 b a0 k),   N_Theta = |W1 Theta_x| + |W2 Theta_y| + b |Theta|
     (0/0 = 0 on y = 0), while Omega_k(3/(2k), 1) = J(3/2) > 0 for every k. So, for a prescribed velocity, a small
     temperature residual, even a small normalized one, does not control the reconstructed vorticity in C^0; the
     gradient of R_Theta, which here does not tend to 0, enters through (a).
This velocity is affine, not sublinear and not the canonical velocity of its vorticity, and the fields are not
profiles; no estimate for the coupled problem is excluded. Status: confirmed (independent derivation and external
review in the independent verification; checked by the authors; external audit of this wording, scope
corrections incorporated).

Proposition 23 (a generating function for the source coordinates). Let beta > 2, a = beta + 2, b = beta - 2, and let
U, B and the source coordinates (xi, eta) be those of Proposition 20(a).
 (a) On a simply connected open set V of B on which eta_y > 0 and (x, y) -> (x, eta) is one-to-one there is a smooth
     function G on the image of V in the (x, eta) plane with y = G_x, xi = G_eta and
     A := G_(x eta) = 1/eta_y(x, G_x(x, eta)) > 0. If V is a connected neighbourhood of 0 invariant under both
     reflections, then, normalized by G(0, 0) = 0, G is odd in x and odd in eta and G = x eta + O((|x| + |eta|)^4).
     The parity uses the parities of xi and eta in Proposition 20(a): other source coordinates need not give it (at
     beta = 4, xi + kappa eta^3 is also area preserving, conjugates the flow to the same linear flow and equals
     x + O(|X|^3), but adds kappa eta^4/4 to G). If B = R^2, eta_y > 0 everywhere and eta(x, y) -> +-inf as
     y -> +-inf for each x, the chart is global.
 (b) Conversely, let G be smooth on an open set of the (x, eta) plane with A = G_(x eta) > 0, put B0 = G_xx,
     C = G_(eta eta), M = a G_eta - b eta C, and use the coordinates (x, y) = (x, G_x) (assumed one-to-one). Define
     W1 = M/A, W2 = B0 M/A + b eta A, U = W - beta (x, G_x), Theta = a0 eta,
     Psi = beta x G_x + b eta G_eta - 2 beta G, and Omega = -(Dx^2 + Dy^2) Psi with the physical derivatives
     Dx = partial_x - (B0/A) partial_eta and Dy = (1/A) partial_eta (Dx^2 and Dy^2 are compositions of operators, so their
     coefficients are differentiated). Then U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x), div U = 0, div W = 2 beta and W.grad Theta = b Theta
     hold identically, Theta_x = -a0 B0/A, and (P1) is equivalent to the single scalar equation
          [(M/A) partial_x + b eta partial_eta] Omega + Omega = -a0 B0/A,
     which is in general of fourth order in G.
 (c) Let G be smooth on the whole (x, eta) plane with A > 0 everywhere, odd in x and in eta, G = x eta +
     O((|x| + |eta|)^4), and G_x -> +-inf as eta -> +-inf for each x, and let a0 != 0. Then (x, eta) -> (x, G_x) is a
     diffeomorphism onto R^2, the fields of (b) are smooth on the physical plane with the A1 parities,
     Psi_xy(0) = -2 and Theta = a0 y + O(|X|^3). If moreover G_eta -> +-inf as x -> +-inf for each eta, then
     (G_eta, eta) is a global diffeomorphism conjugating the flow of W to (xi, eta) -> (e^(a t) xi, e^(b t) eta), so
     the flow is complete and the backward basin of 0 is the whole plane. If in addition U = o(|X|) uniformly, then
     U is the canonical velocity of Omega in the sense of Section 2.3 (U is divergence-free with curl U = -Omega by
     construction and has the A1 parity; that definition is by uniqueness, and convergence of the subtracted kernel
     integral is not asserted, see the sufficient condition there); if also Theta, Omega and their first derivatives
     are polynomially bounded, a solution of the scalar equation of (b) is a class A' profile.
Not asserted: that every profile has eta_y > 0 globally or a global (x, eta) chart; existence of a solution of the
scalar equation; any selection of beta. The dilation symmetry acts by G_l(x, eta) = l^2 G(x/l, eta/l). Status:
confirmed (independent derivation and external review in the independent verification; checked by the authors;
external audit of this wording, scope corrections incorporated).

Proposition 24 (backward basin, temperature sign and stagnation points). Let beta > 2, b = beta - 2, and let
(beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in class A'. Then W = beta X + U is smooth with div W = 2 beta and
|W(X)| <= C (1 + |X|), so its flow is complete; DW(0) = diag(beta + 2, b); B denotes the backward basin of the origin
(Proposition 20).
 (a) B = R^2 if and only if a0 y Theta(x, y) > 0 for every (x, y) with y != 0. In that case W1(x, 0) has the sign of
     x for x != 0; in particular the origin is the only zero of W on the x-axis.
 (b) If grad Theta(P) != 0 at every P with W(P) = 0, then the origin is the only zero of W and B = R^2.
 (c) Consequently, if B != R^2, there is at least one P != 0 with W(P) = 0, Theta(P) = 0, grad Theta(P) = 0 and
     Omega(P) = 0, and at every such P the matrix DW(P) is symmetric with trace 2 beta.
 (d) Let P be as in (c) and put A = DW(P), H = D^2 Theta(P), v = grad Omega(P) and e_x = (1, 0). Then
     A^T H + H A = b H and (A^T + I) v = H e_x. In an orthonormal eigenbasis of A (eigenvalues l1, l2 with
     l1 + l2 = 2 beta; e_x expressed in the same basis) H is diagonal and (2 l_i - b) H_ii = 0. Hence H = 0 unless an
     eigenvalue of A equals b/2; if H != 0, then H has rank one, the eigenvalues of A are b/2 and 2 beta - b/2, A is
     positive definite and v = (A + I)^(-1) H e_x; if A is not positive definite, then H = 0; if H = 0 and -1 is not an
     eigenvalue of A, then v = 0. If Theta has a first nonzero homogeneous Taylor polynomial p_m at P (necessarily
     m >= 2), then every monomial z1^i z2^j occurring in p_m, in eigen-coordinates z1, z2 of A, satisfies
     i l1 + j l2 = b.
 (e) If moreover A is positive definite (P is then a hyperbolic source of W), exactly one of the following holds:
     (e1) Theta and Omega vanish identically on the backward basin B_P of P (the set of X with Phi_(-t) X -> P as
     t -> infinity), which is open, contains a neighbourhood of P and is invariant under the flow; U is curl-free and
     divergence-free on B_P, all derivatives of Theta and Omega vanish on its closure, and the origin is not in that
     closure; (e2) Theta is not identically zero on any
     neighbourhood of P, its first nonzero homogeneous Taylor polynomial p_m exists, the smaller eigenvalue of A equals
     b/m for an integer m >= 2, the larger equals 2 beta - b/m, and p_m = C z_min^m with C != 0, z_min being the
     coordinate along the eigenvector of the smaller eigenvalue. In particular, if the smaller eigenvalue exceeds b/2,
     (e1) holds.
Hypotheses actually used: (a) and (b) use only (P2), the A1 parities, Theta = a0 y + o(|X|) at 0 with a0 != 0,
div U = 0, U = o(|X|) uniformly and the smoothness of U (Theta in C^1 suffices for (a)); (c) uses in addition (P1)
and curl U = -Omega; (d) and (e) use, beyond the properties of P supplied by (c), only the smoothness of the fields
near P and (P1), (P2) there. Part (d) and the Taylor alternative in (e) are local necessary conditions; the vanishing in (e1) propagates to the
whole basin B_P (this uses in addition the complete flow and (P1), (P2) on B_P). The local equations alone do not force
DW(P) to be singular: with k = beta - b/2, the fields Psi = -k x y, U = (k x, -k y), W = ((2 beta - b/2) x, (b/2) y),
Omega = 0, Theta = y^2 satisfy (P1)-(P3) everywhere and have Theta, grad Theta and Omega vanishing at the equilibrium 0,
where DW is positive definite (an instance of (e2) with m = 2); they violate the oddness of Theta in y, the condition
a0 != 0 and the sublinearity of U, so this example makes no existence claim in class A'. Relation to Proposition 8: that proposition gives "B = R^2 implies the strict sign" and "a unique
zero of W implies B = R^2"; new here are the converse of the first, the sufficient condition (b) and the restriction (c).
By (a), for class A' profiles with beta > 2 the hypothesis B = R^2 of Propositions 20 and 21 is equivalent to the strict
sign of the temperature. Part (c) asserts the existence of at least one such P; it does not describe every additional
zero of W. Not asserted: that the sign condition of (a) or the condition of (b) holds for a sought profile, that a
point P as in (c) cannot exist, or that DW(P) is singular at such a point. Status: confirmed (independent derivations,
each with two rounds of external review, in the independent verification; checked by the authors; external audits
of this wording, corrections incorporated).

Proposition 25 (stagnation points on the horizontal axis). Let beta > 2, a = beta + 2, b = beta - 2, let
(beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in class A', put sigma = sign(a0), V(x) = W1(x, 0) and tau(x) = Theta_y(x, 0) for
real x, and let x1 be the smallest positive zero of V (x1 = inf if there is none). Then:
 (a) V is odd, tau is even, V'(0) = a, tau(0) = a0, V(x) > 0 for all large x, and V tau' = (V' - a) tau on R. On an
     interval J containing no zero of V, tau(x) = tau(x_J) (V(x)/V(x_J)) exp(-a int_{x_J}^x du/V(u)) for x, x_J in J,
     so tau vanishes either identically on J or nowhere on J. sigma tau > 0 on [0, x1).
 (b) Let x0 > 0 be a zero of V with l = V'(x0) != 0 such that tau does not vanish identically on any neighbourhood
     of x0. Then exactly one of the following holds: (b1) l = a and tau(x0) != 0, so DW(x0, 0) = diag(a, b) and
     grad Theta(x0, 0) = (0, tau(x0)) != 0; (b2) l = -a/(k - 1) for an integer k >= 2, tau vanishes at x0 to order
     exactly k, and Theta, grad Theta and D^2 Theta vanish at (x0, 0).
 (c) At every zero x0 > 0 of V with V'(x0) = 0, tau is flat. If in addition V > 0 on (x0, x0 + e), or V < 0 on
     (x0 - e, x0), for some e > 0 (an outgoing side), then tau vanishes identically on that interval.
 (d) If V has a positive zero, then either V'(x1) = -a/(k - 1) for an integer k >= 2 and tau vanishes at x1 to order
     exactly k, or V'(x1) = 0 and tau is flat at x1. In both cases P1 = (x1, 0) is a zero of W with Theta(P1) = 0 and
     grad Theta(P1) = 0.
 (e) If x1 is a simple zero (first case of (d)), then V has a smallest zero x2 in (x1, inf), sigma (-1)^k tau > 0 on
     (x1, x2], V'(x2) = a, and P2 = (x2, 0) is a hyperbolic source of W with the same linearization diag(a, b) as the
     origin and grad Theta(P2) = (0, tau(x2)) != 0; the backward basins of P2 and of the origin are disjoint open sets.
 (f) If P is a zero of W with Theta(P) = 0 and grad Theta(P) = 0, and X satisfies |Phi_(-t) X - P| <= C e^(-mu t) for
     all t >= 0 with mu > b/2, then Theta(X) = 0. If V has a positive zero, P1 = (x1, 0) has DW(P1) = diag(l, 2 beta - l)
     with l = V'(x1) <= 0 as in (d), and there is a C^1 curve through P1, tangent there to the y-direction and invariant
     under y -> -y, on which Theta vanishes: in the first case of (d) (l = -a/(k - 1) < 0, P1 a hyperbolic saddle) the
     global unstable manifold {X : Phi_(-t) X -> P1 as t -> inf}, an injectively immersed C^1 one-dimensional manifold;
     in the second case (l = 0) a strong unstable curve, the union of the forward images of a local C^1 curve through
     P1 along which backward orbits converge to P1 at an exponential rate mu > b/2 (it need not contain every point
     whose backward orbit converges to P1). In both cases each of the two orbits forming the
     curve minus P1 stays in one open half-plane, so the zero set of Theta in the open upper half-plane is nonempty and
     accumulates at P1.
Hypotheses actually used: smoothness, the A1 parities, (P2), div W = 2 beta, U = o(|X|), DW(0) = diag(a, b) and the
completeness of the flow; (P1), (P3), the canonical-velocity condition and the polynomial bounds are not used. Relation
to Propositions 10 and 24: (a) is the axis equation behind Proposition 10; (d) and (f) make Proposition 24(c) explicit
when the strict sign of the temperature fails at the horizontal axis; the vanishing order in (b2) is the resonance
i l1 + j l2 = b of Proposition 24(d) with i = k, j = 1. Not asserted: that V has, or has no, positive zero for a
sought profile. Status: confirmed (derived by the authors;
independent derivation by the independent verifier with two rounds of external review; external audit of the wording,
corrections incorporated).

Proposition 26 (formal centre jets exist for every beta > 2 and a0 != 0). Let beta > 2, a0 != 0, a = beta + 2,
b = beta - 2, L = a x d_x + b y d_y, and let f_2, f_3, ... be arbitrary real numbers. Then there is exactly one formal
power series G(x, eta) = x eta + sum_{n >= 2} H_{2n}(x, eta), each H_{2n} a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2n odd in x
and in eta whose coefficient of x^(2n-1) eta is f_n, such that the fields of Proposition 23(b) built from G (formal
chart y = G_x, Theta = a0 eta, Psi = beta x G_x + b eta G_eta - 2 beta G, U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x), Omega = -Lap Psi,
W = beta X + U, all as formal power series in (x, y)) satisfy (P1) and (P2) coefficient by coefficient. These formal
fields have the A1 parities, Theta_y(0) = a0 and Psi_xy(0) = -2; the coefficient of xy in Omega is -6 a0 f_2/(2 beta + 1),
so Omega is not identically zero if f_2 != 0 (for f_n = 0 for all n the series is G = x eta, with the exact fields
Theta = a0 y, Psi = -2xy, Omega = 0, which violate the canonical sublinearity). More precisely, at each even
degree N >= 4 the degree N - 2 part of the residual of (P1) is affine in H_N with linear part
   T_N H = -(L + 1) Lap (L - 2 beta) H + a0 H_xx,
and T_N, restricted to the odd-odd homogeneous polynomials of degree N without the monomial x^(N-1) y, is a bijection
onto the odd-odd homogeneous polynomials of degree N - 2. For every even N >= 4, the truncation of G through degree N
defines smooth fields on a neighbourhood of 0 (depending on N) that satisfy (P2) exactly and (P1) up to O(|X|^N) (for odd
N only O(|X|^(N-1)) holds in general).
Consequently, for every beta > 2 and a0 != 0 the complete system of Taylor coefficient identities obtained from
(P1)-(P3), the A1 parity and the centre conditions is formally consistent, also with f_2 != 0; coefficientwise
compatibility at the centre imposes no restriction on (beta, a0). Restrictions arising from convergence, estimates,
realization by actual solutions, or global compatibility are not addressed. Not asserted: convergence of the series,
realization of a prescribed formal jet by an actual local or global solution, or compatibility with the canonical global
inverse or its moment constraints. Relation to Proposition 17: with the lower coefficients fixed,
h_(n-1,0) = 2a(n - 1) f_n + C_n, where h_(n-1,0) is the coefficient of x^(2n-1) y in Psi and C_n depends only on
f_2, ..., f_(n-1), so at each degree the free coefficients correspond by an affine bijection (the correspondence of whole
sequences is nonlinear, for example h_20 = 4a f_3 - 6a f_2^2). Any use of the canonical-moment identification of
Proposition 17 keeps the additional hypotheses of that result; none of them is used here.
Status: confirmed (independent derivation and exact symbolic checks by the independent verifier with two rounds of
external review; generating-function form and exact symbolic check of T_N at degrees 4 and 6 by the authors;
external audit of this wording, corrections incorporated).

Proposition 27 (no finite member of the logarithmic generating family solves (P1) near the centre). Let beta = 3,
alpha > 0, s > 0 and a0 != 0, put d = 1 - e^(-alpha), and for real (x, eta) let
   E = 1 + x^2 + (eta/s)^6,   t = -log(1 - d E^(-1/6))/alpha,   w = (eta/s)^2 E^(-1/3),
   xi_l = x^2/(R_l^2 + x^2),   zeta_l = eta^2/(R_l^2 + eta^2),
   G = x eta E^(1/3) [ P(t, w) + sum_{l=1}^m exp(-(x^2 + eta^2)/L_l^2) Q_l(xi_l, zeta_l) ],
where m >= 0, P and Q_1, ..., Q_m are real polynomials in two variables and R_l, L_l > 0 (a member of the logarithmic
generating family). Assume h := G_(x eta)(0, 0) = P(1, 0) + sum_l Q_l(0, 0) > 0. Then (x, eta) -> (x, G_x) has a real
analytic inverse eta(x, y) near 0, and the fields of Proposition 23(b) at beta = 3,
   Theta = a0 eta,  Psi = 3x G_x + eta G_eta - 6G,  U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x),  Omega = -Lap Psi,  W = 3X + U,
are real analytic on a neighbourhood of 0, have the A1 parities, Psi_xy(0) = -2 and Theta_y(0) = a0/h, and satisfy
(P2) and (P3) there; but they do not satisfy (P1) on any neighbourhood of 0: the residual W.grad Omega + Omega -
Theta_x is not identically zero on any neighbourhood of X = 0. Here alpha > 0, s > 0, a0 != 0, the degrees and
coefficients of P and Q_l, the number m of patches and the scales R_l, L_l > 0 are arbitrary. In particular R_l = 1 is
allowed: the first form of this result assumed R_l != 1 (then the patch coefficients are holomorphic at the complex point
used in the proof), and this restriction is removed by the meromorphic case analysis of the proof. Only the total h must
be positive (P(1, 0) may be zero or negative), and no global chart, tail bound or velocity inverse is assumed. The case
alpha = 0 is not covered. Finite sums of products of shifted Chebyshev polynomials are polynomials, so the stored
beta = 3 states of Section 6.9 (t = tau at alpha = 3, s = s_e, core functions with R = 0.1, L = 0.4) are members (the
runs of Section 6.9 at other fixed exponents or with a free exponent are not); this
proposition is the precise form of the paragraph "No finite member with h > 0 is exact" there. Not asserted: any positive lower
bound for the residual of (P1) of a member, uniform or not in the degrees, the number of patches or the coefficients
(no quantitative residual bound is provided, and neither a uniform residual floor for fits in this family nor its
absence is established); any statement about limits as the degrees or the number of patches tend
to infinity; anything about other representations (other radial maps or exponents in E, different radii in the two
patch variables, infinite series, general analytic or smooth G); anything about class A' or Setting A1 in general;
anything for alpha = 0 or beta != 3. Status: confirmed in the independent verification (independent derivation, exact symbolic identities, high-precision
evaluations as precision checks only, and external case reviews); this text (statement, outline and A.28 Steps 1 to 8)
confirmed by the independent verifier and by an external audit, with two outline sentences corrected as proposed; the
multipliers, case computations and domination arguments of A.28 rechecked by the authors.

Proposition 28 (canonical velocity and flow for members with a global positive chart). Let G be a member of the
logarithmic generating family of Proposition 27 (alpha > 0, s > 0, real polynomials P, Q_l, scales R_l, L_l > 0), let
a0 != 0, let Theta, Psi, U, Omega, W be the fields of Proposition 27, and assume that for a constant delta > 0
   (H)   A := G_(x eta)(x, eta) >= delta E^(1/3)   for every (x, eta) in R^2.
 (a) (x, eta) -> (x, G_x) is a diffeomorphism of R^2 onto R^2; the fields are smooth on R^2, have the A1 parities and
     satisfy (P2), (P3) and div U = 0 identically; h = G_(x eta)(0, 0) >= delta, Psi = -2xy + O(|X|^4) and
     Theta = (a0/h) y + O(|X|^3).
 (b) W vanishes only at 0, DW(0) = diag(5, 1) and DU(0) = diag(2, -2). The map X -> (G_eta(x, eta(X)), eta(X)) is an
     area-preserving diffeomorphism of R^2 that conjugates the flow of W to (xi, eta) -> (e^(5 sigma) xi, e^sigma eta).
     Hence the flow is complete, both axes are invariant, the backward basin of 0 is R^2, and W has no periodic orbit and
     no bounded complete orbit other than {0}.
 (c) For every n >= 0 there is C_n with, for all X, <X> = (1 + |X|^2)^(1/2),
        |D^n Psi(X)| <= C_n <X>^(5/3 - n),   |D^n U(X)| <= C_n <X>^(2/3 - n),
        |D^n Omega(X)| <= C_n <X>^(-1/3 - n),   |D^n Theta(X)| <= C_n <X>^(1/3 - n).
     In particular U = o(|X|) uniformly and Omega -> 0.
 (d) For every X the subtracted integral int [K(X - Y) - K(-Y)] Omega(Y) dY of Section 2.3 converges absolutely; it is a
     smooth function of X and equals U. So U is the canonical velocity of Omega, given by this integral, with no added
     affine strain or harmonic field.
 (e) c |y|^(1/3) <= |Theta(0, y)| <= C |y|^(1/3) for |y| >= 1, with c, C > 0; in particular Theta is unbounded on the
     vertical axis.
 (f) (a criterion for (H)) Write G = G_o + sum_l G_l with G_o = x eta E^(1/3) P(t, w). Then (G_o)_(x eta) =
     E^(1/3) Q_o(t, w) with an explicit linear combination Q_o of P, P_t, P_w, P_tt, P_tw, P_ww with coefficients
     elementary in (t, w) (Appendix A.29, (29.20)); the range of (t, w) is D intersected with {t > 0}, whose closure is the
     compact set D = {0 <= t, w <= 1, T(t)^6 + w^3 <= 1}, T(t) = (1 - e^(-alpha t))/(1 - e^(-alpha)); D does not depend on s; and
     (G_l)_(x eta) = E^(1/3) Z_l with an explicit combination Z_l of Q_l, (Q_l)_xi, (Q_l)_zeta, (Q_l)_(xi zeta) whose
     coefficients are bounded (Appendix A.29, (29.22)); define B_l = sup_(x,eta in R^2) |Z_l(x,eta)| < inf, with the compact variables evaluated at that same (x,eta). If Q_o >= delta_o on D and
     sum_l B_l < delta_o, then (H) holds with delta = delta_o - sum_l B_l. Both inequalities concern explicit functions on
     compact sets; if the input constants admit certified rational enclosures to arbitrary precision, finite interval
     subdivision can certify them when they hold with strict slack (certification at an exact minimum may require an
     additional analytic argument).
Consequently the fields satisfy every requirement of class A' (Section 2.3), with Theta_y(0) = a0/h, except (P1), and by
Proposition 27 (P1) fails on every neighbourhood of 0. Part (b) uses only that G is smooth, odd in x and in eta, with
G_(x eta) >= delta > 0 on R^2 (no factor E^(1/3)); in that generality it holds for every beta > 2 with the fields of
Proposition 23(b), DW(0) = diag(beta + 2, beta - 2), the linear flow (e^((beta+2) sigma) xi, e^((beta-2) sigma) eta) and
Theta_y(0) = a0/h. Relation to Proposition 23(c): that proposition assumes h = 1 and the two onto conditions and gives
canonicity only by uniqueness, under the additional hypothesis U = o(|X|); here h is arbitrary (a0 is the physical slope
only if h = 1), the onto conditions follow from (H), sublinearity and the polynomial bounds are proved, the subtracted
integral converges, and the uniqueness of the zero of W and the absence of periodic or bounded complete orbits are added.
Not asserted: (P1) (it fails, Proposition 27); error bounds for numerical quadrature of the integral in (d), for
numerical inversion of the chart or for fitting; leading or next-order asymptotic terms of the fields at infinity, or
their compatibility with the far-field results (Theorems 11, 12, 15 and 16); values of the constants C_n; an explicit
perturbation radius for (H) in the coefficients (a strict margin is stable under sufficiently small changes); that (H) holds for any given member without a certificate; that (H) is
necessary for any conclusion. Applied, via exact interval certificates of the chart margin, to particular numerical
states described in Section 6.9. Status: the underlying results are confirmed in the independent verification (independent derivation; exact symbolic
checks for the flow identities and the chart criterion; hand derivation and external review for the tail bounds and the
velocity integral); the extension of the tail bounds to several patches (A.29 Step 2), the two-sided rate in (e) and the
sentence on class A' are additions of this text, checked by the authors. This text: (a) to (e), the criterion in (f)
and A.29 Steps 1 to 8 confirmed by the independent verifier and by an external audit; the range statement in (f), the
extrema of the patch factors and the edge and input-enclosure treatment of the certificate recipe (Step 9) corrected as
they proposed; the corrected full text, including the recipe wording, confirmed by the independent verifier.

Proposition 29 (vertical compression of a hydrostatic profile; a caution on the normalized residuals). Let beta > 2 and
let Psi, Theta be smooth on R^2 with coordinates z = (x, eta), Psi odd in x and in eta, Theta even in x and odd in eta. Put
U = (-Psi_eta, Psi_x), W = (beta x + U1, beta eta + U2), H = -Psi_(eta eta), J = Psi_xx, Q = W.grad J + J, and assume the
hydrostatic profile equations
   W.grad H + H = Theta_x,   W.grad Theta = (beta - 2) Theta,   Theta_eta(0) = a0 != 0,   Psi_(x eta)(0) = -2.       (HS)
For lambda > 0 define at physical X = (x, y): Psi_l(x, y) = lambda^(-1) Psi(x, lambda y), Theta_l(x, y) = lambda Theta(x, lambda y),
U_l = (-d_y Psi_l, d_x Psi_l), Omega_l = -Delta Psi_l, W_l = beta X + U_l, and S_l z = (x, eta/lambda). Then:
 (a) R_Theta = 0 and E = 0 identically, d_x d_y Psi_l(0) = -2, d_y Theta_l(0) = a0_l := lambda^2 a0,
     Omega_l(S_l z) = lambda H(z) - lambda^(-1) J(z) and R_Omega(S_l z) = -lambda^(-1) Q(z).
 (b) H, J, Q are odd in x and in eta, Q/(x eta) extends smoothly to R^2, and at corresponding points
     R_Omega/(x y) = -Q/(x eta), independent of lambda. If Psi = -2 x eta + d1 x^3 eta + d2 x eta^3 + O(|z|^6), the
     extension equals -6 (2 beta + 1) d1 at the centre.
 (c) At S_l z, wherever the denominators are positive,
       |R_Omega|/N = lambda^(-2) |Q| / ||t - lambda^(-2) v||_1,   |R_Omega|/N2 = lambda^(-2) |Q| / ||h - lambda^(-2) j||_1,
     with t = (W1 H_x, W2 H_eta, H, Theta_x), v = (W1 J_x, W2 J_eta, J, 0), h = (U1 H_x, U2 H_eta, beta x H_x + beta eta H_eta
     + H, Theta_x), j = (U1 J_x, U2 J_eta, beta x J_x + beta eta J_eta + J, 0) evaluated at z. If K is compact,
     inf_K ||t||_1 >= n > 0 and M = sup_K ||v||_1, then for lambda^2 >= 2M/n the first ratio is at most
     2 sup_K |Q| / (n lambda^2) = 2 |a0| sup_K |Q| / (n |a0_l|) on S_l K; the second obeys the same bound with its own
     constants inf_K ||h||_1 > 0 and sup_K ||j||_1. Every component of t, v, h, j and Q vanishes on the axes, where the
     ratios are undefined; on compact sets meeting the axes, cancellation of the common factor |x eta| defines a continuous extension
     wherever its divided denominator is positive, and the same bounds hold for the divided vectors t/(x eta), v/(x eta), h/(x eta), j/(x eta) and
     Q/(x eta), with their own constants. These are upper bounds; a uniform two-sided rate needs a positive lower bound for |Q| on K, or for |Q/(x eta)| in the divided formulation.
 (d) R_Omega vanishes identically for one lambda if and only if Q vanishes identically, and then for every lambda. If
     moreover U = o(|X|) and |H| + |J| <= C (1 + |X|)^(-sigma) for some sigma > 0, then for each lambda, U_l is the
     canonical velocity of Omega_l (Section 2.3), and Q does not vanish identically, so no member satisfies (P1).
Under the genuine scaling of Section 2.4 (with factor mu) a0 and the normalized ratios at corresponding points are
unchanged, while R_Omega/(x y) at corresponding points is multiplied by mu^(-2); so the divided absolute residual
depends on the spatial scale. Not asserted: existence of a nontrivial profile satisfying (HS) and the hypotheses of
(d); any statement on families whose shape changes with lambda; inverse or tail bounds uniform in lambda; a two-sided rate without additional hypotheses;
nonexistence in the full admissible class A'. Status: the identities, estimates, sufficient canonical-inverse hypotheses,
scaling remark and nonvanishing argument have standalone analytic proofs. Exact symbolic checks cover algebraic
identities only. An external audit removed an unnecessary restriction sigma < 1, separated the normalizer
constants and proposed the nonvanishing observation. The independent verification checked that observation in a new
standalone proof and audited this corrected text; no hydrostatic base or endpoint is asserted.

Proposition 30 (the free-exponent family near the centre for every beta > 2, and under a global chart bound). For beta > 2
put b = beta - 2, p = 1/beta and m = beta/b, let alpha > 0, s > 0 and a0 != 0, put d = 1 - e^(-alpha), and for real
(x, eta) let
   E = x^2 + (1 + (eta/s)^6)^(m/3),   t = -log(1 - d E^(-p/2))/alpha,   w = (eta/s)^2 E^(-1/m),
   xi_l = x^2/(R_l^2 + x^2),   zeta_l = eta^2/(R_l^2 + eta^2),
   G = x eta E^p [ P(t, w) + sum_{l=1}^n exp(-(x^2 + eta^2)/L_l^2) Q_l(xi_l, zeta_l) ],
where n >= 0, P and Q_1, ..., Q_n are real polynomials in two variables and R_l, L_l > 0. (At beta = 3 these are the
formulas of Proposition 27; the free-exponent family of Section 6.9 with M = 3 is the subfamily alpha = 3, s = s_e without
patches, and adding the core functions of Proposition 27 stays in the family.) Put h := G_(x eta)(0, 0) = P(1, 0) + sum_l Q_l(0, 0).
 (a) Let beta be 5/2 or 8/3 (so m = 5 or m = 4) and assume h > 0. Then (x, eta) -> (x, G_x) has a real analytic inverse
     eta(x, y) near 0, and the fields of Proposition 23(b),
        Theta = a0 eta,  Psi = beta x G_x + b eta G_eta - 2 beta G,  U = (-Psi_y, Psi_x),  Omega = -Lap Psi,  W = beta X + U,
     are real analytic on a neighbourhood of 0, have the A1 parities, Psi_xy(0) = -2 and Theta_y(0) = a0/h, and satisfy
     (P2) and (P3) there; but they do not satisfy (P1) on any neighbourhood of 0: the residual
     W.grad Omega + Omega - Theta_x is not identically zero on any neighbourhood of X = 0. No global chart, tail bound or
     velocity inverse is assumed.
 (b) Let 5/2 <= beta <= 7/2 and assume that for a constant kappa > 0
        A := G_(x eta)(x, eta) >= kappa E^p   for every (x, eta) in R^2.
     Then the fields of Proposition 23(b), defined on R^2 through the global inverse of (x, eta) -> (x, G_x), do not
     satisfy (P1) on R^2. Hence no member of this family with such a global chart bound is an exact profile of class A',
     for any beta in [5/2, 7/2].
 (c) Let beta > 2. If m = beta/(beta - 2) is an integer other than 3, that is beta = 2m/(m - 1) with m = 2 or an integer
     m >= 4 (beta = 4, 8/3, 5/2, 12/5, 7/3, ...), and h > 0, the conclusion of (a) holds: the fields do not satisfy (P1) on
     any neighbourhood of 0 (for m = 4 and 5 this is (a); for m = 3, that is beta = 3, see Proposition 27). Assume that
     A >= kappa E^p on R^2 for a constant kappa > 0, as in (b) but now for any beta > 2. Then the fields of Proposition
     23(b), defined on R^2 through the global inverse of (x, eta) -> (x, G_x), do not satisfy (P1) on R^2. Hence no member of this family with such a global chart
     bound is an exact profile of class A', for any beta > 2; part (b) is the case beta in [5/2, 7/2].
 (d) Let beta > 2 be arbitrary (m = beta/(beta - 2) need not be an integer, and beta need not be rational) and assume
     h > 0. Then the conclusion of (a) holds: the fields do not satisfy (P1) on any neighbourhood of 0. In particular the
     global assertion of (c) also follows from (d), without Steps 10 and 11 of A.31: under A >= kappa E^p on R^2,
     h = A(0, 0) >= kappa > 0 (E(0, 0) = 1), and fields satisfying (P1) on R^2 satisfy it near 0, where they coincide
     with the fields defined through the local inverse (uniqueness in the implicit function theorem).
