Proposition 31 (conditional obstructions for large-beta asymptotic families). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a family of
smooth solutions of (P) with the A1 parity and Theta_y(0) = a0 != 0, indexed by a sequence beta -> oo, with
a0 = a0(beta) allowed to depend on beta; by (P2) at the centre, Psi = -2xy + O(|X|^4) (Section 2.4). Put eps = 1/beta,
X = r (cos phi, sin phi), s = (ln r)/beta and
   Theta = r theta(s, phi),   Psi = r^2 psi(s, phi),   Omega = omega(s, phi)
(the dependence on beta is not written), eta = theta/a0, and let p_beta(s) be the coefficient of sin 2phi in
psi(s, .). Then, exactly,
   (T) theta_s + 2 theta + 2 psi theta_phi - psi_phi theta + eps (psi_s theta_phi - psi_phi theta_s) = 0,
   (V) omega_s + omega + 2 psi omega_phi + eps (psi_s omega_phi - psi_phi omega_s) = B theta + eps cos phi theta_s,
   (E) omega = -(4 psi + psi_phiphi) - 4 eps psi_s - eps^2 psi_ss,
where B f := cos phi f - sin phi f_phi. The pure strain Theta = a0 y, Psi = -2xy, Omega = 0 (theta = a0 sin phi,
psi = -sin 2phi, omega = 0) solves (P) for every beta and violates U = o(|X|). For each member p_beta(s) -> -1 as
s -> -oo (centre jet), and p_beta(s) -> 0 as s -> +oo if U = o(|X|) uniformly (then |Psi| = o(r^2)); the scaling
Theta -> lambda Theta(X/lambda), Psi -> lambda^2 Psi(X/lambda), Omega -> Omega(X/lambda) maps solutions to solutions
with the same a0 and translates s by (ln lambda)/beta. Hence each member with U = o(|X|) uniformly (in particular each
member of class A') can be scaled to p_beta(0) = -1/2 (the normalized scale); this translation depends on beta and need
not preserve a given limit or expansion, so in the consequence below the hypotheses are imposed on the normalized
fields. Below, T = R/(2 pi Z), Q1 removes the sin phi Fourier coefficient, and convergence and expansions
are required in C^2(J x T) for every compact interval J of R.
 (a) Suppose theta = theta_0 + eps theta_1 + o(eps), psi = psi_0 + eps psi_1 + o(eps), omega = omega_0 + eps omega_1
     + o(eps), with coefficients of class C^2 having the A1 parities, and that at some s1
        theta_0 = a* sin phi (a* != 0),   psi_0 = -sin 2phi,   omega_0 = 0,   Q1 theta_1 = 0,   omega_1 = 0   at s = s1.
     Then theta_0 = a* sin phi, psi_0 = -sin 2phi, omega_0 = 0, Q1 theta_1 = 0 and omega_1 = 0 on R x T, and
     theta_1 = t(s) sin phi, psi_1 = q(s) sin 2phi with t' + 2 a* q = 0. In particular p_beta -> -1 locally uniformly
     on R.
 (b) Suppose liminf |a0(beta)|/beta > 0 and eta -> eta_0, psi -> psi_0, omega -> omega_0, with eta_0 not identically
     zero. Then eta_0 = alpha sin phi with a constant alpha != 0, psi_0 = -sin 2phi and omega_0 = 0 on R x T. In
     particular p_beta -> -1 locally uniformly on R.
 (c) Suppose |a0(beta)| -> oo and eta = eta_0 + eps eta_1 + o(eps), psi = psi_0 + o(1), omega = omega_0 + o(1), with
     eta_0, eta_1, psi_0, omega_0 of class C^2 and eta_0 not identically zero. Then the conclusion of (b) holds.
 (d) (Finite beta, by compactness.) For every Lambda >= 1 there is beta_0(Lambda) > 2 such that, for beta >
     beta_0(Lambda), no smooth solution of (P) with the A1 parity, a0 != 0 and p_beta(0) = -1/2 satisfies all of
       (d1) |a0| >= beta/Lambda,
       (d2) ||eta||_(C^3(Q)) + ||psi||_(C^3(Q)) + ||omega||_(C^3(Q)) <= Lambda,
       (d3) max over [-1, 1] x T of |eta| >= 1/Lambda,
     where Q = [-2, 2] x T, the norms are taken in the variables (s, phi), and ||f||_(C^3(Q)) is the sum of the
     suprema over Q of the derivatives of f of order at most 3. Since d_s = beta r d_r, (d2) bounds the sum of the
     suprema of beta^j |(r d_r)^j d_phi^l f| (j + l <= 3) for f = Theta/(a0 r), Psi/r^2 and Omega on
     e^(-2 beta) <= r <= e^(2 beta). Every single solution satisfies (d1) and (d2) for some Lambda depending on it,
     and (d3) as well unless eta vanishes on [-1, 1] x T, an exception that does not occur for profiles with beta > 2
     (end of A.32); (d) says that no Lambda serves for all beta above
     beta_0(Lambda). Hence, for beta > beta_0(Lambda), every member of class A' violates (d1), (d2) or (d3) in its
     normalized scale. beta_0(Lambda) is not explicit, and it may be enlarged at will. No analogous statement is
     derived from (a) or (c): at leading order the system of (a) leaves p free, and the bounds of (d2) alone do not
     control the first-order hypothesis used in the argument of (c).
Consequently, no family whose normalized fields satisfy the hypotheses of (a), of (b) or of (c) exists. A
sufficient condition for the data of (a) with a* = a0 when a0 is independent of beta: in the normalized scale, for
some s_* > s1, both fixed independently of beta, and radii rho_beta >= e^(beta s_*),
|Theta - a0 y| <= C r^3/rho_beta^2, |Psi + 2xy| <= C r^4/rho_beta^2 and |Omega| <= C r^2/rho_beta^2 for r <= rho_beta,
with the same bounds for (r d_r)^j d_phi^l of the three remainders and constants C = C(j, l) independent of beta.
In (b) the obstruction is an exact identity on the x-axis: (B f)_phi = -sin phi (f + f_phiphi) vanishes at phi = 0, so
the phi-derivative of (V) at phi = 0 equals eps a0 eta_(s phi)(s, 0), and the limit then forces alpha' = 0. In (c) a
non-zero alpha'(s) would force the first temperature correction to contain alpha'(s) sin phi ln|sin phi|, which is not
C^1 at the x-axis, so angular C^1 regularity forces alpha' = 0 and hence p = -1 (a C^0 expansion is not excluded by
this: a hydrostatic temperature F(y) = a0 y alpha(ln|y|/beta), with alpha smooth and such that F is smooth (for example
alpha constant for all sufficiently negative arguments, or alpha(s) = 1 + exp(-e^(-s)), which is not constant on any
half-line), has eta = sin phi alpha(s + eps ln|sin phi|), whose first correction eps alpha'(s) sin phi ln|sin phi| is
not C^1 at phi = 0 where alpha' != 0). Not asserted: anything at a finite beta other than (d) (beta_0 is not explicit,
and no common Lambda along a family of solutions is derived from (P)), in particular nothing at beta = 3; nonexistence
in Setting A1 or in class A' (the expansions, the limits and the data of (a) are hypotheses on hypothetical families,
not derived from (P), the A1 parity, the canonical inverse or bounds on a0); that alpha = 1 in (b) or (c) (the limit
s -> -oo of each member and the limit beta -> oo are not interchanged); uniqueness for bounded a0 when only the limits
of the fields as s -> -oo are known; anything for amplitudes with a0/beta -> 0 without the expansion of (c), for
normalized temperatures tending to 0, or for families without such limits or expansions, for example transitions over
s-widths tending to 0 (the free even-degree centre coefficients of Proposition 26 enter psi through e^(2 k beta s),
k >= 1, times angular functions), angular layers, |U|/r of order beta or larger, or structures that escape every compact
s-interval as beta -> oo; any selection of beta. Parts (a) and (b) were first formulated and proved by the independent
verifier while checking earlier drafts by the authors (for (a) first with data propagated to s >= s1; the extension to
all s and to C^2 coefficients was observed in an external audit and then proved independently by the verifier), which
contained a hypothesis set that is inconsistent by continuity and an invalid uniqueness argument (Appendix B).
The independent verification confirmed (a) in this two-sided C^2 form, (b) and (c), each with
its own complete proof (closed 2026-10-21 at 16:31Z and 17:20Z for (a), 16:43Z for (b), 17:20Z for (c); Appendix B);
its finite symbolic checks are consistency checks of the algebra, not part of the proofs.
Part (d) and Step 11 were confirmed by the independent verification with its own complete proof (closed 2026-10-21
at 18:29Z; Appendix B), after an external audit of an earlier draft; neither gives an explicit beta_0, a Lambda common
to a family of solutions, or anything at beta = 3.

Proposition 32 (rough separated modes at the pure strain; linear level). Linearize the closed order-1 system of A.32
Step 4 (the deviation (v, w, p, a) on the leading harmonic branch) at the pure strain p = -1, a = a* > 0, v = w = 0,
and put S = sqrt(9 + 4a*). A separated solution has v = e^(lam s) f(phi), w = e^(lam s) g(phi),
psi_1 = e^(lam s) h(phi), p = -1 + P e^(lam s) and a = a* + A e^(lam s), with lam A = -2 a* P. It is reduced by
f = sin phi F(z), g = sin 2phi G(z), h = sin 2phi H(z), z = sin^2 phi, to a regular singular linear system (*) for
Y = (F', G, H', P) (A.33); the fundamental and kernel directions of the unprojected system are invisible in Y.
 (i) For every real lam with 0 < lam < (S - 1)/2, the solutions Y of (*) with f in H^1, g in L^2 and h in H^2 form a
   one-dimensional space, and every non-zero one has P != 0.
 (ii) Let k >= 2 be an integer with a* > 64k^2 + 24k. For every real lam with 4k - 1 < lam < (S - 8k - 5)/2, the
   solutions Y of (*) with f, g in C^k and h in C^(k+2) form a one-dimensional space, and every non-zero one has
   P != 0.
 (iii) For no real lam does a non-zero solution Y of (*) give f, g, h in C^oo.
 (iv) Every non-zero solution in (i) or (ii) admits angular reconstructions with Q1 f = f and h = K g + q sin 2phi,
   where q can be chosen so that the unprojected order-1 angular equations hold exactly; with A = -2 a* P/lam it is a
   separated solution of the closed linearized system and of its unprojected lift, P and A are non-zero, the
   perturbation (v, w, psi_1, p + 1, a - a*) tends to 0 in the stated norms as s -> -oo, and it is non-zero at every
   finite s. More generally the full order-1 temperature
   coefficient is f + t sin phi with lam t + 2 a* q + c0 = 0, where c0 is a constant determined by f, g and P (A.33).
Reading. Proposition 31(a) uses zero deviation data at one finite slow position s1. At the linear level, Proposition 32
shows that convergence to the pure strain as s -> -oo cannot replace these data: in the energy class in which the
estimate of A.32 works there are non-zero separated deviations for every a* > 0, and in C^k coefficients (k >= 2)
whenever a* > 64k^2 + 24k, that is k < (S - 3)/16; they tend to 0 as s -> -oo and change the strain (P != 0). This is a
range of counterexamples to a linear argument, not a regularity threshold above which rigidity holds: no fixed C^k
class excludes these modes for all a* > 0, while smoothness excludes every non-zero reduced separated mode, and no
optimal threshold is established. The modes are compatible with Proposition 31(a): an inequality |Z'| <= C Z permits
non-zero exponentials that decay as s -> -oo.
Not asserted: non-linear ancient solutions or a non-linear unstable manifold; failure of uniqueness from zero deviation
data at a finite position (excluded by Proposition 31(a)); perturbations bounded on the whole s-line (the modes grow as
s -> +oo); an optimal regularity threshold or a complete spectral description; anything about C^2 modes for
a* <= 304; that the energy modes are C^2 expansion coefficients in the sense of Proposition 31; absence of smooth
solutions of the full unprojected system (the fundamental and kernel directions f = t sin phi,
h = -(lam t/(2a*)) sin 2phi, g = P = A = 0 are smooth and invisible in Y); anything at finite beta; any NO statement for
Setting A1.
Status: proved by the authors after two external audits of earlier drafts (commissioned by the authors), which
supplied part (i), the proof that P != 0 and the argument of part (iii), and corrected the endpoint discussion and the
lift; confirmed by the independent verification with its own complete proof (closed 2026-10-21 at 18:29Z; Appendix B).
The numerical matching computations of A.33 are consistency checks, not part of the proof, and were not reproduced
independently.

Proposition 33 (vorticity slope on the horizontal axis). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in class A' and put
a = beta + 2, V(x) = W1(x, 0), tau(x) = Theta_y(x, 0) and w(x) = Omega_y(x, 0) for real x. Suppose that V has no
positive zero (x1 = inf in Proposition 25; equivalently V > 0 on (0, inf); this holds in particular when the origin is
the only zero of W). For x > 0 put
   xi(x) = x exp( int_0^x (a/V(u) - 1/u) du ),    E(x) = xi(x)^((1 + 2 beta)/a) / V(x).
 (a) xi is smooth and positive on (0, inf) with xi' = a xi/V, xi(x) = x (1 + O(x^2)) as x -> 0+ and
     xi(x) = C_xi x^(1 + 2 delta) (1 + o(1)) as x -> inf for a constant C_xi > 0. On (0, inf), tau = a0 V/(a xi) and
     tau' = (a0/a) (V' - a)/xi, and F'(0) = lim_{x -> inf} x^(2 delta) tau(x) = a0 beta/(a C_xi).
 (b) V w' + (1 + 2 beta - V') w = tau' on R, and w(x) = E(x)^(-1) int_0^x E(u) tau'(u)/V(u) du for x > 0.
 (c) x^(1 + delta) w(x) -> A'(0) as x -> inf, and
        A'(0) = (a0/(a c_E)) int_0^inf xi(x)^((beta - 1)/a) (V'(x) - a) V(x)^(-2) dx,
     with c_E = C_xi^((1 + 2 beta)/a)/beta > 0 and an absolutely convergent integral; here
     V' - a = U1_x(x, 0) - 2 = U1_x(x, 0) - U1_x(0, 0).
 (d) If V' <= a on (0, inf) (equivalently U1_x(x, 0) <= 2 for all x > 0; equivalently a0 tau' <= 0 on (0, inf), that
     is, tau is monotone in the non-strict sense on [0, inf); this holds in particular if V(x)/x is nonincreasing), then
     sign A'(0) = -sign a0, so branch (i) of Theorem 12 holds, and there are R0 > 0 and 0 < phi0 < pi/2 with
     a0 Omega < 0 on the sector {r > R0, 0 < phi < phi0}.
 (e) In branch (ii) of Theorem 12, V' - a and tau' take both signs on (0, inf); in particular U1_x(x, 0) > 2 for some
     x > 0, and tau is not monotone on [0, inf).
Reading. Along a horizontal axis without stagnation points other than the origin, the leading far-field vorticity
slope A'(0) is a weighted integral, with positive weight, of the excess U1_x(x, 0) - U1_x(0, 0) of the axis strain
over its centre value. Since this excess tends to -2, branch (ii) of Theorem 12 (A = 0) requires the axis strain to
exceed its centre value somewhere. The proposition gives a necessary condition for branch (ii) and a sufficient
condition for branch (i); it decides neither. The two axis equations of (a) and (b), the centre data and the sublinear
tails alone do not exclude branch (ii): for every beta > 2 there are smooth axis functions with these properties for
which the integral in (c) vanishes (A.34, constructed by the independent verification); no extension of such axis
data to a solution in the plane is claimed.
Not asserted: that V has no positive zero for a sought profile (the hypothesis does not exclude zeros of W off the
horizontal axis); any sign of V' - a for a sought profile; any conclusion on the vertical axis (differentiating (P1)
there brings in Theta_xx(0, y), which the vertical-axis transport equation does not supply, so the argument does not
apply directly; Proposition 34 treats the vertical axis through a coupled linear system for Theta_xx(0, y) and
Omega_x(0, y)); existence or nonexistence for beta > 2.
Status: proved by the authors after an external audit (commissioned by the authors), which found (a) to (e) proved and
corrected the wording of (d), of the vertical-axis remark and of the numerical commentary; confirmed by the
independent verification with its own proof (closed 2026-10-21 at 20:22Z; Appendix B). The numerical model checks in
A.34 are consistency checks of the algebra, not part of the proof; the authors' runs were not executed independently.

Proposition 34 (vorticity slope on the vertical axis). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in class A' and put
b = beta - 2, D = 2 (beta + 2)(2 beta + 1) (the constant of Proposition 17; D = 70 at beta = 3) and, for real y,
   Y(y) = W2(0, y) = beta y + U2(0, y),  T(y) = Theta(0, y),  s(y) = Theta_xx(0, y),  z(y) = Omega_x(0, y).
 (a) Y > 0 on (0, inf), and a0 T' > 0 on [0, inf). On R,
        Y T' = b T,
        Y s' + (3 beta + 2 - 2 Y') s = T' (z + Y''),
        Y z' + (1 + 2 beta - Y') z = s,
     and z + Y'' = -U2_xx(0, y).
 (b) Write Y = b y + Y3 y^3 + O(y^5), s = s1 y + O(y^3), z = z1 y + O(y^3). Then s1 = (2 beta + 1) z1 and
     (D - a0) z1 = 6 a0 Y3. More generally, for n >= 1 the coefficients of y^(2n-1) in (s, z) solve a linear system with
     matrix [[2nb + 8, -a0], [-1, 2nb + 5]] whose right side is fixed by a0, the lower coefficients of s and z and the
     coefficients of Y through y^(2n+1). The determinant vanishes when a0 = (2nb + 8)(2nb + 5), the number appearing as
     the sufficient bound [2n(beta - 2) + 8][2n(beta - 2) + 5] in Proposition 17. This is a singularity of the displayed
     axis coefficient system with Y prescribed; no exceptional amplitude for the full centre-jet problem is asserted.
 (c) Put eta(y) = y exp( int_0^y (b/Y(u) - 1/u) du ) and E_v(y) = eta(y)^((1 + 2 beta)/b) / Y(y) for y > 0. Then
     T = a0 eta, eta(y) = C_eta y^(1 - 2 delta) (1 + o(1)) and E_v(y) = c_v y^(1 + delta) (1 + o(1)) as y -> inf with
     C_eta > 0 and c_v = C_eta^((1 + 2 beta)/b)/beta, (E_v z)' = E_v s/Y on (0, inf), and
        y^(1 + delta) z(y) -> -A'(pi/2),   A'(pi/2) = -(1/c_v) int_0^inf E_v(y) s(y) Y(y)^(-1) dy,
     with an absolutely convergent integral.
 (d) s is not identically zero on (0, inf). If a0 s >= 0 on (0, inf), then a0 z >= 0 on (0, inf), a0 z > 0 on (y_s, inf)
     where y_s = inf {y > 0 : s(y) != 0}, a0 A'(pi/2) < 0, branch (i) of Theorem 12 holds, and there are R0 > 0 and
     0 < phi0 < pi/2 with a0 Omega > 0 on the sector {r > R0, pi/2 - phi0 < phi < pi/2}.
 (e) The hypothesis a0 s >= 0 of (d) holds in each of the following cases:
     (H1) 0 < a0 < D and U2_yy(0, y) >= 0 for all y > 0 (Y convex on [0, inf)); then s >= 0 and z >= 0 on (0, inf);
     (H2) U2_xx(0, y) <= 0 for all y > 0 (either sign of a0).
 (f) Consequently, if a0 > 0 and (H1) or (H2) holds, Omega <= 0 on Q1 is impossible, and with Proposition 6 Omega takes
     both signs on Q1. If in addition V(x) = W1(x, 0) > 0 and V'(x) <= beta + 2 for all x > 0 (Proposition 33(d)), then
     A'(0) and A'(pi/2) both have the sign of -a0, so A takes both signs on (0, pi/2), and there is R1 such that Omega
     takes both signs on Q1 intersected with every circle |X| = R > R1.
Reading. For a prescribed vertical-axis velocity Y, the transverse traces Theta_xx(0, y) and Omega_x(0, y) satisfy the
linear system of (a), and the far-field vorticity slope A'(pi/2) at the vertical axis is minus a positive-weight
integral of Theta_xx(0, y) (c). The condition a0 Theta_xx(0, y) >= 0 on (0, inf) gives branch (i) of Theorem 12 and,
for a0 > 0, excludes Omega <= 0 on Q1; (H1) and (H2) are two sufficient conditions for it, stated on traces of the
unknown profile. Conversely, in branch (ii) of Theorem 12 the integral in (c) vanishes and s is not identically zero,
so Theta_xx(0, y) takes both signs on (0, inf) and neither (H1) nor (H2) holds.
The bound a0 < D in (H1) is the condition mu_+ < b of the proof; for a0 > D and Y3 > 0 the order-one relation of (b)
gives s1, z1 < 0, a conditional local obstruction to extending the convexity criterion (A.35, Remark 1). For the
stored numerical state 62df5606, which is not a profile, the exact centre coefficients give a0 > D, and
U2_xx(0, y) > 0 and a0 Theta_xx(0, y) < 0 on some interval (0, epsilon) with no certified radius (A.35, Remark 3), so
neither sufficient condition holds for it.
Not asserted: a scalar equation for Theta_xx(0, y) independent of Omega_x(0, y) (the vertical temperature equation
alone does not supply these traces; for prescribed Y they satisfy the coupled linear system of (a), with
-U2_xx = z + Y''); any definite-sign or branch conclusion when a0 s changes sign on (0, inf) (the equations and the
formula of (c) remain valid); that a sought profile satisfies a0 s >= 0, (H1) or (H2); a selection of beta; existence
or nonexistence for beta > 2. The proposition gives no endpoint.
Status: proved by the authors after an external audit (commissioned by the authors), which found (a) to (d) and (f)
proved and (e) proved with minor repairs of the proof that do not change the statement, and corrected the wording of
(b), of the remarks and of the numerical commentary; confirmed by the independent verification with its own proof
(closed 2026-10-21 at 21:15Z; Appendix B), whose corrections of the Reading and of Remark 3 in A.35 are incorporated.
The numerical model checks in A.35 are consistency checks of the algebra, not part of the proof; the authors' runs
were not executed independently.

Proposition 35 (nonpositive vorticity on the first quadrant: necessary conditions). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a
profile in class A' (so beta > 2 by Corollary 4), and use the notation of Propositions 33 and 34 (V, tau, w, xi, E on
the horizontal axis; Y, T, s, z, eta, E_v on the vertical axis) and of Theorems 11 and 15 (F, A, H,
gamma = 1 - 2 delta, d = 2 - delta). Put L = pi/2, C(y) = U2_xx(0, y), h = (beta + 1)/b and, for 0 < u < R <= inf,
   P(u) = eta(u)^(4 beta/b) Y(u)^(-4),   K_R(u) = P(u) int_u^R eta(t)^(-h) dt,   J_R = int_0^R K_R(u) C(u) du.
 (a) For every such profile (either sign of a0, no sign assumption on Omega) and every y > 0, K_y > 0 on (0, y), the
     integrals converge absolutely, and
        E_v(y) z(y) = -a0 b J_y,   A'(pi/2) = (a0 b/c_v) J_inf,
     where c_v is the constant of Proposition 34(c). Moreover, with w(x) = Omega_y(x, 0) and an absolutely convergent
     integral,
        int_0^inf (1 - 2 U1_x(x, 0)) w(x) dx = -a0.
Suppose in addition that a0 > 0 and Omega <= 0 on Q1. Then:
 (b) Psi < 0 on Q1, Psi_y(x, 0) < 0 and Psi_x(0, y) < 0 for x, y > 0; hence V(x) > beta x and 0 < Y(y) < beta y for
     x, y > 0, and the hypothesis of Proposition 33 (V > 0 on (0, inf)) holds.
 (c) A <= 0 on [0, pi/2], A is not identically zero (branch (i) of Theorem 12), and A'(0) < 0 <= A'(pi/2); the
     integral in Proposition 33(c) is strictly negative. The function q(x) = -Omega_y(x, 0) is nonnegative, not
     identically zero and integrable on (0, inf), and the q-weighted mean of the horizontal axis strain is int_0^inf
     U1_x(x, 0) q dx / int_0^inf q dx = 1/2 - a0/(2 int_0^inf q dx) < 1/2 (while U1_x(0, 0) = 2).
 (d) J_y >= 0 for every y > 0 and J_inf >= 0, with J_y > 0 for some y; in particular, if J_y < 0 for some y > 0, then
     Omega > 0 somewhere on Q1.
 (e) Theta_xx(0, y) < 0 for some y > 0, and Omega_x(0, y) < 0 at every such y; U2_xx(0, y) > 0 for some y > 0.
 (f) H'(pi/2) > 0 and U2_yy(0, y) = delta (1 - delta) H'(pi/2) y^(-1 - delta) + o(y^(-1 - delta)) as y -> inf, so Y is
     strictly convex on (y1, inf) for some y1. The centre coefficient Y3 of Proposition 34(b) satisfies Y3 <= 0 if
     a0 < D, Y3 = 0 if a0 = D and Y3 >= 0 if a0 > D. If 0 < a0 < D, then U2_yy(0, y) < 0 for some y > 0, so Y changes
     convexity on (0, inf).
 (g) Omega_x(0, y) < 0 and J_y > 0 for all sufficiently large y. If A'(pi/2) = 0, then sigma = F''(pi/2) + gamma
     F(pi/2) > 0, y^(1 + 2 delta) Theta_xx(0, y) -> sigma and y^(1 + 2 delta) Omega_x(0, y) -> -sigma as y -> inf; so
     Theta_xx(0, .) changes sign on (0, inf), and for every sufficiently large y, Theta_x(x, y) > 0 for all small
     x > 0 and Theta_x(x, y) < 0 for some x > 0. If A'(pi/2) < delta (1 - delta) H'(pi/2), then U2_xx(0, .) changes
     sign on (0, inf).
 (h) If Omega_xy(0, 0) = 0, then Theta = a0 y + O(|X|^5), Psi = -2 x y + O(|X|^6) and
     Omega = G1 x^3 y + G2 x y^3 + O(|X|^6) with G1 <= 0 and G2 <= 0; if moreover G1 and G2 are not both zero, then
     a0 >= 4 (beta + 2)(4 beta + 5) (= 340 at beta = 3).
Reading. On the vertical axis the vorticity slope Omega_x(0, y) is -a0 b/E_v(y) times a positive-kernel integral of
the transverse curvature U2_xx(0, u) of the vertical velocity over 0 < u < y (a); since U2_xx(0, u) = -Omega_x(0, u) -
U2_yy(0, u), this is an identity on the unknown profile, not a condition on prescribed data. Proposition 6 excludes
Omega >= 0 on Q1; the opposite one-signed class Omega <= 0 with a0 > 0 is not excluded here. It forces a nonpositive
stream function, components W1(x, 0) > beta x and 0 < W2(0, y) < beta y of the transport field on the two axes
(equivalently U1(x, 0) > 0 and U2(0, y) < 0), branch (i) with a strictly negative far-field slope at the horizontal
axis, negative values of Theta_xx on the positive vertical axis, and eventual strict convexity of the vertical axis
velocity, which for a0 < D must be preceded by a concave interval.
At a degenerate centre (Omega_xy(0, 0) = 0) a nonzero quartic part of Omega requires a0 >= 4 (beta + 2)(4 beta + 5)
(h). The angular sign conditions listed in (b), (c), (f) and (g) admit explicit data for which the two-term far-field
vorticity is negative throughout Q1 at sufficiently large radii (A.36, Remark 2); these data are not matched to a
centre or to a profile. (H2) of Proposition 34 is the case C <= 0 of (d).
Not asserted: that Omega <= 0 on Q1 is possible or impossible for a profile; any sign of J_y for a sought profile
without the additional assumption Omega <= 0 on Q1; positive values of Theta_xx(0, y) unless A'(pi/2) = 0; that the
strict inequality A'(pi/2) > 0 holds; that a0 > D or a0 < D for a sought profile; any restriction on a0 when
Omega_xy(0, 0) = 0 and the quartic part of Omega vanishes; existence or nonexistence for beta > 2. The vertical-axis
relations alone do not exclude Omega_x(0, y) < 0 with Y convex at a0 = D (A.36, Remark 1).
Status: proved by the authors after external consultations (commissioned by the authors). The first checked the
authors' arguments for (b) and (c), strengthened (c) to A'(0) < 0 and supplied (a) (first identity), (d) to (f) and
Remark 1 of A.36; an external audit found these parts proved, supplied (g) (first and last sentences) and corrected
the wording; a second consultation supplied the second identity of (a), the last sentence of (c), the limits and the
sign change of Theta_x in (g), part (h) and Remark 2, which the authors checked; a further external audit found (a) to
(h) and both remarks correct and supplied wording and notation clarifications, which are incorporated. The independent
verification confirmed the second draft (parts (a) to (g) and Remark 1) and, separately, the additions of the later
drafts (the second identity of (a), the last sentence of (c), the limits and the sign change of Theta_x in (g), part
(h) and Remark 2), each with its own proof; at its request the sixth draft restricts the scope of Remark 2 to the
displayed angular signs. The symbolic checks mentioned in A.36 are consistency checks, not part of the proof.

Proposition 36 (nonpositive vorticity on the first quadrant with a0 < 0: necessary conditions). Let
(beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in class A' (so beta > 2 by Corollary 4) with a0 < 0, and use the notation of
Propositions 33, 34 and 35 (V, tau, w, xi, E, C_xi, c_E on the horizontal axis; Y, T, s, z, eta, E_v, c_v on the
vertical axis; L = pi/2, C(y) = U2_xx(0, y), P, K_R and J_R) and of Theorems 11 and 15 (F, A, H, B,
gamma = 1 - 2 delta). Suppose that Omega <= 0 on Q1. Then:
 (a) Psi < 0 on Q1, V(x) > beta x and 0 < Y(y) < beta y for x, y > 0 (so the hypothesis of Proposition 33 holds),
     T < 0 and T' < 0 on (0, inf), A <= 0 on [0, pi/2] and A'(0) <= 0 <= A'(pi/2).
 (b) The integral I(x) = int_0^x E(u) tau'(u)/V(u) du of Proposition 33(b) satisfies I(x) <= 0 for every x > 0.
     Consequently U1_x(x, 0) > 2 for some x > 0; Theta_xy(x, 0) > 0 and Omega_y(x, 0) < 0 for every sufficiently large
     x; and A'(0) = I(inf)/c_E <= 0, with x^(1 + 2 delta) Omega_y(x, 0) -> 2 delta F'(0) < 0 as x -> inf if A'(0) = 0.
     The function q(x) = -Omega_y(x, 0) is nonnegative, not identically zero and integrable on (0, inf), and int_0^inf
     U1_x(x, 0) q dx / int_0^inf q dx = 1/2 - a0/(2 int_0^inf q dx) > 1/2.
 (c) J_y <= 0 for every y > 0 and J_inf <= 0, with J_y0 < 0 for some y0 > 0, so U2_xx(0, y) < 0 for some y in (0, y0).
     Theta_xx(0, y) < 0 for some y > 0, and Omega_x(0, y) < 0 at every such y. If A'(pi/2) = 0, then Theta_xx(0, .)
     and U2_xx(0, .) take both signs on (0, inf), sigma = F''(pi/2) + gamma F(pi/2) >= 0, and y^(1 + 2 delta)
     Theta_xx(0, y) -> sigma and y^(1 + 2 delta) Omega_x(0, y) -> -sigma as y -> inf.
 (d) g = Omega_xy(0, 0) <= 0. If g < 0, then Psi = -2 x y + d1 x^3 y + d2 x y^3 + O(|X|^6) with d1 = -D g/(6 a0) < 0
     and d2 = (D - a0) g/(6 a0) > 0 (D = 2 (beta + 2)(2 beta + 1)), so U1_x(x, 0) = 2 - 3 d1 x^2 + O(x^4) > 2 and
     U2_xx(0, y) = 6 d1 y + O(y^3) < 0 for small x, y > 0, and the coefficient Y3 of Proposition 34(b) equals d2 > 0.
     If g = 0, then Omega = O(|X|^6), Theta = a0 y + O(|X|^7) and Psi = -2 x y + O(|X|^8).
 (e) In branch (ii) of Theorem 12 (A = 0), B = sin(phi) F' - gamma cos(phi) F <= 0 on [0, pi/2], F < 0 on (0, pi/2],
     Theta < 0 on the upper half-plane {y > 0}, and the backward basin of the origin is R^2 (Proposition 24(a)).
 (f) With rho = -Omega on Q1, int_Q1 Theta_x rho^(m - 1) dx dy = -(1 - 2 beta/m) int_Q1 rho^m dx dy < 0 for every
     m > 2 beta, and int_Q1 Theta_x rho^(2 beta - 1) dx dy = -(1/2) int_0^(pi/2) |A(phi)|^(2 beta) d phi; in
     particular Theta_x < 0 at some point of Q1 where Omega < 0, although int_0^inf Theta_x(x, y) dx = -T(y) > 0 for
     every y > 0.
Reading. Proposition 6 excludes Omega >= 0 on Q1 and Proposition 35 lists necessary conditions for Omega <= 0 on Q1
when a0 > 0; this proposition treats Omega <= 0 on Q1 when a0 < 0, where the buoyancy source Theta_x of (P1) has
positive integral along every horizontal line in Q1. The class is not excluded here. As for a0 > 0 the stream function
is negative on Q1 and W1(x, 0) > beta x, 0 < W2(0, y) < beta y on the axes, but the sign of J_y is reversed (J_y <= 0,
so U2_xx(0, .) < 0 somewhere; the signs forced on Theta_xx(0, .) and Omega_x(0, .) are those of Proposition 35), the
horizontal axis strain U1_x(x, 0) must exceed its centre value 2 somewhere (which a nondegenerate centre already
provides near the origin, (d)), and its q-weighted mean exceeds 1/2. At a degenerate centre the quartic part of Omega
vanishes for every a0 < 0 (compare Proposition 35(h)). Branch (ii) is not excluded; in it the temperature is negative
on the whole upper half-plane, so the backward basin of the origin is the whole plane. The two weighted identities of
(f), and the existence of a point of Q1 with Theta_x < 0 and Omega < 0, are stated, and were independently verified,
under a0 < 0; the proof (A.37, Step 6) uses the sign of a0 only for the positivity of the horizontal-line integral, so
they also hold for either sign of a0 (with Omega <= 0 on Q1), an extension stated by the external audit (Status below)
and not independently verified; the horizontal-line identity also holds for either sign, but the positivity of its
value uses a0 < 0. The centre moment identity C_2 = -1 of Proposition 17 and the cubic centre equations admit explicit
smooth data with Omega < 0 on Q1 for every a0 < 0 (A.37, Remark 1), and the far-field sign conditions admit explicit
angular data in both branches (A.37, Remark 2); these data are not matched to each other or to a profile.
Not asserted: that Omega <= 0 on Q1 with a0 < 0 is possible or impossible for a profile; A'(0) < 0 or A'(pi/2) > 0;
sigma > 0; any restriction at a degenerate centre beyond the vanishing of the quartic part of Omega; existence or
nonexistence for beta > 2.
Status: proved by the authors from an external consultation (commissioned by the authors), whose answer the authors
rederived step by step; an external audit found (a) to (f) and both remarks correct, corrected the wording of (b), of
the Reading, of Step 4 of A.37 and of both remarks (of the statements in (f) only the positivity of the
horizontal-line integral uses a0 < 0), supplied the residual coefficients of Remark 1 and the sigma = 0 data of
Remark 2, and strengthened (e) from Theta <= 0 to Theta < 0 on the upper half-plane by a sublevel-set area argument,
which the authors rederived. The independent verification confirmed the first draft (parts (a) to (f), with Theta <= 0
in (e), and both remarks) and, separately, the changes of the second draft (the strict sign and the whole backward
basin in (e), the residual coefficients and the sigma = 0 data), each with its own proof. The text here differs from
the verified second draft only by renamed symbols in Step 5 of A.37 and by the explicit form 2 beta/b = 2 + 4/b of the
area exponent there. The symbolic checks mentioned in A.37 are consistency checks, not part of the proof.

Proposition 37 (one sign change of the vorticity on vertical lines: necessary conditions). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be
a profile in class A' (so beta > 2 by Corollary 4), with either sign of a0, and use the notation of Propositions 33 to
35 (V, tau, w, xi, E, C_xi, c_E on the horizontal axis; Y, T, s, z, eta, E_v, c_v, C(y) = U2_xx(0, y), I_s, P, h, J_R
on the vertical axis; L = pi/2) and of Theorems 11, 15 and 16 (F, A, H, B, A_j, gamma = 1 - 2 delta, d = 2 - delta).
Put g = Omega_xy(0, 0), p = A'(0), alpha = A'(L), f = F(L) (f has the sign of a0), sigma = F''(L) + gamma f,
m = delta (1 - delta) H'(L), D = 2 (beta + 2)(2 beta + 1), D4 = 4 (beta + 2)(4 beta + 5) and
K = 4 beta (4 beta - 3) (D4 = 340 and K = 108 at beta = 3). Suppose that the profile is in class S: there is a
function G: (0, inf) -> (0, inf) such that for every x > 0, Omega(x, y) < 0 for 0 < y < G(x) and Omega(x, y) > 0 for
y > G(x). Then:
 (a) G is continuous, Omega(x, G(x)) = 0 and Omega_y(x, G(x)) >= 0 for x > 0; w <= 0 on (0, inf) and g <= 0. There are
     no heights 0 < y1 < y2 with z(y1) > 0 > z(y2), and no angles 0 < phi1 < phi2 < L with A(phi1) > 0 > A(phi2). If
     0 < phi* < L and A(phi* - eps) < 0 < A(phi* + eps) for every sufficiently small eps > 0, then G(x)/x -> tan(phi*)
     as x -> inf.
 (b) Omega(x, y) = x z(y) + O(x^3 y^(-3 - delta)) uniformly for 0 < x <= 1 and y >= 1, and
     max(-z(y), 0) = o(y^(-3 - delta)) as y -> inf. If j is an integer with 0 <= j < 4 beta, A_i'(0) = 0 for
     0 <= i < j and A_j'(0) != 0, then A_j'(0) < 0. If j is an integer with 0 <= j <= 2 beta, A_i'(L) = 0 for
     0 <= i < j and A_j'(L) != 0, then A_j'(L) < 0 and z(y) > 0 for all large y. In particular p <= 0 and alpha <= 0;
     since B'(0) = 2 H'(0) p + 2 delta F'(0) and B'(L) = 2 H'(L) alpha + sigma, p = 0 implies F'(0) <= 0, and
     alpha = 0 implies sigma <= 0; z > 0 for all large y if alpha < 0, or if alpha = 0 and sigma < 0.
 (c) As x, y -> 0+, w = g x + O(x^3), z = g y + O(y^3), s = (2 beta + 1) g y + O(y^3), a0 C = -D g y + O(y^3),
     a0 U2_yy(0, y) = (D - a0) g y + O(y^3) and a0 (U1_x(x, 0) - 2) = (D/2) g x^2 + O(x^4). If g = 0, then
     Theta = a0 y + O(|X|^5), Psi = -2 x y + O(|X|^6), Omega = G1 x^3 y + G2 x y^3 + O(|X|^6) with
     K G2 = (a0 - D4) G1, and G1 < 0 unless G1 = G2 = 0; moreover z = G2 y^3 + O(y^5), a0 C = -K G2 y^3 + O(y^5),
     a0 U2_yy(0, y) = (K - a0) G2 y^3 + O(y^5) and a0 (U1_x(x, 0) - 2) = (beta + 2)(4 beta + 5) G1 x^4 + O(x^6). In
     particular, if g = 0, (G1, G2) != (0, 0) and a0 < D4, then G2 > 0, z > 0 on some interval (0, eps) and z >= 0 on
     (0, inf).
 (d) int_0^inf E_v s/Y dy = -c_v alpha >= 0, and s > 0 and a0 C < 0 at some points of (0, inf). If alpha = 0, or if
     g < 0, then s and C both take both signs on (0, inf). If g < 0 and z > 0 somewhere, put y_C = inf {y > 0 :
     a0 C(y) < 0}, y_s = inf {y > 0 : s(y) > 0} and y_z = inf {y > 0 : z(y) > 0}; then 0 < y_C < y_s < y_z, and there
     is v > 0 with s(v) > 0 > z(v), so Theta_x(x, v) > 0 > Omega(x, v) for all sufficiently small x > 0. As y -> inf,
     U2_yy(0, y) = m y^(-1 - delta) + o(y^(-1 - delta)) and C(y) = (alpha - m) y^(-1 - delta) + o(y^(-1 - delta)). If
     alpha = sigma = 0, then s(y) = -gamma f m y^(-1 - 3 delta) + o(y^(-1 - 3 delta)),
     z(y) = (gamma f m/2) y^(-1 - 3 delta) + o(y^(-1 - 3 delta)) and a0 H'(L) >= 0. If g < 0 and either
     alpha = 0 > sigma or alpha = sigma = 0 != H'(L), then there are heights y1 < y2 < y3 with s(y1) < 0, s(y2) > 0
     and s(y3) < 0. Class S is impossible if s <= 0 on (0, inf) or if a0 C >= 0 on (0, inf); if a0 > 0 and (H1) or
     (H2) of Proposition 34(e) holds, then g = 0, s >= 0 and z >= 0 on (0, inf), and alpha < 0.
 (e) The function q = -w is nonnegative and integrable on (0, inf), Q = int_0^inf q dx > 0, int_0^inf
     (1 - 2 U1_x(x, 0)) q dx = a0, and int_0^inf U1_x(x, 0) q dx/Q = 1/2 - a0/(2 Q). If a0 < 0, then V > 0 on (0, inf)
     (so Proposition 33 applies), F'(0) < 0, U1_x(x, 0) > 2 for some x > 0, and w < 0 on (x2, inf) for some x2. If
     a0 > 0 and V > 0 on (0, inf) (in particular if the backward basin of the origin is R^2, Proposition 24(a)), then
     F'(0) > 0, p < 0, branch (i) of Theorem 12 holds and w < 0 on (x2, inf) for some x2. If a0 > 0 and p = 0 (in
     particular in branch (ii)), then V has a positive zero, the backward basin of the origin is not R^2, and
     Proposition 24(c) applies.
 (f) With Omega_+ = max(Omega, 0), Omega_- = max(-Omega, 0), A_+ = max(A, 0) and A_- = max(-A, 0), for every n > 2
     beta, (1 - 2 beta/n) int_Q1 Omega_+^n dx dy = int_Q1 Theta_x Omega_+^(n - 1) dx dy and (1 - 2 beta/n)
     int_Q1 Omega_-^n dx dy = -int_Q1 Theta_x Omega_-^(n - 1) dx dy, with absolutely convergent integrals and positive
     values; at n = 2 beta, int_Q1 Theta_x Omega_+^(2 beta - 1) dx dy = (1/2) int_0^L A_+^(2 beta) dphi and -int_Q1
     Theta_x Omega_-^(2 beta - 1) dx dy = (1/2) int_0^L A_-^(2 beta) dphi. In particular Theta_x > 0 at some point of
     Q1 where Omega > 0, and Theta_x < 0 at some point of Q1 where Omega < 0.
 (g) Suppose that the backward basin of the origin is R^2 (equivalently a0 y Theta(x, y) > 0 for y != 0, Proposition
     24(a)) and that Omega_y(x, G(x)) > 0 for every x > 0; then G is smooth and Theta_x = Omega_y (W2 - G' W1) on the
     graph of G. If g < 0, then Theta_x > 0 at some point of the graph. If g = 0, (G1, G2) != (0, 0) and a0 < D4, then
     Theta_x < 0 at some point of the graph. The following implication requires neither a complete backward basin nor
     the condition Omega_y(x, G(x)) > 0 on the nodal graph: if Theta_x >= 0 at every point of Q1 where Omega > 0, and
     z > 0 somewhere, then alpha < 0.
Reading. In the sign-structure scan of 6.9 (by the authors: 28 vertical lines of each of three stored numerical
states; reproduced by the independent verification on three of these lines for each state), every sampled vertical
line shows one detected reversal of Omega and one of Theta_x, negative below and positive above, with the Theta_x
reversal below the Omega reversal. The sampled signs of Omega are consistent with class S on the sampled lines; the
order of the two reversals is an additional numerical observation. Those states are not profiles, and the samples do
not prove the structure. For an exact profile in class S the proposition gives necessary conditions on the axis traces
and on the far-field data: neither the slope Omega_x(0, .) on the vertical axis nor the angular function A has a
positive value followed (at a larger height, respectively angle) by a negative one, while either may fail to take both
signs and intervals of zeros are not excluded (a); p <= 0 and alpha <= 0, with the higher-order tests of Theorem
16 (b); positive values of Theta_xx(0, .) and values of U2_xx(0, .) of the sign of -a0 somewhere, sign changes of both
at a nondegenerate centre or when alpha = 0, and the order of the first transitions of U2_xx(0, .), Theta_xx(0, .) and
Omega_x(0, .) when g < 0 and Omega_x(0, .) is positive somewhere (d); an excess of the horizontal axis strain over its
centre value somewhere when a0 < 0, and branch (i) when a0 > 0 and V > 0 (e). When g < 0 and Omega_x(0, .) is positive
somewhere, (d) gives a height v at which Theta_x > 0 > Omega near the vertical axis, so a Theta_x reversal lies below
the Omega reversal there, the order seen in the samples. With a complete backward basin and Omega_y(x, G(x)) > 0 for
every x > 0, Theta_x cannot be nonpositive on the whole nodal graph when g < 0, nor nonnegative on it when g = 0 with
a nonzero quartic block and a0 < D4 (g). Class S is not excluded here: the characteristic formula admits the sampled
order of the reversals in a scalar example (A.38, Remark 1), and explicit angular data meet the far-field restrictions
(A.38, Remarks 2 and 3); none of these examples is a profile.
Not asserted: that class S contains or excludes any profile; that z, s or C has exactly one sign change; g < 0; that A
takes both signs (A.38, Remark 3); an eventual strict sign of z when alpha = sigma = H'(L) = 0; a global sign of Psi
(the maximum-principle argument of Proposition 35(b) uses Omega <= 0 on Q1); branch (i) for a0 > 0 without V > 0; the
complete backward basin, the regularity of the nodal graph or a sign of Theta_x on it for a sought profile; any
property of the stored numerical states beyond the samples of 6.9; existence or nonexistence for beta > 2.
Status: proved by the authors from an external consultation (commissioned by the authors), whose answer the authors

Proposition 38 (one sign change of Theta_x on vertical lines: necessary conditions). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a
profile in class A' (so beta > 2 by Corollary 4) and use the notation of Proposition 37 (V, tau, xi, C_xi on the
horizontal axis; Y, T, s, z, eta, E_v, c_v, C, I_s, P on the vertical axis; g, p, alpha, f, sigma, m, D4, G1, G2; F,
A, H, gamma, d; L = pi/2), and put J_T = gamma cos(phi) F - sin(phi) F', so that r^(2 delta) Theta_x -> J_T uniformly
in phi (Theorem 11(b)). The profile is in class T if there is a function G_T: (0, inf) -> (0, inf) such that for every
x > 0, Theta_x(x, y) < 0 for 0 < y < G_T(x) and Theta_x(x, y) > 0 for y > G_T(x); in class ST if it is in class S
(Proposition 37, nodal graph G) and in class T; and in class ST< if it is in class ST and G_T(x) < G(x) for every
x > 0. Then:
 (a) In class T: G_T is continuous, Theta_x(x, G_T(x)) = 0 and Theta_xy(x, G_T(x)) >= 0 for x > 0; tau' <= 0 on
     (0, inf), a0 > 0 and g <= 0. There are no heights 0 < y1 < y2 with s(y1) > 0 > s(y2), and no angles
     0 < phi1 < phi2 < L with J_T(phi1) > 0 > J_T(phi2). If 0 < phi* < L and J_T(phi* - eps) < 0 < J_T(phi* + eps) for
     every sufficiently small eps > 0, then G_T(x)/x -> tan(phi*) as x -> inf. Moreover F > 0 on (0, L], Theta > 0 on
     the open upper half-plane, the backward basin of the origin is R^2, V > 0 on (0, inf), tau > 0 on [0, inf),
     U1_x(x, 0) <= 2 for x > 0, F'(0) > 0, p < 0, and branch (i) of Theorem 12 holds.
 (b) In class T, Theta_y > 0 and W2 > 0 at every point of the graph of G_T. If Theta_xy(x, G_T(x)) > 0 for every
     x > 0, then G_T is smooth and W2 - G_T' W1 = -U2_x Theta_y/Theta_xy on the graph; if in addition g < 0, then
     U2_x < 0 at some point of the graph.
 (c) In class ST: sigma >= 0, and either alpha < 0 and z(y) > 0 for all large y, or alpha = sigma = H'(L) = 0 and
     z <= 0 on (0, inf); in particular z > 0 somewhere if and only if alpha < 0. If sigma = 0, then s(y) =
     gamma f (alpha - m) y^(-1 - 3 delta) + o(y^(-1 - 3 delta)) as y -> inf and m <= alpha. A < 0 on some interval
     (0, eps) and A > 0 at some point of (0, L). There are no heights 0 < y1 < y2 with z(y1) > 0 > z(y2) (as in
     Proposition 37(a)). Put y_C = inf {y > 0 : a0 C(y) < 0}, y_s = inf {y > 0 : s(y) > 0} and y_z = inf
     {y > 0 : z(y) > 0}, the infimum of the empty set being inf. If g < 0, put ell_s = sup {y > 0 : s(y) < 0} and
     ell_z = sup {y > 0 : z(y) < 0} (possibly inf); then, with limits as x -> 0+,
        0 < y_C < ell_s <= liminf G_T(x) <= limsup G_T(x) <= y_s < ell_z <= liminf G(x) <= limsup G(x) <= y_z,
     so G_T(x) < G(x) for all sufficiently small x > 0, and U2_yy(0, y_s) > 0.
 (d) In class ST with g = 0, (G1, G2) != (0, 0) and a0 < D4:
     on Q1, Omega/(x y) = G1 x^2 + G2 y^2 + O(|X|^4) and
     Theta_x/(x y) = (4 beta + 5) G1 x^2 + (4 beta - 3) G2 y^2 + O(|X|^4), and as x -> 0+, G(x)/x -> mu =
     (-G1/G2)^(1/2) and G_T(x)/x -> mu ((4 beta + 5)/(4 beta - 3))^(1/2) > mu, so G_T(x) > G(x) for all sufficiently
     small x > 0. Hence class ST< contains no profile with g = 0, (G1, G2) != (0, 0) and a0 < D4.
 (e) In class ST<: Theta_x > 0 at every point of Q1 where Omega = 0; the set {Omega > 0} intersected with Q1 is
     forward invariant and {Omega < 0} intersected with Q1 is backward invariant under the flow of W; and if
     0 < phi1, phi2 < L, J_T(phi1) < 0 and A(phi2) > 0, then phi1 < phi2.
Reading. In the sign-structure scan of 6.9 (by the authors: 28 vertical lines of each of three stored numerical
states; reproduced by the independent verification on three of these lines for each state), every sampled vertical
line shows one detected reversal of Omega and one of Theta_x, negative below and positive above, with the Theta_x
reversal below the Omega reversal: the sampled signs are consistent with class ST< on the sampled lines. Those states
are not profiles, and the samples do not prove the structure. For an exact profile, (a) shows that the sign structure
of class T alone fixes the sign of the temperature amplitude and excludes the alternatives left open elsewhere in this
report: within class T, a0 < 0, a sign change of the temperature on the upper half-plane, an incomplete backward
basin, a nonzero stagnation point on the horizontal axis and branch (ii) of Theorem 12 do not occur. In class ST, (c)
sharpens Proposition 37(b) and (d): either the far-field vertical slope alpha is negative, or alpha, sigma and H'(L)
all vanish and Omega_x(0, .) is nowhere positive; and A takes both signs. At a nondegenerate centre (g < 0) the nodal
graph of Theta_x lies below that of Omega near the vertical axis, the order seen in the samples; at a degenerate
centre with a nonzero quartic block and a0 < D4 it lies above it (d), so such centres are incompatible with class ST<.
The angular data of A.38, Remark 2 meet the restrictions of (a), (c) and (e) on F, J_T and A (A.39, Remark 1); no
profile is matched.
Not asserted: No existence result is proved for T, ST or ST<, and none of these classes is proved empty as a whole.
Part (d) excludes the specified degenerate-centre subclass from ST<. No nonexistence result for the entire subclass
with g < 0 (the case of the stored numerical states) is obtained. No general limit of G_T(x) or G(x) as x -> 0+ is
asserted beyond the subcase in (d); intervals of zeros of s or z are not excluded. A unique zero with strict opposite
signs on its two sides is not asserted for either s or z. The ordering results exclude a positive value followed by a
negative one; for g < 0, s takes both signs, and z does so when alpha < 0. Also not asserted: that Theta_xy > 0 on the
nodal graph of Theta_x; a version of (d) for higher-order degenerate centres; any property of the stored numerical
states beyond the samples of 6.9; existence or nonexistence for beta > 2.

Proposition 39 (far-field separation of the two nodal graphs in class ST<). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in
class ST< (Proposition 38), with the notation of Propositions 37 and 38 (G, G_T, F, A, H, J_T, gamma, delta, d;
L = pi/2) and V = -H' e_r + d H e_phi as in Theorem 11(b). Put K_T = gamma sin(phi) F + cos(phi) F' and
   M = (1 - delta) (d cos(2 phi) H - sin(2 phi) H') - sin(phi)^2 A,
so that r^delta U2_x -> M uniformly in phi (Theorem 15(b)). Then:
 (a) J_T(theta) >= 0 at every theta in (0, L) with A(theta) = 0.
 (b) Put theta_A = sup {phi in (0, L) : A(phi) < 0}. Then 0 < theta_A < L, A <= 0 on [0, theta_A], A >= 0 on
     [theta_A, L] and A(theta_A) = 0. With I_- = int_0^theta_A sin(d u) A(u) du and
     I_+ = int_theta_A^L sin(d (L - u)) A(u) du, one has I_- < 0 < I_+,
        M(theta_A) = (1 - delta) [sin(delta (L - theta_A)) I_- - sin(delta theta_A) I_+]/sin(delta L) < 0,
     and J_T(theta_A) > 0.
 (c) There are x0 > 0 and 0 < k1 < k2 such that G_T(x) < k1 x < k2 x < G(x) for every x >= x0. In particular
     limsup G_T(x)/x < liminf G(x)/x and liminf (G(x) - G_T(x))/x > 0 as x -> inf. Hence class ST< contains no
     profile with liminf (G(x) - G_T(x))/x = 0 as x -> inf; for example, none whose two nodal graphs have the same
     asymptotic slope.
Reading. Part (b) is a necessary condition on the leading far-field data alone: at theta_A, the leading coefficient
J_T of Theta_x on rays is strictly positive. No clean crossing of A at theta_A and no simple zero is assumed. The
ordering of Proposition 38(e) (every angle with J_T < 0 below every angle with A > 0) does not by itself exclude
J_T(theta_A) = 0; part (b) does. For example, at beta = 3 the data A_0 = -sin(4 phi), F = sin(phi) (1 + cos(phi)^2),
H_0 = -(9/119) sin(4 phi) (the extension to c = 0 of the family of A.38, Remark 2, stated there for 0 < c < 2) meet
every restriction of Proposition 38 on F, J_T and A listed in A.39, Remark 1, but J_T(theta_A) = 0 at theta_A = pi/4,
so they are not the leading data of a profile in class ST<; the members with 0 < c < 2 of that family satisfy (b)
(A.40, Remark 1). Part (c) says that two rays of fixed positive slopes separate the two nodal graphs for every
sufficiently large x; in particular the vertical distance between them is at least a positive multiple of x. At
x = 10^6 the sampled reversals of the stored numerical states of 6.9 lie at distinct slopes (y/x about 0.29 to 0.30
for Theta_x and 0.81 to 0.85 for Omega in the a = 600 states, about 0.36 to 0.38 and 0.99 to 1.03 in the third state;
scan by the authors, this line reproduced by the independent verification); these states are not profiles, and finite
samples neither prove nor test a statement about x -> inf.
Not asserted: no existence result and no exclusion of class ST<, of its subclass with g < 0, or of the classes S, T or
ST as a whole. Part (c) requires eventual separation of the two nodal graphs by two fixed rays; in particular, it
excludes the profiles in class ST< with liminf (G(x) - G_T(x))/x = 0. Proposition 39 alone asserts no convergence of
G(x)/x or of G_T(x)/x (Propositions 37(a) and 38(a) give such limits under strict sign changes of A or of J_T, and in
class ST< Proposition 40(c) gives the limit of G(x)/x; no general limit of G_T(x)/x is asserted). No restriction on
beta or on a0 beyond those already implied by class ST< (including beta > 2 by Corollary 4 and a0 > 0 by
Proposition 38(a)). No property of the stored numerical states beyond the attributed finite samples. No general
existence or nonexistence result for profiles of class A' with beta > 2.

Proposition 40 (asymptotic slope of the vorticity nodal graph in class ST<). Let (beta, Theta, Omega) be a profile in
class ST<, with the notation of Propositions 38 and 39 (G, G_T, F, A, J_T, M, theta_A; L = pi/2), and put
   theta_+ = inf {phi in (0, L) : A(phi) > 0}.
Then:
 (a) theta_A <= theta_+ < L, and A = 0 on [theta_A, theta_+].
 (b) M(theta) < 0 and J_T(theta) > 0 for every theta in [theta_A, theta_+].
 (c) G(x)/x -> tan(theta_+) as x -> inf.
Reading. In class ST< the vorticity nodal graph has an asymptotic slope without a strict-crossing hypothesis on A (A
takes both signs by Proposition 38(c)). For a profile in this class that satisfies the strict sign condition of
Proposition 37(a) at phi*, theta_A = theta_+ = phi*, and (c) recovers the limit given there; the equality
theta_A = theta_+ does not itself assert that strict sign condition, and no converse for exact profiles is asserted
here. If theta_A < theta_+, then for each fixed phi in (theta_A, theta_+), Theorem 15(c) gives Omega(r, phi) =
r^(-2 delta) (-J_T(phi) + o(1)) < 0 for all large r, so each such ray eventually lies below the graph, and the slope is
that of the right end of the zero interval. By Proposition 39(b), the continuity of J_T and Theorem 11(b) (equivalently,
by the choice of rays in Step 6 of A.40), limsup G_T(x)/x < tan(theta_A) <= lim G(x)/x.
Not asserted: no existence result, and no proof that class ST< is empty; part (c) is a necessary condition that every
profile in this class satisfies. No convergence of G_T(x)/x, no rate for the convergence in (c), and no restriction on
beta or on a0 beyond those already implied by class ST<. No general existence or nonexistence result for profiles of
class A' with beta > 2.
Status: proved; the argument was found by the independent verification, which gave its own complete proof, and was
written in this form by the authors from Proposition 39 and Theorem 15(c). An external audit (commissioned by the
authors) of the first draft of this text found the four steps of A.41 correct and complete, with no mathematical error
or gap, and corrected the wording of the Reading (the comparison with Proposition 37(a), the eventual position of the

Open: existence or nonexistence for beta > 2. Any such profile has unbounded temperature (Corollary 4) and one of
the two velocity asymptotics of Theorem 12.
