### 6.3 Centre quantities
c = Psi_xy(0) from the full-plane inverse, the part of c contributed beyond the fitted radius (and beyond larger
radii where available), and the Taylor identities T1, T2, T3 of Section 2.4 as relative defects (defect divided by the
sum of the absolute values of its terms). The centre moments and the Taylor quantities were computed from the stored
coefficients by exact rational polynomial integration, and the contributions beyond finite radii by floating-point
polynomial quadrature:

| state | a0 | c | strain contributed beyond r | T1 | T2 | T3 |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16+16, r <= 1e6 | 44.345379 | -1.99999995 | +0.0187 beyond 1e6 | 1.03e-3 | 2.09e-2 | 3.95e-6 |
| 24+24, r <= 1e6 | 52.350002 | -1.99999999 | +0.0199 beyond 1e6 | 2.23e-4 | 4.07e-3 | 8.84e-7 |
| 24+24, r <= 1e9 | 52.828950 | -1.99999999 | +0.0177 beyond 1e6; +0.0019 beyond 1e9 | 2.25e-4 | 4.64e-3 | 6.60e-7 |
| 32+32, r <= 1e6 | 59.098810 | -1.99999998 | +0.0170 beyond 1e6; +0.0026 beyond 1e9; +0.00028 beyond 1e12 | 3.16e-4 | 1.31e-2 | 2.66e-7 |

The deviations |c + 2| are 5.0e-8, 1.0e-8, 8.7e-9 and 1.5e-8. In every state about one percent of c comes from beyond
r = 1e6, i.e. from the extrapolated part of the representation for the states fitted to 1e6. These are the
contributions of the stored continuation; its discrepancy from an admissible asymptotic tail is not bounded, so the
uncertainty of c due to the tail is not quantified. A later independent check (Section 7, closed 2026-10-22T07:21Z)
recomputed every cell of the table and the four deviations |c + 2| from the stored coefficients, with beta = 3 and the
exponents of the radial representation taken as the intended exact rationals, the seven contributions beyond finite
radii by exact rational polynomial arithmetic with a rigorous enclosure of the sixth root that bounds their
integration interval; all agree with the printed values after rounding. These are exact values for the stored
continuation, and they bound no difference between it and an admissible tail. The identity T2 fails in every state by
far more than any rounding error, and the same check found its defect to be a nonzero exact rational number for each
of the four stored fields, so none of them satisfies (P2) exactly near the origin and none is an exact profile; this
gives no distance to a nearby solution. A Taylor-coefficient defect is not the pointwise residual ratio of the prompt,
and the numerical rejection of these states rests on the pointwise residuals of 6.2.

### 6.4 Far field beyond the fitted domain
Evaluating the stored finite basis algebraically at r -> infinity gives the defect of the next-order far-field
coefficient equations, i.e. of the compatibility relations that an exact profile must satisfy (Theorems 15, 16).
Maximum over 1024 midpoint angles of the absolute defect: temperature 1181.9 and vorticity 440.2 (16+16), 6218.8 and 1475.9 (24+24 fitted to 1e6), 16.6 and 2.70 (24+24
fitted to 1e9); maximum over the angles of the defect divided by the sum of the absolute values of its terms: 1 and
0.84, 1 and 0.93, and 0.069 and 0.025. For the 32+32 state the independent verification confirmed the 128 exact
Fourier coefficients of the stored representation at infinity and obtained, by orthogonality, the exact lower bounds
996.92 for the maximum over the angles of the absolute temperature defect and 59.00 for the vorticity defect (sampled
maxima at 1024 midpoint angles 4219.0 and 526.7). These values concern the stored representation with its far-field
exponents read as the intended rational values 1/3 (temperature) and -1/3 (vorticity); with the stored binary64
exponents read literally it is a different function, which is also not a stationary profile, for a separate reason,
and to which these values do not apply. These are coefficient-level defects, not the prompt's pointwise residual
ratios; at beta = 3 the temperature defect multiplies the power r^0 in the temperature residual, so the stored
continuation is not an asymptotic solution even where the pointwise ratio is small. The
leading angular coefficient of the vorticity far field changes from 3.02 (24+24, fitted to 1e6) to 1.28 (24+24,
fitted to 1e9), so the far field is not determined stably by these states. For the 24+24 state fitted to 1e6, the
critical vorticity identity of Proposition 14(d) fails by 7.3 percent of its flux term (source integral 5.203e6
against endpoint flux 4.847e6, independent Jacobi quadrature at three resolutions); a single moment identity does not
determine beta.

 - Stagnation points (16+16 and 24+24 fitted to 1e6; the verifier's own full-plane modal quadrature on three grids per

   exterior bound below; no floors). The sampled minima of W1/x and W2/y (with their smooth axis limits) are 2.770 and
   0.991 (16+16) and 2.800 and 0.998 (24+24), agreeing to within 5e-5 across the three grids, so W has no zero other
   than the origin at the sampled points; the smallest sampled radial drift W_r/r is close to 1, on the y-axis at
   radius about 1.3. A bound from exact rational majorants of the stored coefficients gives W_r/r >= 3/2 for
   r >= 5.15e9 (16+16) and r >= 6.67e10 (24+24), so W has no zero there. The absence of zeros of W between the sample
   points of the bounded region is not certified.
 - Spatial scale. The radius at which Theta_y(x, 0) falls to a0/2 is 43.31 (16+16) and 62.67 (24+24 fitted to 1e6):

### 6.6 Velocity-based transport reconstruction
An independent consistency diagnostic for the two 24+24 states of 6.2 (fitted
to r <= 1e6 and to r <= 1e9). The velocity of the stored vorticity, multiplied by k = -2/c (k - 1 is
about 5e-9), was used to recompute Theta, grad Theta and Omega along backward characteristics ending near the
origin (the formulas of Proposition 20 with the linear jet at the origin), with an implementation independent of the
solver (own full-plane modal Green quadrature, analytic velocity gradient from the Hessian of the stream function,
backward trajectories in a signed logarithmic variable, forward variational equations). Results (sampled points
only):
 - At eight scattered points the reconstructed vorticity differs from the stored vorticity by up to 8.55 percent
   (first state) and 7.88 percent (second state) of the stored absolute vorticity, at (x, y) = (0.4, 1.7); at
   (73, 113) by 4.56 and 3.78 percent. These values are unchanged to the displayed digits under refinement of the
   quadrature order (80, 120, 160), of the ODE tolerances (1e-8 to 1e-12) and of the backward time (9, 12, 15).
   The relative temperature discrepancies are at most 1.5e-4 and the gradient discrepancies at most 1e-3.
 - Near the y-axis the discrepancy is larger. For the state fitted to r <= 1e9, at 17 points (radii 0.03 to 2, angles 5 to 89 degrees from the
   x-axis), the discrepancy of Omega/(xy) is below 3 percent at 5 and 15 degrees but 12 to 33 percent at 80 to 89
   degrees (largest 32.67 percent at r = 2, 89 degrees); at r = 0.1, 85 degrees it is 22.61 percent and the
   discrepancy of Theta_x is 25.05 percent. At the centre the coefficients of xy in the reconstructed and in the
   stored vorticity differ by 0.045 percent of the stored coefficient (both states); by an exact identity the signed
   difference (reconstructed minus stored coefficient) equals -T1/35 - T3/7, with T1, T3 the signed defects of the identities of Section 2.4 for the velocity
   kU and vorticity k Omega at beta = 3. The large discrepancies are therefore produced at finite radius.
 - At r = 0.1, 85 degrees, the prompt's normalized temperature residual is 6.1e-6, while the x-derivative of the
   temperature equation, normalized by the sum of the absolute values of its five terms, has ratio 0.136; the
   continuous extension of this ratio to the y-axis is 0.185 at y = 1.
Reading: near the y-axis the error in Theta_x enters the temperature residual only through W1 Theta_x, which is small
compared with W2 Theta_y there, so the prompt's normalized residual does not detect it, and the stored vorticity is
not the one transported by the stored velocity. This is consistent with Proposition 22 (a small temperature residual
does not control the vorticity for a prescribed velocity). These are sampled consistency diagnostics, not interval
bounds, and they do not exclude a nearby solution.

### 6.7 Resolution, domain and optimization budget
The four states have unequal optimization histories, so their differences alone do not separate optimization from
resolution.
Equal outer-iteration comparison (solver logs; the records were parsed independently in the verification). From one
common 16+16 state (a0 = 42.24, obtained from the 16+16 state of 6.2 by 100 further iterations during which the logged
objective varied within 2.5 percent and a0 decreased from 44.35), 150 Levenberg-Marquardt iterations with the same row
definitions and weighting rule (evaluated on different grids) were run at 16+16 (radial degree 47, 300 x 48
collocation points), 24+24 (degree 63, 400 x 64) and 32+32 (degree 95, 500 x 96); the last two are the 24+24 (r <= 1e6)
and 32+32 states of 6.2. Logged pre-step objective (a sum of squares on each run's own grid, so not comparable between
runs) and post-step a0 at iterations 0, 50, 100, 149:

| basis | objective | a0 |
|---|---|---|
| 16+16 | 4.74e-4, 4.66e-4, 4.73e-4, 4.70e-4 | 42.24, 41.80, 40.73, 40.21 |
| 24+24 | 8.39e-4, 7.17e-5, 4.17e-5, 3.63e-5 | 42.24, 47.91, 51.83, 52.35 |
| 32+32 | 1.57e-3, 1.22e-4, 5.22e-5, 3.11e-5 | 42.24, 46.50, 53.63, 59.10 |

At 16+16 the objective stayed within 3 percent of its initial value over all 150 records while a0 moved by 4.8
percent. The comparison equalizes outer iterations only, not trial evaluations or wall time (summed step times 530,
1981 and 10004 s). At its end the 24+24 and 32+32 objectives were still decreasing and a0 was still increasing, so it
does not separate optimization error from resolution error. Continuing the 32+32 run with unchanged settings (a
snapshot containing 47 further accepted records and no termination marker) increased a0 at every step, from 59.10
to 62.38, while the objective decreased from 3.11e-5 to 2.46e-5; no limit follows from these records.
Domain. Enlarging the fitted domain from 1e6 to 1e9 at 24+24 (with 100 further iterations) lowered the residual beyond
the fitted domain and the far-field coefficient defects and left the core residuals essentially unchanged; it changed
a0 from 52.35 to 52.83. a0 is invariant under the scaling symmetry, so its variation (44.35, 52.35, 52.83, 59.10) is
not a gauge effect; it shows no convergence of a0.
Jacobian (solver diagnostic; its source and labels were checked in the verification, the singular value
decomposition was not recomputed). At the 24+24 state, on an older diagnostic grid (300 x 48 points, the two equation
row blocks only, columns scaled to unit norm), the singular values range from 11.2 down to about 1.8e-15. The scaling
generator (delta Theta = Theta - X.grad Theta, delta Omega = -X.grad Omega) is represented in the basis with relative
field 2-norm errors 1.9e-8 and 6.5e-6 on that grid, and the column-scaled Jacobian maps the corresponding unit vector
to a vector of 2-norm 4.2e-11. This is consistent with an approximately neutral direction but is not implied by the
symmetry at an approximate state: the derivative of the residuals along the generator is
delta R_Theta = R_Theta - X.grad R_Theta, delta R_Omega = -X.grad R_Omega, which vanishes automatically at an exact
solution. A frozen-weight centred difference of the residual in beta (step 1e-4), projected against the retained
column space after removal of the represented dilation direction, has relative size 8.5e-5, so in this linearization
beta enters weakly. The dependence of these numbers on the step, grid, rank cutoff and weights was not studied.
Fixed-beta continuation (solver logs; endpoint fields recomputed independently). From the common 16+16 state above
(a0 = 42.24), two chains in beta (upwards and downwards) in steps of 0.01, each step warm-started from its neighbour
with the fields re-expanded in the basis of the new beta, 50 iterations per step (beta = 3 reference: 100 iterations),
with a half-width gauge Theta_y(x*, 0) = a0/2 (x* located on a logarithmic grid from the preceding state, so the gauge
location moves by up to one grid cell between steps), ended with the logged pre-step objectives and a0

| beta | 2.96 | 2.97 | 2.98 | 2.99 | 3.00 | 3.01 | 3.02 | 3.03 | 3.04 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| objective | 6102 | 3.08 | 0.0799 | 7.22e-4 | 4.75e-4 | 7.91e-4 | 0.0582 | 2.96 | 36.3 |
| a0 | -0.00021 | 47.6 | 43.0 | 41.7 | 42.1 | 42.4 | 43.5 | 51.6 | 7.48 |

The objective is lowest at beta = 3, the value at which the chains started, with similar orders of magnitude at equal
offsets on the two sides. These are finite endpoints of chains with unequal cumulative work and a state-dependent
normalization, and several final histories were still changing (at 2.96, 2.98, 3.02 and 3.03 the last change was an
increase); they identify no fixed-beta optimum or floor and do not determine beta. The endpoint fields at 2.96 and 3.04
are not zero (independent evaluation: sampled maxima of |Omega| 6.07 and 1.27, c = -2.00017 and -2.0000022), although
at 2.96 a0 changed sign and nearly vanished.

### 6.8 Other numerical approaches
Records of finite computations that did not produce an admissible state. The numbers
below were read from the run logs and stored histories as they stood at 2026-10-20T20:16Z and checked against them
independently by the verifier (an audit of the records, not an independent rerun of the evolutions). They are not
evidence for or against existence.
 - Dynamic rescaling. The time-dependent equations in self-similar variables, Omega_s + (c_l X + U).grad Omega =
   c_w Omega + Theta_x and Theta_s + (c_l X + U).grad Theta = (c_l + 2 c_w) Theta, were evolved on a grid uniform in
   log r with the A1 parity built into the angular basis and a numerical implementation of the full-plane modal Green
   formula with a power-law tail closure beyond the grid (no tail error bound is claimed); c_w and c_l were fixed by
   normalization conditions at the centre and at one point of the x-axis (x = 0.784). A steady state with c_w < 0
   converts, by a change of time unit and amplitudes, into a profile (P) with c = -2, beta = c_l/(-c_w) and
   a0 = 4 Theta_y(0)/c^2, where c = Psi_xy(0) in the evolved variables; along a varying trajectory these are
   instantaneous diagnostics only. From Gaussian data (32 angular modes, 512 radial points): c = -0.092, -0.056, -0.033
   at s = 13.6, 20.6, 32.4, with instantaneous beta 1.95, 2.43, 2.55 and instantaneous a0 474, 1272, 3675; the
   instantaneous a0 reached 2.85e4 at s = 44.8, after which c changed sign and the run stopped on a discrete
   blow-up criterion (s = 47.0). With the initial vorticity amplitude multiplied by 4 and by 16, at s = 40: c = -0.028
   and -0.072, beta 2.77 and 2.73, instantaneous a0 5164 and 780, in both cases after a decrease from about 6000.
   With a0 < 0 the strain changed sign (c = 3.47 at s = 6.8) and the run stopped on the blow-up criterion. Started from
   three 16+16 least-squares states at beta = 3 (and reruns with a smaller time step, with 24 angular modes
   and with 512 radial points), all six short runs left the initial state: the stored quantity max |d Phi/ds| / |c_w| over the grid (Phi = Theta/r;
   right-hand side and c_w evaluated before the step they are recorded with) rose, in five of the runs, with fitted
   log-slopes 4.1 to 5.8 on 0.1 <= s <= 0.5 (two to five records per run; the sixth run has too few records in that
   window; these short fits establish neither an exponential law nor a rate independent of resolution), and by s = 0.6 to 0.7 the runs had c between -1.96 and
   -1.89 and instantaneous beta between 2.82 and 2.94; one longer run reached c = -0.38 and instantaneous beta = -1.93
   at s = 2.02. No run approached a steady state. These finite histories do not establish an unbounded amplitude, do
   not rule out later convergence, and do not identify an unstable mode of a profile.
 - Characteristic Newton iteration with beta free. The unknown is the vorticity in a finite basis (equivalently the
   stream function, with the canonical inverse); Theta and Omega are reconstructed by integrating backward along the
   characteristics of W from the exact linear jet at the centre (Proposition 20); the closure defect (basis vorticity
   minus reconstructed vorticity, in weighted or projected coordinates), the condition c = -2 and a dilation gauge are
   driven to zero by a Newton-Krylov iteration with backtracking, accepting a step only if the Euclidean norm |E| of
   the defect vector decreases. |E| is not the prompt's residual ratio, and its values are not comparable between the
   two basis variants. Start: the 24+24 least-squares state at beta = 3. Variant 1 (fixed far-field exponents):
   |E| = 1.051, 0.543, 0.492, 0.379, 0.360, 0.356 with beta = 3, 2.877, 2.677, 2.519, 2.470, 2.478 and a0 = 50.2,
   73.2, 109.6, 170.4, 206.1, 196.0; restarted from a refitted state at beta = 2.519: |E| = 2.453, 1.245, 1.000, 0.677,
   beta = 2.519, 2.724, 2.905, 2.990, a0 up to 228.8. Variant 2 (beta-dependent exponents, smooth filtered fit; two
   filter levels): |E| from 0.4347 to 0.2851 and from 0.5494 to 0.4627 in four accepted steps each, beta from 3 to

   variant-2 runs, full Newton steps multiplied |E| by 9.1 to 26.5, and 12 of the 16 accepted steps of the four runs
   (logs as of 2026-10-20T20:16Z) used damping. The physical closure defect of variant 2 is not
   controlled by |E| alone (its fit is a smooth filter, not a projection) and was monitored separately; no state with a
   small closure defect was obtained. The beta paths differ (decreasing, and increasing after the restart), so these
   iterations do not determine beta.

### 6.9 A transport-exact representation in mixed coordinates
Formulation. We work on the branch a0 > 0, Theta_y > 0 (positive temperature slope on the open quadrant). There the map
(x, y) -> (x, eta), eta = Theta/a0, is a local chart; a global chart additionally needs coverage (properness), which local
positivity does not give. On the chart, y = G_x(x, eta) for a generating function G with A = G_x,eta = a0/Theta_y > 0.
With a = beta + 2, b = beta - 2, B0 = G_xx, C = G_eta,eta and M = a G_eta - b eta C, the velocity W = beta X + U is
W1 = M/A, W2 = B0 M/A + b eta A, the stream function is Psi = beta x G_x + b eta G_eta - 2 beta G, and Omega = -Lap Psi with
the physical derivatives d/dx - (B0/A) d/d eta and (1/A) d/d eta. For every G with A > 0 the temperature equation (P2) holds
identically and U = curl Psi locally; the only remaining equation is (P1), whose residual in these variables is
R = (M/A) Omega_x + b eta Omega_eta + Omega + a0 B0/A, the prompt's R_Omega at the corresponding physical point (the four
terms of N_Omega are pulled back separately, before taking absolute values). Near the centre G = h x eta + O(4) with
h = P(1, 0) (P the polynomial below, plus the centre values of the core functions when they are present); then c = -2 for
every h > 0 and the physical slope is Theta_y(0) = a0/h. The solvers impose h = 1 through a weighted residual row
(weight 1e4; the collocation rows of normalized residuals have weight 1), not exactly; for the stored states a7e057ae, d6efe320 and 2fe327c0 of
6.9 exact certificates give h - 1 approximately 7.03e-15, -5.31e-16 and -1.92e-14, and for 62df5606, fb05ac9a and
134d9098 the independent verifier's exact rational sums of the stored coefficients at the centre give h - 1
approximately -1.55e-15, -6.80e-15 and -1.43e-14; for these six states |h - 1| < 2e-14 holds by exact comparison, and
the stored coefficient and the physical slope a0/h agree to the digits reported. In solver labels a0 denotes the stored coefficient of Theta = a0 eta;
the physical centre slope is a0/h, and a label such as 600 is a rounded display of 600/h, not an exact decimal. That U is the canonical velocity of Omega
on R^2 is not automatic: on R^2 the function G = h x eta gives Omega = 0 and the strain velocity U = (2x, -2y). For each
state evaluated independently below without core functions, both points were settled by proofs. An exact certificate gives
A >= delta E^(1/3) everywhere, with delta = 1e-5 for the (48, 26) state (705 leaves), 1e-3 for the (64, 34) state fitted with
prompt rows (522 leaves), 1e-4 for the (80, 40) state (517 leaves), 1e-5 for the (64, 34) state fitted with grouped rows
(512 leaves) and 1e-4 for the outer-only (80, 40) state with a0 = 600 (375 leaves); with G_x(x, 0) = 0 this makes
eta -> G_x(x, eta) strictly increasing and onto the real line for each x, so the chart is global. A theorem on this family
(differentiated tail bounds U = O(r^(2/3)), Omega = O(r^(-1/3)), Theta = O(r^(1/3)), absolute convergence of the
origin-subtracted Biot-Savart integral, and a sublinear Liouville argument with U(0) = 0) then shows that U is the canonical
inverse of Omega. For states with core functions the same conclusion holds: a bound on the differentiated patch tails extends the
theorem, and exact certificates give A >= E^(1/3)/20 for the (80, 40) state at a0 = 600 with the patch added and
A >= E^(1/3)/100 for four later states (the core-patch continuation at (80, 40), and three (80, 64) states below;
about 400 outer and 200 patch leaves each). These are
statements about the particular stored functions, not about the vorticity equation. The constructed temperature
Theta = a0 eta is unbounded along the vertical axis, because the global chart maps each vertical line onto the whole eta line
(it grows like r^(1/3) there); the admissible class of Section 2.3 allows this, but such a function is not bounded initial
data for a blow-up construction.
Basis and solver. The reported lineage has beta fixed to 3; trials with other fixed exponents are listed separately
below; none determines beta. G = x eta E^(1/3) P(tau, w), P = sum_{n <= J, k <= K} c_nk T_n(2 tau - 1) T_k(2 w - 1),
E = 1 + x^2 + (eta/s_e)^6, w = (eta/s_e)^2 E^(-1/3), and tau = -log(1 - (1 - e^(-3)) E^(-1/6))/3 (a logarithmic map of
E^(-1/6), which behaves like r^(-1/3) at infinity, clustering nodes towards the centre). One soft gauge row acts
on the dilation: the mixed-coordinate value G_x,eta(1, 0) (at (x, eta) = (1, 0)), which the dilation changes, has weight
1e2, and its target is reset to the value of the initial coefficients at every invocation. For the four explicitly
checked stored states 2f1a793c, d6efe320, a7e057ae and 2fe327c0 its value is approximately 1.081400020, with computed
pairwise spread below 2.3e-11. This is soft agreement, not an exactly inherited invariant and not a proof that the
finite basis is closed under dilation. a0 is
free unless stated. For E > 1, w_max = (1 - E^(-1))^(1/3) is the largest value of w at fixed E (attained on the vertical
axis); in the sampling descriptions below t = E^(-1/6), with t = 0 for the limiting section at infinity, and
S = w/w_max in [0, 1]. At E = 1 the point is the centre and S is undefined; centre residuals are evaluated separately
through their derivative limits. Where 305 values of S are stated, they are 1e-8, 1e-4, 1e-2, 1 - 1e-4, 1 - 1e-8 and the
300 Chebyshev points (1 - cos(pi (i + 1/2)/300))/2, i = 0, ..., 299 (one evaluation of the state a7e057ae used the
same five values and the 305 points (1 - cos(pi (i + 1/2)/305))/2, i = 0, ..., 304, 310 in all, as stated by the
authors from their code; the printed six-decimal values of S agree with this prescription).
Values on 2000 random points are the
authors' summaries: the logs of these samples print 40 of the sampled values and the maximum over all 2000, and the
independent replay of the printed logs (Appendix B, entry closed 17:03Z on 2026-10-21) could not reconstruct these
maxima from the printed samples. Collocation of R/N_Omega on a Chebyshev grid
in (tau, S) up to E^(-1/6) = 0.01
(radius about 1e6 along the horizontal axis, larger along the vertical axis), Levenberg-Marquardt with an analytic Jacobian
(automatic differentiation of the pointwise residual, evaluated in floating point; directional finite-difference
checks agreed to relative 1.3e-8 on the tested directions). Code checks: a manufactured G; on actual states,
Omega = -Lap Psi, U = curl Psi and the temperature residual by root inversion of y = G_x and centred finite differences
(agreement O(h^2), 4e-6 at the finest step). The chain rule, the velocity and stream function formulas, the transport
identity, the residual pullback and the centre formulas were also checked in an independent written audit and in an
external review; they are elementary and are not counted as results. Rows with a second normalizer, localized core
functions and added collocation points are described further below. The fits at (80, 40) and above were run with a second
implementation of the same solver on the GPU.

Normalization in the far field. The prompt's N_Omega contains |W1 Omega_x| + |W2 Omega_y| + |Omega|, whose leading
homogeneous parts are of order r^(-1/3), while the leading parts of W.grad Omega + Omega cancel (Euler's identity
beta Z.grad omega0 + omega0 = 0 for omega0 homogeneous of degree -1/beta). Under differentiated far-field expansions
(which hold for the stored functions of this family) one has, in directions where the leading denominators are
positive, |R_Omega|/N_Omega = r^(-1/3)(|C|/N0 + o(1)) and |R_Omega|/N2 -> |C|/N20 for the grouped normalizer
N2 = |U1 Omega_x| + |U2 Omega_y| + |beta X.grad Omega + Omega| + |Theta_x|, where N0, N20 are the leading coefficients
of the two normalizers (independently proved and externally reviewed; no statement is made where a leading
denominator vanishes, in particular on the axes, where the desingularized ratios above are used). The prompt ratio
therefore suppresses a far-field defect of the next order by r^(-1/3), a factor 1e-3 at r = 1e9; this is why the two
l = 2 states above fitted with prompt rows have prompt ratios of order 1e-4 at r = 1.7e9 but grouped ratios 0.03 to 0.26
there. The prompt's minimum verification item on far-field asymptotics requires the next order, so the grouped ratio is
reported with the prompt ratio below. In N2 the two leading parts that cancel are grouped before the absolute value is
taken; in the core N2 and N_Omega are comparable (the grouped ratio is about 0.78 times the prompt ratio at the centre and
at (0, 0.0431) in the evaluations above).
Floating-point sensitivity of far rows. The residual R is a difference of terms much larger than itself in the far
field, and N2 groups cancelling terms, so the grouped ratio computed in binary64 is sensitive at large radii. Under a
random relative perturbation of the coefficients of size 1e-14, the computed grouped ratio of the frozen state (64, 34)
fitted with rows R/N2 changes by about 4e-2 for 1e10 <= r < 1e14, by 1.5e-4 for 1e8 <= r < 1e10 and by at most 5e-7 for
r < 1e6; for the (56, 30) core-patch state described below the changes are at most 2e-6 for r < 1e10 and up to 2e-4
beyond. This is a sensitivity test: the perturbation changes the function, so it is not a measurement of the rounding
error at fixed coefficients, and it says nothing about the true value of the ratio at those radii. Fits that included
collocation rows at r beyond about 1e10 stopped early (no decrease of the objective); the fits below end the collocation
at r of about 4e7 (E^(-1/6) of about 3e-3) or report larger radii separately. The far-axis values of the independent
evaluations above were computed with 80 to 125 digits and are not affected. The limit of the grouped ratio as
r -> infinity, |C|/N20 in directions where the leading denominators are positive, is a property of the coefficients that
a collocation ending at a finite radius does not constrain directly. The independent analytic evaluation of this limit
for the (64, 34) state fitted with rows R/N2 gives 0.0488 on the vertical axis, 0.0499 on the ray w/w_max = 0.999 and
5.67e-5 on the horizontal axis; 85- and 125-digit evaluations at fixed coefficients approach these values as r grows
(0.0135, 0.0376 and 0.0461 at r = 1e10, 1e12 and 1e14 on the vertical axis), so the large far values of this state are
a property of the function and not of the arithmetic. A solver-side estimate (not independent) extrapolates the signed
grouped ratio along rays of fixed w/w_max to E^(-1/6) = 0 by a polynomial fit through those of eleven radii (E^(-1/6)
from 5e-4 to 1.6e-2) at which the perturbation sensitivity is at most 1e-6. On the (64, 34) state it gives 0.0481,
0.0491 and 4.8e-5 at the three directions above, and on the (80, 40) state 0.0339 on the vertical axis, where the
independent analytic value is 0.0342. For the two a0 = 600 states it gives values of order 1e-5 to 6e-5 on the rays
w/w_max >= 0.99 and on the horizontal axis of the core-patch state, where the exact limits above are 1.4e-5 to 2.3e-5 and
1.63e-5; at most intermediate rays the perturbation sensitivity exceeds 1e-6 at most of the eleven radii, and there the
exact limits reach 1.1e-4 to 1.6e-4. The extrapolation is therefore not a substitute for the exact limit.
Exact far limit on a section. The limit at infinity can be evaluated directly. On the compact section
F = x^2 + (eta/s_e)^6 = 1 of the leading homogeneous chart, with x = (1 - w^3)^(1/2), eta = s_e w^(1/2), 0 < w < 1
(w -> 0 is the horizontal axis, w -> 1 the vertical axis), let G0 = x eta F^(1/3) P(0, w), G1 = c1 x eta F^(1/6) P_t(0, w)
and G2 = x eta (c2 P_t(0, w) + (c1^2/2) P_tt(0, w)), with c1 = d/3, c2 = d^2/6, d = 1 - e^(-3) and P_t, P_tt the
derivatives in the Chebyshev variable tau; A = G0_x,eta, b = G0_xx/A, D_x = d_x - b d_eta, D_y = A^(-1) d_eta; S0 = -G1,
S1 = -2 G2 + G1_x G1_eta/A, u01 = -D_y S0, u02 = D_x S0, omega_j = -(D_x^2 + D_y^2) S_j. Then the limit of R_Omega/N2
along the ray through a section point is C/N20 with C = Z1 + Z2 + Z3 + Z4 and N20 = |Z1| + |Z2| + |Z3| + |Z4|, where
Z1 = -omega1, Z2 = u01 D_x omega0, Z3 = u02 D_y omega0, Z4 = a0 b (proof in the independent verification, with symbolic and high-precision
checks; core functions do not contribute). A binary64 implementation of these formulas reproduces the exact
values to at least nine digits at the reference directions (for example 0.0498746559 at w = 0.999 for the (64, 34) state
fitted with rows R/N2 and 1.567561e-4 at w = 3/4 for the outer a0 = 600 state). On 221 directions (w from 1e-8 to
1 - 1e-8) its largest sampled values of |C|/N20 are 6.3e-5, 3.5e-5 and 2.8e-5 for the three core-patch continuations at
(80, 40) with a0 at 600, (80, 40) with a0 free and (96, 48) with a0 free described below, at w = 0.465, 0.335 and 0.057
(binary64 values without a rigorous error bound; sampled maxima, not suprema). They exceed the dense-check maxima of these
states on the collocated range by factors of two to six. The formulas are differentiable in the coefficients and can be
used as collocation rows at t = 0 (exact rows still require conditioning and fixed-coefficient arithmetic checks); fits
with these rows are described below.
Axis amplitude diagnostic (solver-side floating point; the endpoint values of the frozen states are the exact ones of
the compatibility bullet). With G fixed the residual on the horizontal axis is affine in a0, R = S1 + a0 S2 with
S2 = B0/A. On the axis B0/A vanishes by parity, so both S1 and S2 are divided by eta before the limit eta -> 0+ is
taken; the root a0*(x) = -S1/S2 of these parity-divided coefficients (assumed nonzero) tends to the centre value as x -> 0 and to the
far-axis value as x -> infinity. For the (64, 34) frozen state fitted with prompt rows, a0*(x) = 393.887 at x = 1e-4,
stays within 392.6 to 394.3 for x <= 1e6 and decreases monotonically beyond, to 390.7 at x = 1.8e6, 297.9 at 1.8e9 and
285.9 at 1e10 (limit 268.8): the two amplitudes separate beyond the fitted domain (x <= 1e6 on the horizontal axis). For
the (64, 34) state fitted with rows R/N2, a0*(x) stays within 401.50 to 401.60 for x <= 1e6 and within 401.34 to 401.60
for x <= 1e10 (exact endpoint values 401.59965 and 401.32402, disjoint). For the (56, 30) core-patch state below, a0*(x)
lies in 400.49 to 400.60 for 1e-4 <= x <= 1.8e9. For the (80, 40) state with a0 fixed at 600 and prompt rows, see the a0
bullet above (600.0 for x <= 1.8e5, 994 at 1.8e9).

and with a0 free: the finite basis is numerically rank deficient, and individual vectors of this cluster have no error
bound. The dilation generator 2G - x G_x - eta G_eta is matched in the basis to relative 1.25e-11 but with coefficient
norm 4.4e8, and its logged projection onto 100 selected singular directions is about 0.17; the dimension of the
numerical near-kernel depends on a threshold, and the projection onto all of it was not computed. Truncated solves
removing the k smallest directions (k = 1 to 10) gave logged residual ratios that decrease at several steps of k, which
exact optima on nested subspaces cannot do, so they are not accurate least-squares optima. The diagnostic determines
neither the amplitude nor the exponent and establishes no stationarity; whether the dilation or the a0 direction is
weak at this state is not decided by it.

Finite checks at points of the axes (independent verification). On the axes the raw residual of (P1) and both raw
normalizers vanish by parity, so the raw ratios are undefined (0/0); they remain undefined, no floor is put under any
denominator, and the axis comparisons use the divided normalizers ND and ND2 defined below, evaluated through their
derivative limits. Underflow: in the authors' binary64 evaluations (dense checks, regional tables, desingularized evaluator) no floor,
clipping or regularization is applied to any normalizer; plain ratios are formed only at chart points with x > 1e-12 and
eta > 1e-12, so the exact axes are never divided by, and the nearest retained rows (relative distance 1e-10 from an axis)
have normalizers of order 1e-10. The authors report no floor under any normalizer in their off-axis binary64 checks;
their treatment of underflow and any counts of underflow events have not been authenticated by the independent
verification. Probes on the current machine of the independent verification's own implementation show that its Gaussian
patch factors round to zero at finite inputs (Section 7 and Appendix B, entry closed 2026-10-21 14:53Z); the
authors' mathematically similar expression was inspected but not executed. This does not establish whether final
normalizers underflowed in the historical evaluations. Bounds on other intermediate quantities or on the final normalizers do not exclude underflow, and its
occurrence and effect in the historical evaluations remain open; the numerical verification record is incomplete in this
respect. In the selected published axis records of the independent verification, the six residual ratios are recorded as
null where the computed denominator is zero; their operands, and the divided normalizers ND of the
130-digit raw reference records at the same points, were checked to be finite, and these values of ND are strictly
positive. The older ratio helpers do not provide a NaN-safe policy in general; the evaluator
for general beta records undefined ratios as null separately. These checks provide no uniform numerical error budget.
What the independent verification checks at the axis points is the divided residual D = R_Omega/(x y) against the divided normalizers
ND = N_Omega/abs(x y) and ND2 = N2/abs(x y), evaluated through the proved derivative limits at the axes, with the two
groupings assembled separately. For each of the three members, at 16 exact rational points (the centre; (x, 0) with
x = 1e-3, 0.0067, 0.05, 0.5, 5, 50, 1e3, 1e6; (0, y) with y = 1e-3, 0.05, 0.5, 4.515, 50, 1e3, 1e6), raw implicit
derivatives of the generating function were evaluated at 90 and 130 digits and compared with Cartesian derivatives of
the physical fields (9 by 9 Lagrange stencils, in long double at up to eight steps and at 100 digits at three steps on 12
of the 16 points: 108 stencils, 8748 nodes and 4311 representative inversions after parity reflection). The largest
values over the 16 points of abs(D)/ND are 6.68e-7, 6.49e-7 and 6.36e-7 for (80, 64), (96, 64) and (96, 80), and of
abs(D)/ND2 5.48e-7, 5.15e-7 and 5.05e-7, all at (0, 0.05) except the (80, 64) grouped value at (0, 4.515); the largest
abs(D) is 3.35e-4, 3.25e-4 and 3.19e-4, at (0, 0.05). These values are below the off-axis zoom maxima of the prompt
ratio above. A separately coded bisection inverse at 100 digits agrees with the Newton inverse at 12 selected points to
a scaled difference of about 1.2e-83 (it shares the evaluation of G). Limits: the 100-digit stencils share the scalar
generating function and the Newton inverse with the raw reference and differ from it only in the differentiation, so
they are not a wholly independent implementation; the long-double differences depend on the step (loss of accuracy at
small steps, cancellation at large coordinates), and the steps singled out afterwards were selected with the raw
reference, so they are not blind error bounds; no bound on truncation or on inverse and rounding amplification is
established; the horizontal points x = 0.0067, 50, 1e3 and 1e6 have no 100-digit stencil check. The divided temperature
residual, which vanishes identically in this representation, is at most about 1.2e-128 at 130 digits (rounding-scale
behaviour, not an independent accuracy statement). Sixteen points per member give no supremum over the axes.

((64, 48) to (80, 64)), 2.8e-4 ((80, 64) to (96, 64)) and 2.0e-5 ((96, 64) to (96, 80)); for Theta 3.4e-4, 1.4e-5 and

With W = 3X + U, the fields of 62df5606 were evaluated with the verifier's own scalar generating-function evaluator
and chart inversion at 148 off-axis points (the nine rays y = m x with m = 1e-4, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10, 100, 1e3 and 1e4,

(r = 10^k, k = -3, ..., 8, on each axis), plus the origin. At all 148 points W.X > 0; the sampled minima of W1/x, W2/y
and |W|/(3|X|) are 0.89545 (at the first targeted point), 1.0000000002 and 0.33333337. These samples do not show
W.X > 0 everywhere; that the origin is the only zero of W follows instead from Proposition 28(b) with the global chart
certificate of this state (Section 7, entry closed 2026-10-21 10:41). Positivity of W.X everywhere is not a
consequence of a global chart: for beta > 2, every smooth generating function G, odd in x and in eta, with
G_(x eta) >= delta > 0 admits suitable perturbations G_N, with G_N - G of compact support away from the axes, that
keep a global chart, (P2) and the centre jets (and the canonical inverse with its tails, when the fields of G have

review; (P1) is not asserted for the perturbed fields; proof in Appendix B). The signed logarithmic radial derivatives
p_T = r Theta_r/Theta and p_O = r Omega_r/Omega were formed on each ray by fourth- and eighth-order differences in ln
r at the steps 0.004, 0.002 and 0.001 (888 slope rows, all at the 148 off-axis points; neither finite-difference slope
is formed on the axes). The slopes and ranges quoted next are those of the eighth-order formula at the step 0.002
(with the fourth-order formula at the step 0.004, |p_O - 2| reaches about 4.15e-9 at r = 1e-5). At
r = 1e-5, |p_T - 1| < 6e-10 and |p_O - 2| < 4e-9 on all nine rays, the degrees of the centre expansion. At r = 1e8,

p_T is 0.205 to 0.481. At the sampled radii the sign of Omega is negative on all nine rays for r <= 1 and on three of
them for r >= 1e3; near these sign changes p_O takes large values (up to 11.26 at r about 3.2), and no average across
sign changes is formed. Changing the step of the eighth-order formula from 0.002 to 0.001 changes p_T by at most
6.3e-13 and p_O by at most 6.5e-11 (7.9e-13 and 6.8e-11 for the fourth-order formula); these differentiation checks
share one evaluator and one chart inverse and are not independent inversions. All values are samples without error
bounds; no uniform limiting exponent and no rate is proved. Exact for this state, from its source certificate and not

the chart and not from the value of h.

Free exponent. In the free-exponent family G = x eta E^(1/beta) P(tau, w), E = x^2 + (1 + (eta/s_e)^(2M))^(m/M),
m = beta/(beta - 2), t = E^(-1/(2 beta)) (the far-field expansion variable r^(-1/beta)), tau = -log(1 - (1 - e^(-3)) t)/3,
w = (eta/s_e)^2 E^(-1/m) (for beta = 3, M = 3 this is the basis above), with beta an unknown of the iteration and a
centred-difference Jacobian column, started from a beta = 3 state at (56, 30) with rows R/min(N_Omega, N2), beta moved from
3 to 3.0000009 in seven stored iterations while the grouped grid maximum decreased from 3.6e-3 to 2.3e-3; this does not
show that beta is determined. Fixed-beta comparison at (56, 30) (not matched in cost) with a 12 by 12 core patch, the added points, rows
R/min(N_Omega, N2) to t = 0.01 and rows C/N20 at 48 directions (this implementation; the range 0 < t < 0.01 has no rows,
and in the fixed-beta runs at beta = 2.95, 3 and 3.05 below the desingularized maximum of R/N2 at t = 3e-3 is 9.5e-4
to 1.46e-3): from a common state at
beta = 3 (objective 1.76e-5), 180 iterations with beta held at 3, and 60 followed by 120 in a new invocation at 3.05, gave objectives 1.52e-5 and 3.74e-5,
solver-grid maxima 2.23e-4 and 3.33e-4 and root-mean-square residuals 3.8e-5 and 5.9e-5, with a0 ending at 406.85 and
432.06 (a0 moves with beta). In the linearization of the least-squares problem at each end state let r be the residual
vector, j the beta column, P the orthogonal projection onto the complement of the span of the other columns and p = |P j|.
With the other unknowns reoptimized, the linearized objective at a beta offset d is F(d) = F* + p^2 (d - d*)^2, with
d* = -(P j . P r)/p^2 and F* = |P r|^2 - p^2 d*^2. Here d* = -4.7e-4 at beta = 3 and -1.2e-4 at 3.05, and F* is about
1/97 and 1/155 of the objective: the minimizer of the unconstrained profiled linear model is displaced by d* from the end
state, at a much smaller objective. Its nonlinear predictive value has not been established, because the norm of the
required shape step and the validity of the linearization over that step are unknown (the iterations realized no such
decrease). Two widths follow from the model: the offset sqrt(objective)/p at which F exceeds its minimum by the current
objective, 0.067 and 0.083 (relative singular-value cutoff 1e-12; 0.056 to 0.088 at 1e-10 and 1e-14), and the offset
sqrt(F*)/p at which F doubles its minimum, 0.0068 and 0.0066. They are diagnostics of the unconstrained linear model in
the retained space, not statements of nonlinear identifiability; moreover the Jacobian behind them holds the residual
normalizers at their lagged values (the derivative of the normalizer is omitted), so they are frozen-weight surrogates,
and they establish neither stationarity in beta nor the accuracy or inaccuracy of the local model. The common start was optimized at beta = 3 (the
first iterate at 3.05 had objective 1.4e3, every row at its bound 1), so the factor 2.5 between the objectives does not
separate the convergence of the shape from an effect of beta. These coarse runs do not identify an exponent: the
linearized widths 0.007 to 0.08 (depending on the definition), at residual levels about 200 times the target, describe
frozen-weight linear models and establish neither nonlinear identifiability nor an optimum near 3; nothing here
determines beta for an exact profile. The same comparison at other values of beta follows the next paragraph; the runs
at (80, 64) are described in the paragraph "Free exponent at (80, 64)" below.
Selection of a0. The spatial scaling of Section 2.4 preserves a0, and the gauge row only fixes that scaling, so a0 is
a genuine unknown of the profile problem. No local condition of the kinds proved here fixes it by itself: the Taylor
coefficient identities at the centre are consistent for every a0 (Proposition 26), and in the far expansion of Theorem 16
the leading data are undetermined, so the formal recursions through the orders proved there do not select a0 by
themselves. The centre and far-axis amplitude conditions evaluated for the frozen states above relate a0 to the shape P;
when P varies they become joint compatibility conditions on (a0, P), which still constrain amplitude and shape together.
Whether these joint conditions and global matching (convergence, the canonical inverse) select a0 remains open. In
the numerical fits a0 is not determined. With prompt rows the best tested a0 moves with resolution (a0 bullet above). With
rows R/min(N_Omega, N2) at (56, 30) with the core patch, fits with a0 held at 350 and 600 reached solver-grid maxima
6.0e-4 and 6.8e-4 (least-squares objectives 4.55e-5 after 70 stored iterations, stopped, and 1.12e-4 after 43 stored
iterations, still decreasing) against 5.3e-4 (objective 2.70e-5) with a0 free at 400.5; these three runs included the
rows beyond r = 1e10. With rows R/min(N_Omega, N2), collocation to r of about 4e7 and no core patch (solver records; at
most 300 iterations; * marks a run stopped with no decrease), the solver-grid maximum of both ratios and the
root-mean-square residual were, at (64, 34): 3.64e-4 and 2.73e-5 at a0 = 350; 2.71e-4 and 2.05e-5 at 400 (80
iterations*); 2.68e-4 and 2.04e-5 with a0 free, ending at 404.91 (162*); 2.72e-4 and 2.08e-5 at 450 (184*); 2.30e-4 and
1.93e-5 at 500; 1.34e-4 and 1.97e-5 at 600. At (80, 40): 1.49e-4 and 7.0e-6 at 400 (99*); 1.49e-4 and 6.9e-6 with a0
free, ending at 403.65 (147*); 5.60e-5 and 5.0e-6 at 600 (at a0 = 600 the maxima along J = 64, 80, 96 are 1.34e-4, 5.60e-5
and 3.08e-5); 5.34e-5 and 6.9e-6 at 700; 6.67e-5 and 1.35e-5 at 800 (the runs
at 700 and 800 started from a state at a0 = 600 with objective 3e1 and 1e2 and were still decreasing at the end). At
equal iteration counts (iteration 98) the (80, 40) objective at a0 = 600 was 0.61 times that at 400 and the maximum 0.38
times. In every run the axis roots a0*(1e-4) and a0*(1e10) agreed with the run's a0 to within 1.2. The three exact
amplitude conditions of the compatibility bullet (centre, horizontal far axis, vertical far axis), evaluated in binary64
from the stored polynomials of the (80, 40) runs, give 400.006, 399.162, 400.181 at a0 = 400; 403.663, 402.963, 403.812
for the free run (a0 = 403.650); 600.056, 600.439, 599.949 at 600; 700.050, 700.287, 699.977 at 700; 800.054, 800.077,
800.665 at 800; and for the core-patch state at a0 = 600 599.936 and 599.985 for the two far conditions, with vertical
grouped limits between 4e-6 and 1.4e-4. At (64, 34) the vertical values were 395.25 at 400 and 594.07 at 600. So for the
listed (80, 40) states at the tested amplitudes the three diagnostics differ from the imposed amplitude by at most about
0.21 percent (the quoted (64, 34) vertical discrepancies are about 1 percent), against mismatches of 100 to 1100 for the
first four shapes evaluated above; no assertion is made for amplitudes that were not tested; the exact values of the independent verification for
the two a0 = 600 states agree with the binary64 values to the digits shown. The stops marked * are a property of this
solver (no decrease after twelve increases of the damping from its current value) and do not show that the state is a
local minimizer: restarts from the a0 = 600 state at (80, 40), with a0 held or free, stopped at the first iteration, so
the free run stayed at 600, and the free runs started near 400 stayed near 404. The ordering of a0 values changes with
the basis and the measure. Without the patch, at (80, 40), a0 = 600 has the smaller maximum and the smaller core residual
(dense check, r < 0.1: 4.4e-5 [5.7e-5] against 1.2e-4 [1.5e-4] for the free state). With the patch, at (64, 34), the free
run near 404 has the smallest maximum (2.95e-5 against 5.00e-5 at 600); at (80, 40) and (96, 48) the runs at 600 have
the smaller maxima (1.07e-5 against 1.87e-5 and 1.26e-5 against 1.84e-5) but at (80, 40) the larger far limit (6.3e-5
against 3.5e-5) and at both resolutions the larger root-mean-square residual (2.3e-6 against 1.23e-6, 1.05e-6 against
7.9e-7). The fits therefore do not determine a0 in the range tested, and the free runs stay near 404 while fits with a0
imposed at the tested values between 450 and 700 reach residuals of the same order at these resolutions. With the three row sets of Appendix C, Fits with rows at infinity (rows
R/min(N_Omega, N2) on the collocated range, C/N20 at 41 directions, desingularized rows at 480 points) at (80, 64) with the
core patch, three runs of at most 100 iterations were started from the a0 = 600 state d6efe320 described there (objective 9.5e-10,
solver-grid maximum 2.01e-6). With a0 free the solver stopped at the first iteration with a0 = 600.00005. With a0 held at
450 and at 800 the objective after 100 iterations was 1.1e-4 and 1.1e-6, the dense maximum of the prompt ratio for r < 1e8
6.8e-4 and 3.2e-5, the largest row value C/N20 9.5e-5 and 4.4e-5, and the desingularized maximum of R/N2 on 2440 points
with t <= 3e-3 1.0e-3 and 1.3e-4; both objectives were still decreasing (by factors of 4 and 3.5 over the last 25
iterations). All three runs start from a shape optimized at a0 = 600, so this comparison favours 600 and does not
determine a0; it shows only that a change of a0 by 150 to 200 is not absorbed by the shape within 100 iterations, and
more slowly downwards than upwards. The linearization of the free-exponent paragraph, applied to the a0 column at
(56, 30) (patch and far rows, beta held, the shape reoptimized), gives p = 1.1e-5 to 2.0e-5 and the two widths
sqrt(objective)/p = 327, 342 and 311 and sqrt(F*)/p = 31, 35 and 25 at the common start (a0 = 404.68) and at the end
states with beta = 3 (a0 = 406.85) and beta = 3.05 (a0 = 432.06). Relative to the size of the unknown these are 72 to 84
percent and 6 to 9 percent (for beta 2 to 3 percent and 0.2 percent), but the two diagnostics profile different sets of
unknowns (the beta column is projected against the shape and a0 columns, the a0 column against the shape columns with
beta held), so no ordering of the two uncertainties follows from them; the caveats of the free-exponent paragraph
apply (F* is 1/96 to 1/155 of the objective).
Exponent at fixed beta (finite comparison). Seven branches at beta = 2.50, 2.70, 2.80, 2.90, 2.95, 3.00 and 3.05 share in their ancestry
the coefficient state obtained by 60 iterations at beta = 3 from the (56, 30) core state (the common start). The nominal
settings are (J, Kw) = (56, 30), a degree 12 core patch, 8160 main and 2560 inner mixed-coordinate points and 48 separate
limiting-section rows; the main physical points depend on beta. The branches at 2.50, 2.70, 2.80, 2.90, 2.95 and 3.00 each
save 180 iterations from the common start (for 2.50 and 2.70 the actual starting arrays and the executable as run were not
archived; the saved records were checked against the documented parent and settings); the branch at 3.05 saves 60, then 120 in a new invocation. Thus the beta = 3 path has
240 iterations at its final beta including the shared prehistory, the others 180. The initial damping is 1e-3 except for
the 3.00 continuation and the 3.05 restart, which use 1e-10. These are not matched-cost comparisons. The objective
contains the rows R/min(N, N2), the limiting-section rows, the weighted row imposing h = 1 and the soft gauge row; the rms column is
R/min(N, N2) over main and inner points, and both ratio maxima include the inner points; maxfar is the largest
|sum Z_j|/sum |Z_j| over the 48 limiting-section rows, with fresh normalization and without the far-row weight; the
seconds are wall-clock time of the saved iterations (for 3.05 the sum of the two invocations).

The terminal objective ordering is 2.90, 2.80, 2.95, 3.00, 3.05, 2.70, 2.50. It does not locate a minimum of a common
continuum objective: beta changes the physical rows, the gauge target is reset on each invocation, the initial damping
differs, 3.05 includes a restart, and the costs differ. The endpoint objectives at 2.70 and 2.50 are lower than their
immediately preceding saved values and than their values 30 iterations earlier (ratios 0.93132 and 0.96755 to the
latter), while their full histories contain 5 and 14 increases of the freshly reweighted objective; this is finite
continued improvement, not a stationarity test. Zero-iteration amplitude diagnostics at these two end states (new
invocations, projected step at relative cutoff 1e-12) print projected amplitude steps about -23.8 (2.70) and -85.5
(2.50); they are linearized logged diagnostics, not realizable nonlinear shifts or uncertainties, and at 2.50 the
restarted initial objective, in [0.000707725, 0.000707735], is disjoint from the saved final objective of the
branch. The ordering of the maxima of R/N differs; among the five branches 2.80 to 3.05 the largest maxfar value
occurs at 2.90, and among all seven at 2.50. The first printed objectives after the common start was reinterpreted at 2.80, 2.90, 2.95 and 3.05 were
4.5002e3, 2.6175e3, 1.9232e3 and 1.3814e3 (before the first accepted step); the beta = 3 continuation starts at 1.7592e-5.
The 3.05 restart starts at 1.0785e-4, whose rounding interval does not contain the saved final objective of its first
segment, 1.0786473632174237e-4; the soft gauge target is reset on each invocation, a possible explanation whose size was
not evaluated. At the 2.80 end state the printed linearized beta increments are positive at all three relative SVD
cutoffs 1e-10, 1e-12, 1e-14 (+6.0506e-4, +3.2403e-3, +2.9323e-3); at 2.90 they are -2.0477e-3, +8.4607e-4, +8.5783e-4. The
saved fresh-weight objectives include eight increases at 2.80 and one at 2.90, compatible with acceptance using lagged
normalizers. These observations establish neither stationarity nor a preferred exponent. The diagnostic prints the width
sqrt(objective)/p; the width sqrt(F*)/p of the minimized projected quadratic is a different quantity. At cutoff 1e-12
the 2.80 and 2.90 beta widths of the printed kind are about 0.0573 and 0.0545; in separate amplitude diagnostics (each a
new invocation with a reset gauge target, projecting out the coefficient columns at fixed beta) the printed widths are
262.6 and 533.2, with linearized increments +121.7 and +109.1. At the 2.95 end state the beta quantities are d* = +1.8e-4,
sqrt(objective)/p = 0.058 and sqrt(F*)/p = 0.0084 (F* = 1/48 of the objective), the amplitude widths 555 and 80. These
finite surrogate diagnostics are not solution error bars. At this resolution and budget the residual is not smallest at
beta = 3; these runs locate no minimum in beta and do not separate its effect from the convergence of the shape.
Free exponent from the end state at beta = 2.90. Sixty further iterations with the same rows and beta free, from the
saved state at beta = 2.90, took 60 negative beta steps and ended at beta = 2.891978958, stored amplitude 503.7301 and
objective 7.57703e-6. This is not an eighth fixed-beta comparison. The final projected beta step has a cutoff-dependent
sign (negative at relative cutoff 1e-10, positive at 1e-12 and 1e-14); the end point is not a determined exponent.
Free exponent from the end state at beta = 3. Sixty further iterations with the same rows and beta free moved beta
from 3 to 2.9924827. All 60 increments of beta were negative, with magnitudes between 3.9719e-5 and 3.7802e-4 and
mean about 1.3e-4; a0 moved from 406.8477 to 412.5999. The objective decreased from about 1.5176e-5 to 1.4517e-5
(about 4.34 percent overall), with one increase in the saved iteration history. At the end, the frozen-weight,
retained-subspace linearization at rcond 1e-12 has minimizer shift d* = -1.3175e-4 and widths sqrt(objective)/p
about 0.0643 and sqrt(F*)/p about 0.00632; the first width raises the quadratic minimum by the current objective, the
second doubles that minimum. Other truncations give end shifts -4.3177e-3 and -2.4041e-4. This finite trajectory
continues toward smaller beta at this budget; it does not determine an exponent of the PDE or establish stationarity.
Free exponent from the end state at beta = 3.05. From the saved state at beta = 3.05, 60 further iterations with the
same rows and beta free moved beta to 3.0355566 and a0 from 432.06 to 442.08. All 60 beta increments were negative, with
magnitudes between 9.19e-5 and 6.06e-4 and mean 2.41e-4. The mean magnitude decreased from 3.54e-4 over the first ten
steps to 1.74e-4 over the last ten; individual step magnitudes were not monotone. The objective decreased from 3.736e-5
to 3.215e-5, about 14 percent, with no increase in the saved history. These beta projections use the collocation points
built at beta = 3.05 and retained throughout the run. At the end, rcond 1e-12 gives the frozen linearized displacement
d* = +6.42e-5 and width sqrt(objective)/p = 0.0756; the displacements at rcond 1e-10 and 1e-14 are -6.05e-3 and
+1.65e-4, so the displacement sign is cutoff dependent. The profiled-quadratic doubling width sqrt(F*)/p at rcond 1e-12
is about 0.00599. Neither width is a nonlinear uncertainty interval. A separate evaluation rebuilds the collocation
points at the ending exponent and resets the gauge target to the ending field: on that grid the objective is 3.176e-5
and the grid maximum 3.32e-4, against 3.215e-5 and 3.42e-4 on the original grid. Holding beta fixed on the rebuilt grid
gives |P j_a| about 1.00e-5 for the a0 column j_a and sqrt(objective)/|P j_a| about 563; this amplitude projection uses
different points and a reset gauge target from the beta projections above, and the objective difference does not
isolate the effect of changing the points. The trajectory from beta = 3 ends at 2.9924827 after 60 steps, while this one
remains above 3. Both saved trajectories move toward smaller beta throughout their budgets; neither had stopped within
its budget, and these records locate no nonlinear stationary exponent.
Free exponent at (80, 64). From the state a7e057ae, with the second implementation and a modified row set (rows of
the ratios up to t = 2e-2, 24 by 80 desingularized rows on (0, 2e-2], no rows at infinity), three runs were made. (i) Beta free, stored a0 held at 600, 60 accepted steps: all beta increments positive and none clipped, beta
from 3 to 3.0000076155, final increment 1.15e-7; the saved objective decreased at every recorded iteration and ended at
9.28388e-10, about 3.5 percent below the rounded initial value 9.62e-10. (ii) From that end, a0 also free, 40 steps:
beta 3.0000090992, stored a0 600.00974, 3 negative and 37 positive beta increments, objective 9.15446e-10. (iii) A
control with beta held at 3, from the same initial coefficients and rows, 60 steps: objective 9.28421e-10. The objective
of (i) is smaller than that of the control by relative 3.5e-5, and both round to 9.284e-10; the saved maxima of the
prompt ratio are 1.9961e-6 and 1.9921e-6 and of the grouped ratio 1.7988e-6 and 1.7997e-6 ((i), control). The budgets
are equal in iterations, not in cost (810 s and 105 s). In all 160 accepted steps the damping parameter follows the
documented recurrence from 1e-11 down to its floor 1e-12. The printed ratio of this floor to the cutoff-projected
curvature of the beta column, 1e-12/(p/|J_beta|)^2, lies between about 8 and 52 across these runs. That comparison
alone determines neither the numerator nor the denominator of the exact damped step in the beta coordinate, so it does
not show that the damping suppresses the beta motion; whether it does is open. The histories were independently
replayed from the saved records (residuals and Jacobians were not recomputed). They are finite trajectories, still
moving, and establish neither stationarity, a preferred exponent nor a uniformly small residual; the physical slope
a0/h of these states was not newly certified. At this resolution beta moved by less than 1e-5 in 100 iterations,
against 7.5e-3 in 60 iterations at (56, 30); resolution, rows, residual level and a0 all differ, so the cause of the
difference is undetermined.
Free exponent and amplitude at equal history. From the state 62df5606, with far rows to t = 2e-2, 24 by 80
desingularized rows on (0, 2e-2], the inner 128 by 80 points, the rows next to the axes, core degree 20 and the gauge
target of 62df5606, three runs of 200 least-squares iterations were made, every step accepted: a control with beta = 3
and the stored a0 = 600 held, a run with beta free and a0 held, and a run with beta and a0 free (stored functions
a93690e9, c4669ba9 and 2231dd93, Section 9). The authors' end values
are objectives 7.379e-10 (control), 7.364e-10 (beta free) and 7.364e-10 (both free; 0.199 and 0.207 percent below the
control), solver-grid maxima 1.2335e-6, 1.2323e-6 and 1.2318e-6, end exponents 2.999931 and 2.999925 and end stored
amplitude 600.0315. The readings were fixed by the authors before the runs (the time of fixing is recorded only in the
authors' own notes and was not independently established): a change of beta under 1e-3 in both free runs is read as
"beta did not move appreciably in 200 iterations from this state", a change of a0 under 2 percent as "the step of the
linearized model was not realized in 200 iterations", and objectives are compared only with the control at equal
history. Beta moved by -6.9e-5 and -7.5e-5 and log a0 by 5.2e-5, so the first two readings apply, and the free runs
attained a lower objective than the control, by 0.2 percent. The per-iteration changes decrease overall but not
monotonically: in the beta-free run 170 of 199 consecutive decrements decrease in magnitude (beta = 2.999943140378384 at
history index 150), and in the run with both free the a0 increment is largest, 7.15e-4, at history index 2 (the third
accepted update, counting from index 0) and falls to 6.01e-5 at the last (1.0e-7 in log a0). The curvature step in
beta printed at the end of that run (+6.1e-4) has the sign opposite
to the observed drift; the curvature computation has no accuracy statement, and these numbers are diagnostics. The
independent verification (closed 2026-10-21 15:57, with external review) decoded the 17118 coefficients of the three
stored functions exactly, replayed all 600 accepted history records and 123 printed checkpoints, and found h > 0
exactly for all three, so none of them is exact near the centre (Propositions 27 and 30(d)); the physical slopes a/h
are about 600.000000000004, 599.999999999991 and 600.031492. Its own evaluations (finite differences at seven step sizes
and raw multiprecision evaluations, 168 and 48 records) give at the point (x, y) = (0.03, 4.54) prompt ratios 1.2563e-6,
1.2550e-6 and 1.2546e-6 and grouped ratios 1.1421e-6, 1.1409e-6 and 1.1405e-6 (control, beta free, both free).
At this point each prompt ratio exceeds its reported solver-grid maximum (a maximum over the solver's points only), and
both normalizations exceed 1e-6. Halving its finest step increases the largest
discrepancy between its evaluations, so these values carry no error bound. The global chart and the canonical inverse were not
certified for these three stored functions. These are finite endpoints of one fitting procedure from one state: they
determine neither beta nor a0, establish no stationarity, and show neither that a0 = 600 is nor that it is not a local
optimum of the fits.

### 6.10 Summary
Each of the four least-squares states exceeds the residual target in the core by a factor of more than 100 and
fails the Taylor identity T2 (6.2, 6.3); the stored far fields of the three states for which this was evaluated fail the
compatibility relations (6.4); the finite comparisons
establish no convergence of a0 (6.5, 6.7). Three approaches were explored: collocation least squares, time-dependent dynamic
rescaling, and characteristic Newton iteration with two basis variants. None produced a state meeting the
independent full-plane residual tests. Dynamic-rescaling runs departed from their initial states and some reached
numerical stop criteria. Newton runs reduced their own closure objectives but retained large defects, and their beta
paths differed. These finite computations leave the existence question open.
The transport-exact representation of 6.9 (a generating function G of the mixed variables (x, eta), Proposition 23(b))
satisfies the temperature equation and the Taylor identities T1 and T2 identically, so only (P1) remains. Of its
states sampled independently at a common set of 10000 points, the best (134d9098: a0 held at 600, beta = 3, degrees
(96, 80), a core patch of degree 20, rows at infinity, in the intermediate far range and next to the axes, and a
fourfold denser inner collocation; the finest member of a resolution sequence from the state 62df5606 at degrees
(80, 64)) has independently sampled maxima of 9.80e-7 (prompt ratio) and 7.83e-7 (grouped ratio) at these points
(r < 1e8) and 1.089e-6 and 8.65e-7 in directed zooms next to the centre, up to 1.09 times the target, and an exact
centre prompt ratio of 1.29e-10; the finite-radius values are sampled values, not bounds (for 62df5606 the limiting
section is certified at most 2.91e-7). At the earlier setting the sampled maximum did not decrease beyond angular
degree K = 64 (it grew next to the vertical axis, a between-node effect; the added rows next to the axes and the
denser inner points reduced the observed near-axis maxima in these runs; the independent finite checks at 16 axis and
centre points per member (6.9) give no supremum over the axes and no certified truncation, inversion or rounding
bound); along the resolution sequence (64, 48), (80, 64), (96, 64), (96, 80) at equal budgets the authors' scan
maximum fell by a factor 13 and then by 16 percent and 1 percent (the independent zoom maxima of the three fine
members by 17 percent and 1.3 percent), with core degree 20 throughout. A core patch of degree 24 at (80, 64) reduced
the divided core defect at the independent core point by a factor 1.82, with the authors' largest sampled prompt ratio
unchanged (it lies next to the vertical axis at r about 5). At (96, 64) and (96, 80), raising the core degree from 20
through 24 and 28 to 32 lowered the authors' largest sampled prompt ratios (over their dense grid, polar sampling and
near-centre annulus) from 1.103e-6 to 7.00e-7, 5.80e-7 and 5.65e-7 and from 1.088e-6 to 6.22e-7, 4.24e-7 and 3.0e-7,
with the absolute vorticity residual nearly unchanged; these members are stalls of the damped iteration, independent
checks exist only at finite sets of points (6.9), and none is a candidate. The direct far-row cutoff was moved over three
decades of horizontal reach (r about 3.7e4 to 3.7e7 on the horizontal axis) with similar sampled residuals; all
members record 41 rows at infinity with weight 1 (identical under the present node rule; its use by the historical
executable is unverified), the desingularized nodes change with the cutoff, and this row-split sensitivity study is
not a sequence of full-plane fit domains (6.9).
The fits do not determine a0
(reported free-amplitude endpoints include values near 404 and 600 and other values in the exponent studies, and none
determines a profile amplitude; at (80, 40) and coarser resolutions fits at tested
imposed values from 400 to 800 reach residuals of the same order, while with the full (80, 64) rows 450 and 800 remained
substantially worse than 600 after 100 iterations from a shape optimized at 600, excursions from 62df5606 to 550, 650,
700 and 800 each ended above its own return to 600 in the objective (6.9; unconverged, the returns with twice the
history), and the linearized a0 widths at (56, 30) are 6 to 120 percent of a0 depending on the definition),
and beta is not determined at a coarser resolution (frozen-weight linearized widths 0.007 to 0.08 at residuals far
above the target, in a fixed-beta comparison not matched in cost terminal objectives ordered 2.90, 2.80, 2.95, 3.00, 3.05,
2.70, 2.50, and free-exponent iterations from 2.90, 3 and 3.05 drifting toward smaller beta without stopping), nor at
(80, 64), where, from the end states at 2.97 and 3.03 with a0 held, freeing beta moved it toward 3 from both sides
with lower objectives than fixed-exponent controls at equal history, without locating a minimum. Every finite beta = 3
member of the family with h > 0 fails (P1) near the centre (6.9), as does, in the free-exponent form, every member
with h > 0 at any beta > 2 (Proposition 30), so each beta = 3 fit has a
nonzero residual (exact nonzero centre defects are certified only for the states identified with such
certificates; for the others the exact check is h > 0), but this supplies no positive
residual floor uniform over coefficients and degrees. No state of either representation currently meets the numerical-YES
verification package of Section 10.6; the missing full-plane domain sequence and the inadequate determination of beta
prevent acceptance; holding the amplitude restricts the search and is disclosed as such (the axis checks are finite,
at 16 points per member), and near-target
sampled maxima and nonzero defects of individual finite approximations neither establish nor by themselves disqualify
numerical existence evidence.
