   G1 = -5 a0 h51/((beta + 2)(4 beta + 5)),   G2 = -3 a0 h33/(2 beta (4 beta - 3)),
   G1 = -20 h51 - 6 h33,   G2 = -6 h33 - 20 h15,
together with (4 beta + 5) G1 = 4 u41, (4 beta - 3) G2 = 2 u23 and, from the coefficient of y^5 in the degree-5 part
of (P2), 4 b u05 + a0 h15 = 0. As in Step 7 of A.36, G1 <= 0 and G2 <= 0. Since a0 < 0, the first two relations give
h51 <= 0 and h33 <= 0, and then the third gives G1 >= 0; so G1 = 0, -20 h51 - 6 h33 = 0 with both terms nonnegative,
h51 = h33 = 0, G2 = 0 and h15 = 0, and then u41 = u23 = u05 = 0. Hence Omega_4 = 0, Theta_5 = 0 and Psi_6 = 0; by the
parities Omega, Theta and Psi contain only monomials of even, odd and even degree, which gives the stated orders.
Step 5 ((e)). Let A = 0. Then B = -gamma cos(phi) F + sin(phi) F', and by Theorem 15(c) r^(2 delta) Omega(r, .) -> B
uniformly, so B <= 0 on [0, pi/2]. By Step 2, B'(0) = 2 delta F'(0) < 0, so B < 0 on (0, phi1) for some phi1 > 0. On

The function F(phi)/sin(phi) is continuous on [0, pi/2] with value F'(0) < 0 at 0 and negative elsewhere, and F is

sin(phi)). By Theorem 15(b), f_R -> F in C^1([0, pi]) as R -> inf; since f_R and F vanish at 0 and
pi, |f_R - F| <= epsilon_R min(phi, pi - phi) <= epsilon_R (pi/2) sin(phi) on [0, pi] with epsilon_R -> 0, so f_R < 0
on (0, pi) for R >= R1, that is, Theta < 0 on {y > 0, r >= R1}. Let y > 0 at X and suppose Theta(X) > 0. The forward
orbit Phi_t X of W exists for all t >= 0 (W is smooth with |W(X)| <= C_W (1 + |X|)) and stays in {y > 0}, which is
invariant since W2(x, 0) = 0. By (P2), Theta(Phi_t X) = e^(b t) Theta(X) -> inf as t -> inf; since Theta is bounded on
{r <= R1}, |Phi_t X| > R1 for large t, where Theta < 0, a contradiction. Hence Theta <= 0 on {y > 0}.
For the strict sign put f = -Theta >= 0 on {y > 0} and suppose f(X0) = 0 for some X0 with y > 0. By Proposition 33(a),
tau = a0 V/(a xi) < 0 on (0, inf); tau is even and tau(0) = a0 < 0, so Theta_y(x, 0) < 0 for every real x, and since
Theta(x, 0) = 0 there is mu in (0, 1) with Theta < 0 on {|x| <= R1, 0 < y <= mu}. Hence f > 0 on the boundary of the
rectangle Rc = (-R1 - 1, R1 + 1) x (mu/2, R1 + 1), whose closure lies in {y > 0}, and every zero of f in {y > 0} lies
in Rc; choose 0 < lambda0 < min f over the boundary of Rc and put N(lambda) = {X in Rc : f(X) < lambda}. By (P2),
f(Phi_t X) = e^(b t) f(X) for all real t. If X is in N(lambda) with 0 < lambda <= lambda0, then
f(Phi_(-s) X) < lambda0 for all s >= 0, so the backward orbit cannot meet the boundary of Rc and stays in Rc;
similarly, if X is in N(lambda e^(-b t)), then Phi_s X stays in Rc for 0 <= s <= t. Hence Phi_(-t)(N(lambda0)) =
N(lambda0 e^(-b t)) for t >= 0. Since div W = 2 beta, the flow map Phi_(-t) multiplies areas by e^(-2 beta t),
so |N(lambda)| = (lambda/lambda0)^(2 beta/b) |N(lambda0)| for 0 < lambda <= lambda0, with |N(lambda0)| finite. On the
other hand f is smooth and nonnegative near X0 with f(X0) = 0, so grad f(X0) = 0 and f(X) <= M |X - X0|^2 on a disk
around X0 in Rc; so N(lambda) contains a disk of radius (lambda/M)^(1/2) and |N(lambda)| >= pi lambda/M for small
lambda > 0. Since 2 beta/b = 2 + 4/b > 1, the two statements contradict each other as lambda -> 0. Hence Theta < 0 on
{y > 0}. As Theta is odd in y and a0 < 0, a0 y Theta > 0 for y != 0, and Proposition 24(a) gives that the backward
basin of the origin is R^2.

The independent verification checked Proposition 36 with its own proof in two steps. For the first draft (parts (a) to

exponent condition and the compact enclosure are needed. Its finite diagnostics are its own (43 exact symbolic records
and 6 scalar weighted examples for the first draft; 27 exact symbolic or positivity checks and 4 scalar transport
examples for the second); the authors' scripts were read as data and not executed. No profile, no realization of the
centre or angular data and no exclusion of the class is asserted.

negative on (0, G(x)), Omega_y(x, G(x)) >= 0. Since Omega(x, 0) = 0 and Omega(x, y) < 0 for 0 < y < G(x),

G(x)/x < tan(phi* + eps).

Step 7 ((g)). Assume the backward basin is R^2 and Omega_y > 0 on the graph. By the implicit function theorem and (a),

some t0, and forward invariance gives Omega(X) >= 0, a contradiction. For the last statement, let Theta_x >= 0

of {Z > 0} containing y0, which therefore contains [y0, inf); so Z >= Z(y0) on [y0, inf) and -c_v alpha = lim Z > 0.

2 e^(mu t), so h(t) = -(lambda + 1) e^(lambda t) + 2 (mu + 1) e^(mu t), e^t o(t) -> 0 as t -> -inf and

### A.39 Proposition 38 (one sign change of Theta_x on vertical lines)

Statement: Section 3, after Proposition 37. Notation: as in the statement and in A.34 to A.36 and A.38.

Throughout, beta > 2, so b > 0, 0 < delta < 1/2, 0 < gamma < 1 and 3/2 < d < 2; a = beta + 2. Write P_T = Theta_x. In

so int_0^L sin(d phi) A dphi = 0; since sin(d phi) > 0 on (0, L] (d L < pi) and A < 0 on (0, eps), A > 0 somewhere.
Let g < 0. By Proposition 37(c), a0 C > 0, s < 0 and z < 0 on some (0, eps), and by Proposition 37(d), C < 0 and s > 0
somewhere, so y_C and y_s are positive and finite. If s(y1) < 0, then P_T(x, y1) < 0 for small x > 0, so
G_T(x) > y1; if s(y2) > 0, then G_T(x) < y2 for small x. Hence ell_s <= liminf G_T(x) and limsup G_T(x) <= y_s as
x -> 0+; in the same way, from Omega(x, y)/x -> z(y) and the definition of G, ell_z <= liminf G(x) and
limsup G(x) <= y_z. On (0, y_C), a0 C >= 0, so S' = -a0 b P C <= 0; since S = I_s s < 0 near 0, S < 0 on
(0, y_C] and, by continuity, on (0, y_C + eps1) for some eps1 > 0. On (0, y_s), s <= 0, so Z' = E_v s/Y <= 0; since
Z < 0 near 0, Z < 0 on (0, y_s] and on (0, y_s + eps2) for some eps2 > 0. Hence s < 0 at some height above y_C and
z < 0 at some height above y_s, that is ell_s > y_C and ell_z > y_s. This proves the chain
of inequalities, and liminf G(x) >= ell_z > y_s >= limsup G_T(x) gives G_T(x) < G(x) for small x > 0. Finally,
s(y_s) = 0 (s <= 0 on (0, y_s) and s > 0 at heights arbitrarily close to y_s from above), s'(y_s) >= 0 and
z(y_s) < 0 (Z(y_s) < 0); at y_s the equation Y s' + (3 beta + 2 - 2 Y') s = T' (z + Y'') of Proposition 34(a) gives
Y'' = Y s'/T' - z > 0, and Y'' = U2_yy(0, .).
Step 9 ((d)). Let g = 0, (G1, G2) != (0, 0) and a0 < D4. By Proposition 37(c), Psi = -2 x y + O(|X|^6),
Omega = G1 x^3 y + G2 x y^3 + O(|X|^6), G1 < 0 and K G2 = (a0 - D4) G1 with K > 0, so G2 > 0. With
W = (a x, b y) + O(|X|^5), the terms of degree 4 in (P1) give
   Theta_x = ((4 beta + 4) + 1) G1 x^3 y + ((4 beta - 4) + 1) G2 x y^3 + O(|X|^6)
           = x y ((4 beta + 5) G1 x^2 + (4 beta - 3) G2 y^2) + O(|X|^6)
(Theta_x is odd in x and in y, so it has no terms of degree 5). Since Omega and Theta_x are smooth and odd in each
variable, Omega = x y Om~ and Theta_x = x y P~ with Om~ and P~ smooth and even in each variable, and the Taylor
polynomials of Om~ and P~ are those of Omega and Theta_x divided by x y; hence
   Omega/(x y) = G1 x^2 + G2 y^2 + O(r^4),   Theta_x/(x y) = (4 beta + 5) G1 x^2 + (4 beta - 3) G2 y^2 + O(r^4),
and Omega/(x y r^2) = G1 cos(phi)^2 + G2 sin(phi)^2 + O(r^2) and Theta_x/(x y r^2) = (4 beta + 5) G1
cos(phi)^2 + (4 beta - 3) G2 sin(phi)^2 + O(r^2), uniformly in phi. For fixed 0 < t1 < mu < t2, the points (x, t1 x)
and (x, t2 x) with small x > 0 have Omega < 0 and Omega > 0 respectively, so t1 < G(x)/x < t2; thus G(x)/x -> mu, and
in the same way G_T(x)/x -> nu = mu ((4 beta + 5)/(4 beta - 3))^(1/2). Since 4 beta + 5 > 4 beta - 3 > 0, nu > mu, and
G_T(x) > G(x) for small x > 0.
Step 10 ((e)). In class ST<, the zeros of Omega in Q1 are the points (x, G(x)), and G(x) > G_T(x), so
Theta_x(x, G(x)) > 0. Along a trajectory, (P1) gives d/dt Omega = Theta_x - Omega, which is positive at every time at
which the trajectory is on {Omega = 0} intersected with Q1. If Omega(X(t0)) > 0 and Omega(X(t1)) <= 0 for some
t1 > t0, let t* be the first time after t0 with Omega(X(t*)) = 0; then Omega(X(t)) > 0 on (t0, t*) and
d/dt Omega(X(t*)) > 0, which is impossible. So {Omega > 0} intersected with Q1 is forward invariant. If
Omega(X) < 0 and Omega(Phi_(-t) X) >= 0 for some t > 0, then either Omega(Phi_(-t) X) > 0, or Omega(Phi_(-t) X) = 0
and Omega > 0 slightly later along the trajectory; in both cases forward invariance gives Omega(X) > 0, a
contradiction. Finally, if J_T(phi1) < 0 and A(phi2) > 0 with phi1 >= phi2, then for large x, by Theorem 11(b),
P_T(x, x tan(phi1)) < 0 and Omega(x, x tan(phi2)) > 0, so x tan(phi2) <= x tan(phi1) < G_T(x) < G(x) < x tan(phi2),
which is absurd.
Remark 1 (angular data). For beta = 3 and 0 < c < 2, the data A_c, F and H_c of A.38, Remark 2 give
J_T = gamma cos(phi) F - sin(phi) F' = -(1/3) sin(4 phi), negative on (0, pi/4) and positive on (pi/4, pi/2); F > 0 on
(0, pi/2], F(pi/2) = 1, F'(0) = 2, sigma = 4/3 > 0, A_c'(0) = -2 c - 4 < 0 and alpha = 2 c - 4 < 0, and A_c changes
sign once, at phi_c in (pi/4, pi/2) with cos(2 phi_c) = -c/2. They meet the restrictions of (a), (c) and (e) on F, J_T
and A: no positive value of J_T before a negative one, F > 0 on (0, L], F'(0) > 0, p < 0, sigma >= 0, alpha < 0, A of
both signs and every angle with J_T < 0 below every angle with A > 0 (since sigma > 0, the condition m <= alpha of (c)
does not apply). These are angular data only: no centre, axis integral, higher far-field order or profile is matched.
Symbolic checks of the displayed identities: by the authors, not part of the proof.
The independent verification checked the second draft of Proposition 38 with its own proof (parts (a) to (e) and
Remark 1): in class T, a0 > 0, V > 0, tau > 0, U1_x(x, 0) <= 2, p < 0, branch (i), F > 0 on (0, L] and Theta > 0 on
the open upper half-plane, the area contradiction obtained from compact positive-level sublevel sets without
integration over a singular zero set, and the whole plane as backward basin by Proposition 24(a), used after the
positivity of Theta; the continuity of G_T, the ordering of s and J_T, the ray limits, Theta_y > 0 and W2 > 0 on the
graph, the crossing formula where Theta_xy > 0 and, when g < 0 and Theta_xy > 0 on the whole graph, a point of the
graph with U2_x < 0, by local Lipschitz bounds along orbit segments and without a global bound on the derivative of
G_T; in class ST, sigma >= 0, the two alternatives for alpha, the chain of thresholds with extended-real endpoints,

intervals of zeros; the reversed slopes of the two nodal graphs at a degenerate centre with a nonzero quartic block
and a0 < D4; and Remark 1 as angular data only. Its finite diagnostics are its own (17 exact symbolic identities). For
the Reading it recomputed nine vertical lines, three for each of the three stored states, with 18000 retained samples:
each sampled field has exactly one negative-to-positive reversal, no reverse reversal and no zero sample, and every
bracket of the Theta_x reversal lies strictly below the corresponding bracket of the Omega reversal; the 84 transcript
lines of the authors (28 per state) were confirmed as saved records of the authors, not as independent evaluations. A
later independent check confirmed the third draft, the text above, conditionally in the same class: among the proof
steps only Step 8 changed, where for Z' = E_v s/Y the positive multiplier and the extension Z(0) = 0 give the
monotonicity also when y_s = 0 and s has intervals of zeros; the assertion on U2_x is read with g < 0 and Theta_xy > 0
at every point of the graph G_T. No profile, no realization of the classes T, ST or ST< and no exclusion of these
classes as a whole is asserted.

### A.40 Proposition 39 (far-field separation of the two nodal graphs in class ST<)

Statement: Section 3, after Proposition 38. Notation: as in the statement and in A.38 and A.39.

Throughout, beta > 2 (Corollary 4), so 0 < delta < 1/2, 0 < gamma < 1 and 3/2 < d < 2; write P_T = Theta_x,
V_r = -H', V_phi = d H and, along a trajectory, rho = r^(-delta). In class S a point of Q1 with Omega > 0 has
y > G(x) and one with Omega < 0 has y < G(x); in class T a point of Q1 with P_T > 0 has y > G_T(x). Hence in class
ST< every point of Q1 with Omega > 0 satisfies y > G(x) > G_T(x), so P_T > 0 there. By
Proposition 38(a), F > 0 on (0, L]. By Theorem 15(a), F, A and V, hence H = V_phi/d, are C^infinity. By the A1
parity (2.2), A is odd about 0 and about L, hence so is the unique periodic solution H of -H'' - d^2 H = A; so
H(0) = H(L) = 0, and H restricted to [0, L] is the unique solution of this equation with these boundary values
(sin(d L) != 0).
Step 1 (two-term expansion of Theta_x). By Theorem 11(b), uniformly in phi, r^delta Omega -> A and
r^(2 delta) P_T -> J_T. By Theorem 15(c) with k = 1, r^(-gamma) Theta = F + r^(-delta) F_1 + R_1 with
F_1 = gamma V_r F + V_phi F' and R_1 = o(r^(-delta)) in C^1(S^1), and r^(-(1 - delta)) U = V + O(r^(-delta))
uniformly. In polar coordinates (P2) reads (beta r + U_r) Theta_r + (U_phi/r) Theta_phi = (beta - 2) Theta, so for
large r
   Theta_r = ((beta - 2) Theta - (U_phi/r) Theta_phi)/(beta r + U_r),
   r^(1 - gamma) Theta_r = gamma F + r^(-delta) (gamma - delta) F_1 + o(r^(-delta))
uniformly: expanding the quotient, the coefficient of r^(-delta) is gamma F_1 - delta (gamma V_r F + V_phi F') =
(gamma - delta) F_1, since (beta - 2)/beta = gamma. No radial derivative of R_1 is used. With
Theta_phi = r^gamma (F' + r^(-delta) F_1' + o(r^(-delta))) and P_T = cos(phi) Theta_r - sin(phi) Theta_phi/r,
   r^(2 delta) P_T = J_T + r^(-delta) J_1 + o(r^(-delta)) uniformly, J_1 = (gamma - delta) cos(phi) F_1 - sin(phi) F_1'.
                                                                                                               (1)
Step 2 (an identity for J_1). Put theta_0 = r^gamma F and u_0 = r^(1 - delta) (V_r e_r + V_phi e_phi). In Cartesian
components grad theta_0 = r^(-2 delta) (J_T, K_T), u_0 . grad theta_0 = r^(gamma - delta) F_1, and
d_x (r^(gamma - delta) F_1) = r^(-3 delta) J_1, since gamma - delta - 1 = -3 delta. Write d_x u_0 = r^(-delta)
(D_1, D_2) with D_1, D_2 functions of phi. Differentiating u_0 . grad theta_0 in x by the product rule and comparing
the coefficients of r^(-3 delta) gives
   J_1 = (D_1 - 2 delta V_r) J_T + V_phi J_T' + D_2 K_T.                                                       (2)
From (u_0)_2 = r^(1 - delta) (d H cos(phi) - H' sin(phi)), d_x = cos(phi) d_r - (sin(phi)/r) d_phi,
H'' = -d^2 H - A and d - 1 = 1 - delta one finds D_2 = M; by Theorem 15(b), r^delta U2_x -> M uniformly. At a zero
theta in (0, L) of J_T, sin(theta) F'(theta) = gamma cos(theta) F(theta), so K_T(theta) = gamma F(theta)/sin(theta) > 0
and, by (2),
   J_1(theta) - V_phi(theta) J_T'(theta) = M(theta) K_T(theta).                                                (3)
Step 3 (an outgoing trajectory with a prescribed limit angle). Since |U| <= C r^(1 - delta) for large r, there is R0
such that r' = beta r + U_r >= beta r/2 and |phi'| = |U_phi|/r <= C r^(-delta) along trajectories of W where r >= R0.
The flow of W is complete (Proposition 24), and a trajectory starting at radius R >= R0 therefore stays outside that
circle, r(t) >= R e^(beta t/2), and its angle has a limit phi(inf) with |phi(inf) - phi(0)| <= C1 R^(-delta)
(C1 = 2 C, as beta delta = 1). Given theta in (0, L), choose eps > 0 with [theta - 2 eps, theta + 2 eps] contained in
(0, L) and R >= R0 with C1 R^(-delta) < eps/2. On the circle of radius R the limit angle is a continuous function of
the initial angle (the flow is continuous over finite times and the remaining angular change after time t is at most
C1 (R e^(beta t/2))^(-delta), uniformly), and the initial angles theta - eps and theta + eps have limit angles below
and above theta; by the intermediate value theorem some trajectory X(t) starting on that circle has phi(t) -> theta.
It stays in Q1, which is invariant (A.39). Along it, rho' = -delta rho (beta + U_r/r) = -rho + O(rho^2), and
rho(s) <= rho(t) e^(-(s - t)/2) for s >= t, since r(s) >= r(t) e^(beta (s - t)/2) and beta delta = 1. Hence rho is
integrable, (log(e^t rho))' = O(rho) gives e^t rho(t) -> kappa in (0, inf), and integrating rho' = -rho + O(rho^2)
from t to inf, with int_t^inf rho(s)^2 ds = O(rho(t)^2), gives int_t^inf rho(s) ds = rho(t) + O(rho(t)^2). Since
phi' = U_phi/r = rho V_phi(phi) + O(rho^2) and V_phi(phi(s)) -> V_phi(theta), integration from t to inf gives
   phi(t) = theta - V_phi(theta) rho(t) + o(rho(t)).                                                          (4)
Step 4 ((a), and the strict sign at a separating zero). Let theta in (0, L) with A(theta) = 0 and X(t) as in Step 3.
By (P1), d/dt (e^t Omega(X(t))) = e^t P_T(X(t)), and e^t Omega(X(t)) = e^t rho(t) (A(phi(t)) + o(1)) ->
kappa A(theta) = 0. Suppose that P_T(X(t)) < 0 for all t >= t1 and that e^t P_T(X(t)) is integrable on (t1, inf).
Then
   Omega(X(t)) = -e^(-t) int_t^inf e^s P_T(X(s)) ds > 0  for t >= t1,
while P_T(X(t)) < 0, against the implication Omega > 0 => P_T > 0 of class ST<. If J_T(theta) < 0, then
P_T(X(t)) = rho^2 (J_T(theta) + o(1)) by Theorem 11(b), negative for large t, and e^t P_T = O(e^t rho^2) = O(e^(-t)):
the contradiction proves (a). If J_T(theta) = 0, then J_T(phi(t)) = J_T'(theta) (phi(t) - theta) + O(rho^2) =
-J_T'(theta) V_phi(theta) rho + o(rho) by (4), and (1) and (3) give
   P_T(X(t)) = rho^3 [J_1(theta) - V_phi(theta) J_T'(theta) + o(1)] = rho^3 [M(theta) K_T(theta) + o(1)];
so J_T(theta) = 0 is impossible wherever M(theta) < 0, by the same contradiction (now e^t P_T = O(e^(-2 t))).
Step 5 (the separating angle theta_A and the sign of M). By Proposition 38(c), A < 0 on some (0, eps0) and A > 0 at
some point of (0, L); by Proposition 37(a), there are no angles phi1 < phi2 with A(phi1) > 0 > A(phi2). Hence
eps0 <= theta_A <= phi for every phi with A(phi) > 0, so 0 < theta_A < L. By definition A >= 0 on (theta_A, L]; a
positive value of A in (0, theta_A) would precede negative values arbitrarily close below theta_A, so A <= 0 on
(0, theta_A); by continuity A(theta_A) = 0. For 0 < theta < L put I_-(theta) = int_0^theta sin(d u) A(u) du and
I_+(theta) = int_theta^L sin(d (L - u)) A(u) du. Then
   H(theta) = [sin(d (L - theta)) I_-(theta) + sin(d theta) I_+(theta)]/(d sin(d L)),
   H'(theta) = [-cos(d (L - theta)) I_-(theta) + cos(d theta) I_+(theta)]/sin(d L)
(direct differentiation, the terms in A(theta) cancelling, gives -H'' - d^2 H = A, and the right side of the first
formula vanishes at 0 and at L, so it is the Dirichlet solution). Since 0 < d L < pi, sin(d L) > 0 and the weights
sin(d u), sin(d (L - u)) are positive for 0 < u < L; at theta_A, A <= 0 on [0, theta_A] with A < 0 near 0 gives
I_- < 0, and A >= 0 on [theta_A, L] with a positive value gives I_+ > 0. As A(theta_A) = 0, M(theta_A) = (1 - delta)
(d cos(2 theta) H - sin(2 theta) H') at theta = theta_A. By the formulas for H and H' and the addition formulas,
   sin(d L) (d cos(2 theta) H - sin(2 theta) H') = sin(d (L - theta) + 2 theta) I_- + sin(d theta - 2 theta) I_+,
and d L = pi - delta L, d - 2 = -delta give sin(d L) = sin(delta L), sin(d (L - theta) + 2 theta) =
sin(delta (L - theta)) and sin(d theta - 2 theta) = -sin(delta theta). This is the formula for M(theta_A) in (b).
Since 0 < delta L < pi/4, 0 < delta theta_A < pi/4 and 0 < delta (L - theta_A) < pi/4, all three sines are positive,
and I_- < 0 < I_+ gives M(theta_A) < 0. By (a), J_T(theta_A) >= 0, and by Step 4, J_T(theta_A) != 0. This proves (b).
Step 6 ((c)). J_T is continuous with J_T(theta_A) > 0, so J_T > 0 on (theta_A - eta, theta_A] for some eta in
(0, theta_A). By the definition of theta_A there is phi2 in (theta_A - eta, theta_A) with A(phi2) < 0; choose phi1 in
(theta_A - eta, phi2). By Theorem 11(b) there is x0 > 0 such that P_T(x, x tan(phi1)) > 0 and
Omega(x, x tan(phi2)) < 0 for x >= x0, so G_T(x) < x tan(phi1) and x tan(phi2) < G(x). Take k1 = tan(phi1) and
k2 = tan(phi2).
Remark 1 (angular data at the boundary of (b)). For beta = 3 and 0 <= c < 2 let A_c = -c sin(2 phi) - sin(4 phi),
F = sin(phi) (1 + cos(phi)^2) and H_c = -(9 c/11) sin(2 phi) - (9/119) sin(4 phi) (A.38, Remark 2, there with
0 < c < 2; H_c solves -H_c'' - (25/9) H_c = A_c also for c = 0). Then
J_T = -(1/3) sin(4 phi), A_c < 0 on (0, phi_c) and A_c > 0 on (phi_c, pi/2) with cos(2 phi_c) = -c/2, so
theta_A = phi_c. For 0 < c < 2, phi_c lies in (pi/4, pi/2) and J_T(phi_c) = (c/3) sin(2 phi_c) > 0, so (b) holds.
For c = 0, phi_0 = pi/4 and J_T(pi/4) = 0, while F and J_T are as in A.39, Remark 1, A_0'(0) = A_0'(L) = -4 (so
p < 0 and alpha < 0), A_0 has both signs and every angle with J_T < 0 lies below every angle with A_0 > 0: these
data meet every restriction of Proposition 38(a), (c) and (e) on F, J_T and A listed in A.39, Remark 1, and (b)
excludes them. Here M(pi/4) = -24/119, K_T(pi/4) = 1/2, and
the coefficient M K_T of Step 4 is -12/119. These are angular data only: no centre, axis integral, higher far-field
order or profile is matched. Symbolic checks of the displayed identities: by the authors, not part of the proof.
The independent verification checked Proposition 39 with its own complete proof, written before its symbolic checks,
for exact smooth profiles in class ST< (the strict signs of Omega and Theta_x on the two sides of the graphs G and
G_T, with G_T < G), with the far-field results of Theorems 11 and 15 and the sign results of Propositions 37 and 38 as
stated dependencies, each checked independently before. It obtained the first correction of Theta_x on rays, with the
coefficient (gamma - delta) F_1, by solving the transport equation for the radial derivative, without a radial
derivative of a remainder; the product-rule identity that gives M as the limit of r^delta U2_x and J_1 - V_phi
J_T' = M K_T at an interior zero of J_T; for each theta in (0, L) an outgoing trajectory with limiting angle theta,
along which e^t rho tends to a positive limit and, when A(theta) = 0, e^t Omega -> 0, so that a zero of A with
J_T < 0, or with J_T = 0 and M < 0, contradicts the implication from Omega > 0 to Theta_x > 0; this gives (a), and
with the Green formulas for H and H', which give I_- < 0 < I_+ and M(theta_A) < 0, it gives (b); and the two fixed
rays of (c), from an interval ending at theta_A on which J_T > 0 and which contains an angle with A < 0. No assumption
g < 0, no transverse crossing of either graph and no nondegenerate graph is used, and the argument holds also when A
vanishes to infinite order at theta_A or on an interval. The example of the Reading and Remark 1 were checked as
angular data only. Its symbolic checks are its own (28 executed assertions on the algebra; consistency checks, not
part of the proof and not a count of independent verifications). Its proof was written for the first draft; it
confirmed the transfer of the statement and of the proof to the third draft, the text above, conditionally in class
ST<. No profile, no realization of class ST< and no exclusion of that class as a whole is asserted.

### A.41 Proposition 40 (asymptotic slope of the vorticity nodal graph in class ST<)

Statement: Section 3, after Proposition 39. Notation: as in the statement and in A.40. The argument was found by the
independent verifier.

As in A.40, in class S a point of Q1 with Omega > 0 lies above the graph of G and one with Omega < 0 lies below it, and
on a fixed ray of angle phi in (0, L) the point at radius r is (x, x tan(phi)) with x = r cos(phi).
Step 1 ((a)). By Step 5 of A.40, 0 < theta_A < L, A <= 0 on [0, theta_A], A >= 0 on [theta_A, L], and theta_A <= phi
for every phi in (0, L) with A(phi) > 0; such angles exist (Proposition 38(c)). The set O_+ = {phi in (0, L) :
A(phi) > 0} is therefore open, nonempty and contained in [theta_A, L), so theta_A <= theta_+ < L. Since
theta_+ >= theta_A > 0 and O_+ is open, theta_+ does not lie in O_+, so A <= 0 on (0, theta_+]. With A >= 0 on
[theta_A, L] this gives A = 0 on [theta_A, theta_+]. Every angle of O_+ exceeds theta_+, and O_+ contains angles
arbitrarily close to theta_+.
Step 2 ((b)). Let theta in [theta_A, theta_+]. By Step 1, A(theta) = 0, A <= 0 on [0, theta], A >= 0 on [theta, L],
A < 0 on some interval (0, eps0) with eps0 <= theta_A (Proposition 38(c) and Step 5 of A.40), and A > 0 at some point
of (theta, L). As in Step 5 of A.40, the weights sin(d u) and sin(d (L - u)) are positive for 0 < u < L, so
I_-(theta) < 0 < I_+(theta). The Green formula for H and H' and the addition formulas in Step 5 of A.40 hold at every
theta in (0, L), and A(theta) = 0 removes the term sin(theta)^2 A(theta) of M; hence
   M(theta) = (1 - delta) [sin(delta (L - theta)) I_-(theta) - sin(delta theta) I_+(theta)]/sin(delta L) < 0.
By Proposition 39(a), J_T(theta) >= 0. By Step 4 of A.40, applied at the zero theta of A, J_T(theta) = 0 is impossible
since M(theta) < 0. Hence J_T(theta) > 0.
Step 3 ((c), upper bound). Let phi in O_+. By Theorem 11(b), r^delta Omega(r, phi) -> A(phi) > 0, so
Omega(x, x tan(phi)) > 0 for all large x; hence G(x) < x tan(phi) for all large x and limsup G(x)/x <= tan(phi). By
Step 1, phi can be taken arbitrarily close to theta_+, so limsup G(x)/x <= tan(theta_+).
Step 4 ((c), lower bound). If theta_A = theta_+, the definition of theta_A gives angles phi < theta_A arbitrarily close
to theta_A with A(phi) < 0; by Theorem 11(b), Omega(x, x tan(phi)) < 0 for all large x, so x tan(phi) < G(x) and
liminf G(x)/x >= tan(phi), hence liminf G(x)/x >= tan(theta_A) = tan(theta_+). If theta_A < theta_+, let phi in
(theta_A, theta_+). Then A = 0 near phi, so A(phi) = A'(phi) = 0 (A is smooth by Theorem 15(a)), and the coefficient
B = -delta V_r A + V_phi A' - gamma cos(phi) F + sin(phi) F' of Theorem 15(c) satisfies B(phi) = -J_T(phi) < 0 by (b).
By Theorem 15(c) with k = 0, r^delta Omega(r, phi) = A(phi) + r^(-delta) B(phi) + o(r^(-delta)), so
Omega(r, phi) = r^(-2 delta) (B(phi) + o(1)) < 0 for all large r; hence x tan(phi) < G(x) for all large x and
liminf G(x)/x >= tan(phi). Letting phi tend to theta_+ gives liminf G(x)/x >= tan(theta_+). With Step 3 this proves
(c).
The independent verification checked Proposition 40 with its own complete proof, written before the authors' text and
before its symbolic checks, with the hypotheses and dependencies of Proposition 39: theta_A <= theta_+ and A = 0 on
the whole interval [theta_A, theta_+], also when it has positive length; M < 0 and J_T > 0 at every angle of that
interval, by the Green formulas and the terminal identity of A.40; the first correction B = -J_T - delta V_r A + V_phi
A' of r^delta Omega on rays, obtained without differentiating a remainder, equals -J_T < 0 inside the interval, so
that every ray inside it eventually lies below the vorticity nodal graph and the limit of G(x)/x is tan(theta_+), at
the right end; and limsup G_T(x)/x < tan(theta_A) <= lim G(x)/x, with no limit of G_T(x)/x. Under additional
simple-zero hypotheses it also derived first-order corrections of the two graphs, which are not part of
Proposition 40. Its symbolic checks are its own (23 executed assertions on the algebra; consistency checks, not part
of the proof). It confirmed the transfer of its statement and argument to the third draft, the text above,
conditionally in class ST<. No profile, no realization of class ST< and no exclusion of that class as a whole is
asserted.

## Appendix C. Development of the row set in the mixed coordinates

This appendix reproduces the part of Section 6.9 that describes the development of the row set between the axis
amplitude diagnostic and the paragraph "Core degree 20, rows next to the axes and denser inner points", with two
corrections: one corrected remark on the comparison of two evaluators (paragraph "Desingularized evaluation at large
radius"), and corrected statements of node lists and of their provenance after an independent replay of the printed
logs, as recorded in Appendix B (entry closed 17:03Z on 2026-10-21). The table in 6.9 (paragraph "Development of the
row set") summarizes it. Positional references in it refer to its original place
in Section 6.9: "above" means the earlier paragraphs of this appendix or of 6.9, "below" the later paragraphs of this
appendix or of 6.9, and "next paragraph" at its end means the paragraph "Core degree 20, rows next to the axes and denser
inner points" of 6.9.

Core patch and fits controlling both ratios. Near the centre the (t, w) square also represents points with x^2 < 0
(x^2 = -w^3 at t = 1), so near the centre the polynomial P also has to represent values of G at imaginary x; we
offer this as a possible interpretation of the slow resolution of the core region, not as an established cause. Localized
functions x eta E^(1/3) exp(-(x^2 + eta^2)/L^2) T_i(2 xi - 1) T_j(2 zeta - 1), xi = x^2/(R^2 + x^2),
zeta = eta^2/(R^2 + eta^2) (R = 0.1, L = 0.4, i, j <= 12 or 16), whose variables cover only the physical quadrant, were
added to the basis. They are analytic and even in x and eta inside the bracket, and in physical variables they are smaller
at infinity than every inverse power of r together with all their derivatives (about exp(-c r^(2/3)) along vertical
rays, where eta grows like r^(1/3)), so the centre normalization (the row h = 1 now includes their centre values) and the
far-field class are unchanged. Without further collocation points the patch overfitted: a first run at (56, 30) lowered
the solver-grid maximum from 3.1e-4 to 1.4e-4, but a denser check including rows next to the axes gave 4.6e-3 in the
strip eta < 0.009 next to the horizontal axis at 0.1 < x < 0.5, which that grid does not sample. With 2560 added
collocation points on a polar grid in (x, eta) (radii 1e-3 to 2) and rows R/min(N_Omega, N2) on a grid reaching E^(-1/6)
of about 4e-4, an l = 2 (56, 30) state continued for 35 stored iterations (labels 0 to 34) stopped with a0 = 400.509 and

Desingularized evaluation at large radius. In binary64 the evaluation of R at large r subtracts O(r^2) terms in Psi and
cancels leading orders in R and N2, and collocation ends at a finite radius, while the exact far limit concerns t = 0 only;
the range between was not examined by either. A second evaluator removes both limitations. For the outer basis with
exponent beta (m = beta/(beta - 2), q = 2M(beta - 2)) put x = l xh, eta = s_e l^(1/m) eh, sigma = l^(-1/beta). Then
G(x, eta) = l^2 s_e g(xh, eh, sigma) identically in l, with g = xh eh Eh^(1/beta) P(tau(t), w),
Eh = xh^2 + (sigma^q + eh^(2M))^(m/M), t = sigma Eh^(-1/(2 beta)), w = eh^2 Eh^(-1/m). If f(x, eta) = l^k F(xh, eh, sigma)
identically in l, then D f = l^k (beta k - sigma d_sigma) F for D = beta x d_x + (beta - 2) eta d_eta; hence
Psi = (D - 2 beta) G = l^2 sigma phi with phi = -s_e g_sigma, and Omega = sigma om with om = -(Dxh^2 + Dyh^2) phi, where
Dxh = d_xh - ghat d_eh, Dyh = (s_e g_xh,eh)^(-1) d_eh and ghat = g_xh,xh/g_xh,eh (partial derivatives at fixed sigma).
With U1 = W1 - beta x and W.grad eta = (beta - 2) eta (an identity of the chart), R = U1 Omega_x + (D + 1) Omega + a0 B0/A
becomes
  R = sigma^2 [ -(Dyh phi) om_xh - om_sigma + a0 s_e ghat ],
  N2 = sigma^2 [ |Dyh phi Dxh om| + |Dxh phi Dyh om| + |om_sigma + (Dyh phi ghat + Dxh phi/(s_e g_xh,eh)) om_eh| + |a0 s_e ghat| ],
  N_Omega = sigma [ |(beta xh - sigma Dyh phi) Dxh om| + |(beta s_e g_xh + sigma Dxh phi) Dyh om| + |om| + sigma |a0 s_e ghat| ].
The brackets involve derivatives of g of order at most four in (xh, eh) and two in sigma at the actual point. They are
bounded as sigma -> 0 on compact subsets of the open quadrant on which g_xh,eh has a positive lower bound, provided q = 1 or
q >= 2 (a generic sigma^q term in g makes om_sigma of order sigma^(q - 2) for 1 < q < 2); here q = 6(beta - 2), and for
beta = 3, M = 3 one has Eh = xh^2 + eh^6 + sigma^6, so sigma = 0 is allowed. On the axes every summand of both normalizers
vanishes and the axis values are limits. The forced subtractions (the O(r^2) terms of Psi, the leading orders of R and of
the grouped term) are carried out analytically; the brackets remain signed sums, and the residual bracket cancels to the
extent that the profile solves (P1). At
sigma = 0, R/N2 is the exact far limit C/N20. Points are placed on the solver's (t, S) square (Eh = 1, so t = sigma). Checks:
against the direct binary64 evaluation at r from 1e3 to 4e7 (differences 4e-11 to 8e-9; these differences alone
identify neither evaluator's error and give no uniform error bound), against the binary64 far-limit implementation at sigma = 0 (seven digits), and against the exact
values for the third source above: 1.102671e-5 at w = 7/16 (exact 1.1026715e-5), and 2.04285e-6 and 1.80048e-6 at
w = 1e-8 and 1 - 1e-8 (certified axis limits approximately 2.04307e-6 and 1.80051e-6). The scaling of G, the formula for Psi and the expressions for R, N2 and N_Omega were checked by an external audit with its
own 50-digit implementation of the direct chart route and of the scaled route (random coefficients, J = 3, K = 2, l = 1e2,
1e6, 1e12: agreement to 41 digits or better), and independently in multiple precision (raw derivatives in the original
coordinates, Cartesian finite differences, parity and guard tests); on the sampled points of that check the grouped ratio
of the evaluator used here differs from the multiple-precision value by at most 6.0e-11.

1.57e-7 < max |C|/N20 <= 3e-7 on the whole section, with certified grouped axis limits approximately 3.73e-8 (horizontal) and 5.17e-8 (vertical);
oddness of G in both variables rules out cubic terms, and its center expansion G = h*x*eta + O((abs(x)+abs(eta))^4), h > 0, gives y = h*eta + O((abs(x)+abs(eta))^3) and Psi = -2*x*y + O((abs(x)+abs(y))^4), with equivalent local orders because h > 0, hence c = -2 exactly. required by the centre and the two axis conditions (600.000047, 600.000136, 600.000182) have pairwise disjoint

The temperature residual vanishes identically in this representation (6.9, Formulation); the values in that column are
rounding. The elliptic relation also holds exactly: Omega = -Lap Psi and U = curl Psi are computed from the same stored
G, and U is the canonical (Biot-Savart) velocity of Omega by the proved chart theorem, so E = 0 analytically. In a
separate numerical comparison, the independent full-plane quadrature of the Biot-Savart integral of the stored
vorticity reproduces the centre strain c = -2 with absolute computed discrepancies about 1.1e-9, 3.4e-11 and 4.0e-12 at 32, 64 and 96 nodes (7.5e-12 and
6.8e-12 at 96 nodes with two other compactification scales), and the stored velocity at the target (41.3, 71.9) with maximum absolute component differences below 2.4e-13 at 96 nodes and 5.0e-13 at 128 nodes of the primary map. The difference increases between these two orders. With the regularized map at 96 nodes, the maximum absolute component difference per configuration ranges approximately from 2.9e-10 to 5.4e-10 across the three scales. Signed component differences are retained in the verification records. These are discrepancies from numerical references at sampled targets, not error bounds. Binary64 quadrature nodes, reference inversion and finite arithmetic limit their interpretation.
The refinement runs from this state used all three row sets and budgets of 100 iterations each: angular degree K = 96 (coefficients 2fe327c0, stopped after 18
iterations) and radial degree J = 96 (coefficients 147551db). The solver-grid maxima fell (1.55e-6 and 1.76e-6), and so did the dense prompt
ratio away from the axis for K = 96 (1.63e-6), and on the line x = 1e-8 next to the vertical axis a separate scan gives the following finite values: the
grouped ratio reaches 3.415e-6 and the prompt ratio 2.419e-6 at y = 1.081 for K = 96. An independent finite witness for the same state at 90 and
130 digits, at x = 4.1050776308483760852e-7 and y = 1.0814492283963557691, gives 3.41538e-6 and 2.41856e-6; this witness is one of the 95 raw references of that state's 10000-point sample and is counted once. For J = 96 the scan found 2.655e-6 and 1.808e-6 near y = 0.564. An independent 90/130-digit check at x = 1e-7, y = 0.564 gives 2.654762e-6 and 1.808425e-6 for J = 96. These checks are finite witnesses, not verification of the entire near-axis line. For the K = 96 state the independent verification also
confirmed the global chart, a nonzero centre defect (about -9.16e-6) with disjoint required amplitudes, and 9.9e-8 <
max |C|/N20 <= 7e-7 on the limiting section. In these two runs, increasing either degree without collocation in that band raised the largest value of the larger ratio found by the stated checks, as in the earlier angular ladder. This is an observation about these runs and samples, not a general refinement law. Rows next to the vertical axis were added afterwards (next paragraph).
